e_en: The correct answer is option D i.e. 1757. The Battle of Plassey Battle of Plassey laid the foundation of the British Empire in India. q_en: Shankar's International Dolls Museum is situated in ________
e_en: The correct answer is option D i.e. New Delhi. Shankar's International Dolls Museum The International Dolls Museum is a large collection of dolls. It is situated in New Delhi. Hence option D is correct. It was set up by K Shankar Pillai, a political cartoonist. The collections of dolls are classified into two parts.

e_en: The correct answer is the President of India.

e_en: The correct answer is Conduct local elections. Election Commission of India The Election Commission of India is an autonomous constitutional body responsible for administering Union and State election processes in India. Part XV of the constitution of India deals with elections and establishes a commission for these matters. Article 324 to 329 of the constitution of India deals with powers, function, tenure, eligibility, etc of the commission and the member.

Kathakali: Kathakali is a blend of dance, music and acting and dramatizes stories. It is one of the Indian recognized classical dance forms from the state of Kerala. Odissi Dance: It is a classical dance form of Odisha. It incorporates two major postures - Tribhanga and Chowk.

q_en: In India, states with ________ of population get more representatives.
e_en: The Correct Answer is Option D i.e Large size. In India, states with a larger size of population get more representatives. In India, Uttar Pradesh has the highest representation in Lok Sabha with 80 seats. q_en: The pen name of Sampooran Singh Kalra, an Indian poet, lyricist and film director is ________
e_en: The Correct Answer is Option C i.e Gulzar. Sampooran Singh Kalra: He is an Indian lyricist, poet, author, screenwriter, and film director. He is popularly known by his pen name Gulzar. He was awarded Padma Bhushan in 2004.

q_en: ________ is the harvest festival of Kerala.
e_en: The Correct Answer is Option D i.e Onam. Onam: It is a harvest festival of Kerala. It was celebrated to commemorate the arrival of King Mahabali. The festival lasts for ten days. It is celebrated every year in August-September. Pongal: Pongal is a four-day-long harvest festival celebrated mostly in the states of South India, especially in Tamil Nadu. The harvest festival is named after the Tamil word, Ponga, which means to boil.

q_en: ________ is the highest military decoration awarded for displaying distinguished acts of valour during war.
e_en: The Correct Answer is Option C i.e Param Vir Chakra. Param Vir Chakra: It is the highest military decoration awarded for displaying distinguished acts of valour during the war. It was introduced by the government on 26th January 1950. Major Somnath Sharma was the first recipient of the Param Vir Chakra (PVC).

q_en: Among the following options, ________ is the highest mountain peak of the Himalayas in India.
e_en: The correct answer is option D i.e Kanchenjunga. Kanchenjunga: It is the third highest mountain in the world with an elevation of 8586 m. It is situated on the border between Nepal and Sikkim. It is a part of the Great Himalayan Mountain Range. It is the highest mountain peak of the Himalayas in India. Namcha Barwa: It is located on the eastern side of the Great Canyon of Yarlung Tsangpo River. It is a mountain located in the Tibet region with an elevation of 7782 m.

q_en: Who was the only Pakistani national who was awarded the Bharat Ratna?
e_en: The correct answer is option A i.e Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan. Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan: He was also known as Frontier Gandhi and Badshah Khan. He founded the Khudai Khidmatgar movement in 1929. He was the only Pakistani national who was awarded the Bharat Ratna.

q_en: After Independence, ________ became India’s first Deputy Prime Minister.
e_en: The Correct Answer is Option A i.e Sardar Vallabhai Patel. Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel: He is popularly known as the Iron Man of India. The Statue of Unity is built in dedication to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. He was India’s first Deputy Prime Minister and first Home Minister. o_en: use of well-developed system of irrigation.
upgradation of the roads of the village.
use of advanced technology in farming.
e_en: The Correct Answer is Option B i.e upgradation of the roads of the village. Green Revolution is also known as the Agricultural Revolution. Green Revolution in India was founded by M S Swaminathan. The aim of the revolution was to increase agricultural productivity with the use of high yielding varieties of seeds, well-developed system of irrigation, technology and agricultural research. It did NOT include upgradation of the roads of the village.

q_en: Zamindari System was introduced by ________ in 1793.
e_en: The Correct Answer is Option C i.e Cornwallis. Zamindari System: The Zamindars were made owners of the land where they earlier have been revenue collectors. Since the settlement was made with the zamindars, it is known as the Zamindari Settlement. The demand for land revenue was fixed and out of controlled revenue (10/11) th part was given to the company. A Sunset clause was also added for zamindars by the company.

q_en: ________ river is the only natural water source that drains inside a lake in the desert.
e_en: The Correct Answer is Option D i.e Luni. River Ganga: The River Ganga originates from the Gangotri glacier in Uttarakhand. Alaknanda River joins Bhagirathi at Devprayag and from there the river is called Ganga. Yamuna (Largest right bank tributary of Ganga), Damodar (Sorrow of Bengal), Ghagra, Gomti, Gandak, Ramganga, Kosi (Sorrow of Bihar), Son, Mahananda are major tributaries of River Ganga.

q_en: The Bharatiya Janata Party's (BJP) origins lie in the Bharatiya Jana Sangh, founded by ________
e_en: The Correct Answer is Option A i.e Syama Prasad Mukherjee. Bharatiya Janata Party's (BJP): It was founded by Syama Prasad Mukherjee in 1951. Syama Prasad Mukherjee: He served as the Minister for Industry and Supply in Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru's cabinet. Recently in June 2020, Kolkata Port Trust was renamed to Shyama Prasad Mukerjee port trust. The Bharatiya Janata Party's (BJP) origins lie in the Bharatiya Jana Sangh, founded by Shyama Prasad Mukerjee.

q_en: ‘Deuce’ is a term associated with ________
e_en: The Correct Answer is lawn Tennis. Tennis originally was known as lawn tennis, and formally still is in Britain, because it was played on grass courts by Victorian gentlemen and ladies. It is now played on a variety of surfaces. The object of the game is to manoeuvre the ball in such a way that the opponent is not able to play a valid return. The deuce is a special score in tennis.

q_en: Which of the following is NOT a Trade Barrier?
e_en: The Correct Answer is Option C. A complete ban on imports from a certain country is called Embargo. Tariff Barriers are taxes on certain imports. Subsidies: It is a form of financial grant or aid given by the state to help an industry or business keep the price of a commodity or service at an affordable price. Export Security: It is a measure used by the government for the protection of producers or consumers of a particular. It is not a trade barrier.

q_en: ________ is the largest democracy of the world.
e_en: The Correct Answer is Option C i.e India. India: It shares a border with seven countries, namely China, Pakistan, Bhutan, Myanmar, Afghanistan, Nepal, and Bangladesh. India shares the longest border with Bangladesh. It is the largest democracy in the world, the representative with the most number of votes gets the power. New Delhi is the capital of India. Droupadi Murmu is the current President of India and Narendra Modi is the current PM of India.

q_en: The swampy belt of the northern Indian plains is known as ________
e_en: The Correct Answer is Terai. Bhabar: It is found in the foothills of Shivaliks. It comprises pebbles and rocks and is not suitable for agriculture. Due to the porosity of this belt, streams disappear in this belt. Terai: It lies next to the Bhabar region and is composed of newer alluvium. The underground streams reappear in this region. The swampy belt of the northern Indian plains is known as Terai.

q_en: The vast meadows in the high elevation ranges of the Himalayas are called ________
e_en: The Correct Answer is Option C i.e Bugyal. Bhabar: It is found in the foothills of Shivaliks. It comprises of pebbles and rocks and is not suitable for agriculture. Bugyal: They are alpine grasslands, or vast meadows, in higher elevation range between 3,300 metres and 4,000 metres of the Himalayas. Bugyal is also known as 'Nature's own gardens' in Uttarkhand.

q_en: Which of the following festivals is associated with the ‘Vaman’ incarnation of Vishnu?
e_en: The correct answer is option C i.e., Onam The festival of 'Onam' is associated with the 'Vamana' incarnation of the Lord Vishnu. Vamana, 5th of the 10 incarnations (avatars) of the Hindu god Vishnu. Onam is a festival celebrated in Kerala which is observed every year in the month of August-September. In the Rigveda, Vishnu took three strides, with which he measured out the three worlds - earth, heaven, and the space between them.

q_en: The Indian constitution declares India as:
e_en: The correct answer is option C i.e., a Union of States Article 1 of the Constitution states that India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States. The territory of India shall consist of: The territories of the states, the Union Territories, and any territory that may be acquired in the future. The names of the states and the Unions have been described in the First Schedule.

q_en: Which of the following is **NOT** a determinant of the patterns of drainage system?
e_en: The correct answer is option B i.e., Source of the drainage system The factors controlling or determining the drainage pattern in a region include the topography, slope, structural control, nature of rocks, tectonic activities, the geological history of that region, climatic conditions of the area, etc. The geometric arrangements of the streams in a region are known as a drainage pattern.

q_en: In the context of Sufi tradition, the term ‘khanqah’ stood for:
e_en: The correct answer is a hospice. A khanqah is a building designated especially for gatherings of Sufi brotherhood. In the past and to a lesser extent nowadays, they often served as hospices for Saliks (Sufi travelers), and Islamic students. Khanegah is also known as Khanqah or Khaniqah or Ribat. Khanegah's are very often found adjoined to dargahs (shrines of Sufi saints), and turbes (tombs of notables), mosques, and madrasas (Islamic schools).

q_en: Which of the following money transfer systems allows 24*7*365 transfer of money?
e_en: The correct answer is option A i.e., IMPS IMPS allows the transfer of money 24*7*365 days. The full form of IMPS is an Immediate Payment Service. IMPS is an instant payment inter-bank electronic funds transfer system

q_en: Which of the following is ***not*** an artificial ecosystem?

q_en: Which of the followings was NOT a Harappan city?
e_en: The correct answer is Mehrgarh Mehrgarh is a neolithic site located near the Bolan pass on the Kacchi Plain of Balochistan, Pakistan, to the west of the Indus River Valley. It is the earliest known neolithic site in the Northwest Indian sub-continent, with early evidence of farming (wheat and barley), herding (cattle, sheep, and goats), and metallurgy. The oldest known example of the wax-lost techniques comes from a 6000-year-old wheel-shaped copper amulet found at Mehrgarh.

q_en: Bhimbetka, a world heritage site, is known for:
e_en: The correct answer is option B i.e., prehistoric rock shelters Bhimbetka, a world heritage site, in the Raisen district of the state of Madhya Pradesh is known for its prehistoric rock shelters. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site that consists of seven hills and over 10 km. It was designated so in the year 2003. Most of the credit to discover the caves goes to Shri V.S. Vakankar.

q_en: What is ‘Bringa’ in Orissa?
o_en: A village known for diamond mines
A stone weapon used by the aboriginals
An edible oil used by the aboriginals
A local name of ‘slash and burn’ agriculture
e_en: The correct answer is option D i.e., A local name of 'slash and burn' agriculture Slash and burn agriculture is a farming method that involves the cutting and burning of plants in a woodland or forest to create a field called a swidden. It is also known as fire-fallow cultivation. The steps for slash and burn agriculture are : Prepare the field by cutting down vegetation, plants that provide food or timber that may be left standing.

q_en: Which of the following option is also termed as the third-tier of democracy in India?
e_en: The correct answer is Local-self government. The Indian Constitution was amended later with an additional level of governance along with the Central and the State governance by adding the Panchayats and Municipalities making it a three-tier government. This was done by the amendment to the Constitution in 1992. The 73rd Amendment of the Constitution has added a new part IX consisting of 16 Articles and the Eleventh Schedule to the Constitution.

q_en: Which of the following rulers built the mosque called ‘Adhai-din-ka-Jhopra’?
e_en: The correct answer is option D i.e., Qutub-ud-din Aibak Qutub-ud-din Aibak was the founder of the Slave dynasty in India, who ruled from 1206 to 1210. Qutub-ud-din Aibak was also known as Lakh Baksha Sultan because of his generosity. He laid the foundation of Qutub Minar which was later completed by Iltutmish. The Quwwat-al-Islam mosque was also commissioned by him. He built the famous 'Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra' mosque in the city of Ajmer, Rajasthan.

q_en: Which of the following constitutional amendments provided for the Right to Education?
e_en: The correct answer is the 86th amendment. The 86th amendment to the Constitution of India in 2002, provided the Right to Education as a Fundamental Right in Part-III of the Constitution. The amendment inserted Arti

q_en: Which of the following institutions is responsible for regulating the formal sources of credit in India?
e_en: The correct answer is RBI. The Reserve Bank of India is the body responsible for regulating the formal sources of credit in India. RBI started its operation on April 1, 1935. RBI was established via the RBI Act of 1934, so it is also known as a statutory body. The nationalization of RBI took place in 1949 and from January 1, 1949, RBI started working as a government-owned bank. The original headquarters of RBI were in Kolkata, but in 1937, it was shifted to Mumbai.

q_en: The Economic Survey of India is published by:
e_en: The correct answer is option B i.e., Department of Economic Affairs. The Economic Survey of India, the document that is brought out a day ahead of the General Budget, is the flagship annual report of the Finance Ministry. The survey is an assessment of the progress of the economy over the 12-month period. The Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance presents the survey in the Parliament every year, just before the Union Budget.

q_en: During British rule in India, ‘gomastha’ was:
o_en: a paid servant to supervise weavers, collect supplies, and examine the quality of cloth
an Indian soldier appointed as the in-charge of a cavalry
a village-level official in the revenue-department
an Indian officialin the intelligence department
e_en: The correct answer is option A i.e., a paid servant to supervise weavers, collect supplies, and examine the quality of cloth Gomasthas were the paid servants who were appointed by the East India Company to supervise weavers, collect supplies and examine the quality of clothes. The word 'gomastha' means agent in Persian. The gomasthas were Indian agents of the British East India Company, who signed bonds with the local weavers and artisans to deliver goods to the Company.

q_en: Which of the following rivers forms the famous Dhuandhar falls?
e_en: The correct answer is Narmada. The Dhuandhar Falls is a waterfall located in the Jabalpur district of Madhya Pradesh, formed by the river Narmada. The word Dhuandhar is derived from two Hindi words - Dhuan (smoke) + Dhar (flow) meaning a waterfall where we get smoke-flow-like feeling. The Dhuandhar Falls are located on the Narmada River in Bhedaghat and are 30 meters high. The Narmada river rises from the Amarkantak Plateau near Anuppur district Madhya Pradesh.

q_en: Magnus Carlsen is famous for which of the following sports?
e_en: The correct answer is Chess. Magnus Carlsen is a famous Chess player. He is a Norwegian chess grandmaster. He is the current world blitz champion. He is the current World Chess Champion. He is the current World Rapid Chess Champion. The highest-ranked player in FIDE world rankings. The youngest person ever to surpassed a rating of 2800 in FIDE world rankings. He became World Chess Champion in 2013 by defeating Viswanathan Anand.

q_en: Which of the following terms is NOT used in the banking field?
e_en: Option B is NOT correct. The term Zero hour is NOT used in the banking field. Zero Hour is a term used in Parliament. Zero Hour is the time when Members of Parliament can raise Issues regarding the urgent public importance. With prior notice to the Speaker, members can raise issues of importance during this time. It is not mentioned in the rules of procedure. Starts immediately after the question hours. It starts at around 12 noon.

q_en: From which country did the Indian Constitution borrow the idea of directive principles of state policy?
e_en: The correct answer is option D i.e Ireland. Indian Constitution borrowed the idea of directive principles of state policy from Ireland. The makers of the Constitution of India were influenced by the Irish Home Rule Movement and other national movements of Ireland. Part IV of the Indian constitution deals with the directive principles of state policy. Directive principles of state policy(DPSP) deal with economic and cultural rights.

q_en: The peninsular plateau of India is part of which of the following landmass?
e_en: The correct answer is option A i.e Gondwana land. Gondwana land was a supercontinent that existed before 550 million years ago. This supercontinent existed between the Neoproterozoic and the Jurassic Era. It was the largest piece of continental crust of the Paleozoic Era. The Gondwana land was named by Austr

q_en: The popular depiction named ‘Ravana Shaking Mount Kailash’ is depicted in which of the following caves?
e_en: The correct answer is Ellora. Ellora is a famous cave located in the Aurangabad district of Maharashtra, India. It is one of the UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India. Designated as the UNESCO World Heritage Sites in 1983. It is the largest single monolithic rock excavation in the world. The popular depiction named &a

q_en: Which of the following articles of the Indian Constitution provides powers to the president of India to declare National emergency?
e_en: The correct answer is option C i.e Article 352. The President of India is empowered to proclaim three types of emergencies to handle extraordinary situations in the country The three types of emergencies in India are namely: National Emergency. State Emergency. Financial Emergency. President can proclaim a National Emergency under Article 352 of the Indian Constitution. President can proclaim National Emergency only after receiving a written recommendation from the cabinet.

q_en: The Brihadeswara temple at Tanjore belongs to which of the religious sects?
e_en: The correct answer is Nayanars. Brihadishvara Temple is a Hindu temple at Tanjore, Tamil Nadu. It is dedicated to Lord Shiva. It is located on the banks of the Kaveri river.</strong

q_en: The National Sports Day is celebrated on which day in India?
e_en: The correct answer is option A i.e August 29. The National Sports Day is celebrating in India on August 29. August 29 is the birthday of hockey legend Dhyan Chand. The government of India designated August 29 as the National Sports Day since 2012 to commemorate his birth anniversary.&

q_en: The Sangai festival is celebrated in which of the following states of India?
e_en: The correct answer is option D i.e Manipur. The Sangai festival is celebrated in Manipur. Sangai festival is an annual cultural festival of Manipur. The Festival is organized by Manipur Tourism Department. It is celebrated every year from 21 to 30 November. The old name of the Sangai festival is Tourism Festival. The festival has been renamed the Sangai festival from 2010 onwards.

q_en: “The Long walk to Freedom”is the autobiography of:
e_en: The correct answer is option A i.e Nelson Mandela. Nelson Mandela was a South African political leader. He is well known as the father of the nation of South Africa. He is well known for the Anti-Apartheid Movement in South Africa. He served as the first President of South Africa from 1994 to 1999. India awarded him the Bharat Ratna in 1990. Pakistan awarded him Nishan-e-Pakistan in 1992. Honored with the Nobel Peace Prize in 1993. Notable works: Long Walk to Freedom.

q_en: Who is the Ex-Officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha?
e_en: The correct answer is Vice President of India. The Vice President of India is the second-highest position in India. Article 63 of the Indian Constitution states that there shall be a Vice President of India. The Vice President is elected by an Electoral College of India. The term of Vice President is 5 years. The powers and functions of the Vice President of India are similar to that of the Vice President of America.

q_en: Which of the rivers given below is also referred to as “Dakshin Ganga’?
e_en: The correct answer is Godavari. The Godavari is the largest peninsular river in India. Origin: Brahmagiri hills, Tryambakeshwar, Maharashtra. Mouth: Bay of Bengal. It flows through the Indian states of Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh. The Godavari is also referred to as “Dakshin Ganga’. The second-longest river in India. Important Dams: Sriram Sagar Dam, Jayakwadi dam, Ghatghar Dam. Important right bank tributaries: Manjira. Darna. Pravara. Sindphana.

q_en: Who of the following gave the statement "Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it"?
e_en: The correct answer is Bal Gangadhar Tilak. Bal Gangadhar Tilak was an independence activist. Popularly known as 'Uncrowned King of India'. He was deported to Mandalay in Myanmar(old Burma) for six years in 1908. As a politician, he is well known as "the father of Indian unrest" He gave the statement "Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it". Notable works: Kesari, Gita Rahasya, and Mahratta.

q_en: The ancient name of Coastal Orissa was:
e_en: The correct answer is option A i.e Kalinga. Odisha is an Indian state located in eastern India. Capital: Bhubaneswar. The ancient name of coastal Orissa was Kalinga. The Kalinga was invaded by the Mauryan emperor Ashoka in 261 BCE in the Kalinga War. Orissa and Utkalam are also the old names of Odisha. Odisha has a 485 Kilometres long coastline. The coastline known as the gift of six rivers is situated in Odisha. The famous Konark temple is located in Odisha.

q_en: The novel “The God of Small Things” is inspired by which country?
e_en: The correct answer is option B i.e India. The God of Small Things was the first novel written by famous Indian writer Arundhati Roy. The story was based on the childhood experiences of fraternal twins. The novel “The God of Small Things” won the Booker Prize in 1997. The story is inspired from Ayemenem, Kottayam district in Kerala, India. Important characters in “The God of Small Things”: Estha, Rahel, Ammu, Velutha, Chacko.

q_en: Which of the following statements describes “endemic species”?
o_en: Species with less population may move to the category of endangered species.
Species that are not found existing after intense searches.
Species that are found only in some particular areas.
Species that have come from abroad.
e_en: The correct answer is option C i.e Species that are found only in some particular areas. Species that are found only in some particular areas are called endemic species. Endemic species can easily become extinct or endangered from the earth. The dodo is an extinct flightless bird that was endemic to the island of Mauritius, in the Indian ocean. Dodo is an example of the vulnerability of endemic species to habitat alteration.

q_en: Which of the following days is observed as the “Human Rights Day’’?
e_en: The correct answer is option C i.e December 10. Human Rights Day is observed annually across the world on 10th December. December 10 was chosen to honor the adoption and proclamation of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights. <li&g

q_en: Ashoka appointed religious officials, known as:
e_en: The correct answer is Dhamma-mahamatta. Dhamma-mahamatta was a group of officers instituted to implement and publicize the various aspects of Dhamma. Ashoka made them responsible for carrying his message to various sections of society. Later they became very powerful and started interfering with state politics.

q_en: Bank rate is decided by which of the following agencies?
o_en: Securities and Exchange Board of India
e_en: The correct answer is Reserve Bank of India. Bank Rate refers to the official interest rate at which RBI will provide loans to the banking system. Bank rate is used as a signal by the RBi to the commercial banks on RBI's thinking about what the interest rate should be.

q_en: In which year was the Earth summit of Rio de Janeiro held?
e_en: The correct answer is option C, i.e. 1992. The Earth Summit 1992 is also known as The United Nations Conference on Environment and Development (UNCED) held at Rio de Janeiro (Brazil).

q_en: Pandit Bhimsen Joshi is associated with which tradition of classical music?
e_en: The correct answer is Hindustani. Pandit Bhimsen Joshi also known as Pandit Bhimsen Gururaj Joshi (February 4, 1922 - January 24, 2011) He was the Hindustani classical vocalist. Member of Kirana Gharana. Known for Khayal form of singing. Award - Awarded Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship in 1998. Bestowed with Bharat Ratna in 2008. ​Hindustani classical music: It is the art music of northern regions of the Indian subcontinent.

q_en: Which of the following languages is NOT a part of the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution?
e_en: The correct answer is option C, i.e. Persian. The list of official languages recognized by the Constitution is mentioned under schedule Eight of the Indian Constitution. The Eighth Schedule to the Indian Constitution contains a list of 22 scheduled languages. Language Spoken in Indian State of Year of Recognition Amendment Act Assamese Assam 1950 Incorporated with the enactment of the Indian Constitution.

q_en: Which of the following is NOT in the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court of India?
e_en: The correct answer is option D. i.e. Financial. The Supreme Court of India has Original, Appellate, writ and Advisory jurisdiction. Original Jurisdiction: As per Article 32 Supreme Court is the guardian/protector of fundamental right and any person whose fundamental rights are violated can directly approach the Supreme Court for a remedy and any matter regarding the enforcement of fundamental rights comes under the original jurisdiction of the supreme court.

q_en: The percolation rate of water is the least in ........... soil.
e_en: The correct answer is option A i.e. Clay. Clay soils have very fine particles through which water cannot easily percolate. What is percolation - When we sprinkle water on the ground, it is soon absorbed by the soil. The process in which water passes down slowly through the soil is called the percolation of water. Percolation varies with soil type while sandy soli allows maximum percolation, clay soil allows minimum percolation of water.

q_en: The Jnanpith Award is given for excellence in which of the following fields?
e_en: The correct answer is option C, i.e. Literature. Jnanpith Award is a literary award presented by the Bhartiya Jnanpith organization to Indian writers every year. The first Jnanpith award was given to G.Sankara Kurup (Malayalam) in 1965 for his novel "Odakkuzhal" (The Bamboo Flute). The winner is given a cash prize of Rs.11 lakh and a bronze replica of Goddess Saraswati, the Hindu goddess of learning.

q_en: Which one of the following countries is NOT a member of the BRICS grouping?
e_en: The correct answer is option D, i.e. Kenya. The BRICS group was formed as the result of an agreement signed by the four countries on November 28, 2009. BRICS is an intergovernmental organization comprising Brazil, Russia, India, China, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, and the United Arab Emirates. The four nations committed to work jointly at the Copenhagen climate summit.

q_en: The 86th Constitution Amendment Act, 2002 inserted which of the following articles in the Constitution of India?
e_en: The correct answer is 21-A. The 86th amendment to the constitution of India in 2002 provided Right to Education as a Fundamental right in part -III of the constitution. The Tropic of Cancer passes through eight states in India: Gujarat (Jasdan), Rajasthan (Kalinjarh), Madhya Pradesh (Shajapur), Chhattisgarh (Sonhat), Jharkhand (Lohardaga), West Bengal (Krishnanagar), Tripura (Udaipur), and Mizoram (Champhai). The Tropic of Cancer is a parallel of latitude on the Earth, 23.5 degrees north of the equator.

q_en: During the reign of which of the following Mauryan kings, the Kalinga War was fought?
e_en: The correct answer is Ashoka. Ashoka Ashoka also is known as "Devanampiya". Piyadasi was the son of Mauryan Emperor Bindusara and was born in 304 BC. His reign lasted from 268 BC to 232 BC. Once he became King, he started expanding his empires by conquest, in the ninth year of his reign he waged a war with Kalinga (present-day Odisha). Ashoka's 13th Rock edicts describe the Kalinga war.

q_en: When was the first complete Census conducted in India?
e_en: The correct answer is 1881. A census is an official systematic survey of the population of a country. Census is a process of collecting, compiling, analyzing, evaluating, publishing and disseminating statistical data regarding the population of a country. It covers demographic, social and economic data. The first complete Census was taken in India in 1881 under British Viceroy Ripon. Lord Mayo was the Viceroy of India from 1869 to 1872.

Only the elected members of both Houses of Parliament
Only the members' of Council of States
The Elected Members of both Houses of Parliament and State Legislative Assemblies.

The President of India is elected by the electoral college which consists of Elected members of both the houses of parliament.

q_en: Which of the following is the thanksgiving festival of Maharashtra, where bulls are honoured as they are considered indispensable to farming?
e_en: The correct answer is Pola Festival. Pola Festival Pola Festival is a thanksgiving festival celebrated by farmers in Maharashtra and Chhattisgarh, to acknowledge the importance of bulls and oxen, who are a crucial part of agriculture and farming activities. It falls on the day of the Pithori Amavasya in the month of Shraavana.

e_en: The correct answer is 395. Indian Constitution was adopted by the Constituent Assembly of India on 26 November 1949 and became effective on 26 January 1950. Dr. BR Ambedkar is known as the father of the Indian Constitution.

Article 21: This Article guards an individual's right to life and personal liberty. Fundamental rights during National Emergency: Articles 358 and 359 describe the effect of a National Emergency on Fundamental Rights.

q_en: In which among the following states, Arabica coffee grown in India?
e_en: The correct answer is Karnataka. Karnataka is the largest coffee-producing state in India. After Karnataka, the next state which accounts for the highest share of coffee production in India is Kerala. Kerala produces around 21% of India’s coffee. Both Karnataka and Kerala together account for around 90% of the total coffee produced in India. The third highest coffee-producing state in India is Tamil Nadu which accounts for 5% of the total coffee produced in India.

q_en: Powers, authority and responsibilities of Municipalities are dealt under which schedule?
e_en: The correct answer is 12th The eleventh Schedule in the Indian Constitution specifies the powers, authority, and responsibilities of Panchayats. 11th Schedule deals with the Power, authority, and responsibilities of Panchayats, 29 subjects over which the Panchayats have jurisdiction. 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992: The institution of Panchayati Raj received a Constitutional guarantee, status, and legitimacy. The XI Schedule was added to deal with it.

q_en: How many types of Bihu festival are celebrated in Assam?
e_en: The correct answer is 3. Bihu is a set of three important Assamese festivals in Assam – 'Rongali' or 'Bohag Bihu' observed in April, 'Kongali' or 'Kati Bihu' observed in October, and 'Bhogali' or 'Magh Bihu' observed in January. The Rongali Bihu is the most important of the three, celebrating the spring festival. The Bhogali Bihu or the Magh Bihu is a harvest festival, with community feasts.

q_en: The concepts of Dhamma was popularized by which of the following Mauryan kings?
e_en: The correct answer is Ashoka. Ashoka was the great Mauryan ruler and grandson of the dynasty's founder Chandragupta Maurya. Ashoka became a Buddhist in the 9th year of his reign i.e., a year after the conquest of Kalinga. Dhamma is the Prakrit form of the Sanskrit word 'Dharma'. Ashoka’s dhamma was neither a new religion nor a new political philosophy, it was a way of life. Ashoka denounced all useless ceremonies and sacrifices held under the influence of superstition.

q_en: The Dronacharya Sports Award is given to the ________.
e_en: The correct answer is Coach of the Team. The Dronacharya Award is given by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, Government of India, for excellence in sports coaching. The award is known after Drona, often referred to as "Dronacharya" or "Guru Drona", a personality from the Sanskrit epic Mahabharata of ancient India. The Dronacharya Award contains a medallion, a certificate, and a money prize of Rs 15 lakh(lifetime) and 10 Lakh (regular).

q_en: Planning Commission was established under ________ on March 15, 1950
e_en: The correct answer is Jawahar Lal Nehru. Planning Commission in India: The Planning Commission was reporting directly to the Prime Minister of India. It was established on 15 March 1950, with Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru as the chairman. The Planning Commission did not derive its creation from either the Constitution or statute but was an arm of the Central/Union Government. The Planning Commission was set up by a Resolution of the Government of India in March 1950.

q_en: Availability of _______ during winter months due to the western temperate cyclones helps in the success of rabi crops.
e_en: The correct answer is precipitation. Rabi crops are sown in winter and harvested in spring. They include crops like wheat, barley, and mustard. Western temperate cyclones bring moisture and precipitation to the northern parts of India during winter months, which is essential for the growth of rabi crops. Frost can be detrimental to crops as it can damage or kill them. Fog, option C, can reduce visibility and sunlight, which can also be harmful to crops.

q_en: On September 1948 the Indian army intervened and took control of which princely state?
e_en: The correct answer is Hyderabad. The Indian army intervened and took control of the princely state of Hyderabad in September 1948. Hyderabad was the largest and the most prosperous princely state in India, ruled by the Nizam of Hyderabad. The Nizam initially refused to accede to either India or Pakistan after India gained independence in 1947, leading to a stand-off with the Indian government.

q_en: Which Indian organisation is responsible for collecting data on poverty in the country?
o_en: Office of Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India
e_en: The correct answer is the National Sample Survey Organisation. The national sample survey Organization [NSSO] conducts a SURVEY every 5 years to estimate poverty in India. It is the organization under the ministry of Statistics of the government of India. The National Sample Survey Organization (NSSO) carries out socioeconomic surveys, undertakes field of work for the Annual Survey of Industries, and follow-up surveys of the economic census.

q_en: The council of ministers is collectively responsible to the ________.
e_en: The correct answer is Lok Sabha. According to Article 75 clause 3, the Council of Ministers shall be collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha(House of the People). Council of Ministers: The Prime Minister and other Ministers are collectively known as the Council of Ministers. Three categories of Ministers viz Cabinet Ministers, Minister of State and Deputy Ministers. All of them are appointed by the President of India.

q_en: The classical text, Hasthalakshana Deepika, is associated with which Indian classical dance form?
e_en: The correct answer is Kathakali. Hasthalakshana Deepika is a text that is associated with the Indian classical dance form of Kathakali. It is a manual that provides a detailed description of the mudras or hand gestures used in Kathakali, along with their meanings and usage. The text is believed to have been written by a scholar named Karthikeya Muni, who was a disciple of the famous Kathakali exponent, Kaplingad Narayanan Namboodiri.

q_en: Government goods and services that aren't sold directly to the consumers, for example defence goods, roads are categorised under:
e_en: The correct answer is public goods. Public Good: Public goods are goods that are commonly available to all people within a society or community and that possess two specific qualities: they are non-excludable and non-rivalrous. Everyone has access to use them, and their use does not deplete their availability for future use. A commodity whose benefits are indivisibly spread among the entire community.

q_en: What is an area of dry land that lies on the leeward side of a mountain called?
e_en: The correct answer is the Rainshadow area. A rainshadow area is a region of dry land that lies on the leeward side of a mountain. When moist air from the ocean or a large water body rises up a mountain range, it cools and condenses to form clouds and precipitation. This process is known as orographic precipitation. As the air moves over the mountain and descends on the other side, it warms up and dries out, leading to a rainshadow area.

q_en: The national level cricket championship, Ranji Trophy, began in ________.
e_en: The correct answer is 1934-1935. About Ranji Trophy: The Ranji Trophy is a Domestic Class National level Cricket tournament. This is one of the oldest cricket tournaments in India which was started in 1934. In this tournament many of the multiple teams representing the Regional and State cricket associations.

q_en: Select the second step of decomposition.
e_en: The correct answer is leaching. Decomposition is the process of breaking down complex organic matter into simpler substances. The first step of decomposition is fragmentation, which involves the physical breakdown of the organic matter into smaller pieces. Leaching is the process of removal of soluble nutrients from the decomposing organic matter by water or other liquids.

q_en: Any person in-charge of or employed in a child care institution, who subjects a child to corporal punishment shall be liable under ________.
e_en: The correct answer is the Juvenile Justice Act. Juvenile Justice Act: This act was enacted in 2000 to provide a comprehensive framework for the care, protection, and rehabilitation of children in need of care and protection. The act defines corporal punishment as any punishment in which physical force is used and intended to cause some degree of pain or discomfort, however light.

q_en: Which of the following is a secondary sector activity?
e_en: The correct answer is Manufacturing. Secondary sector activities involve the processing of raw materials extracted from the primary sector into finished goods. Manufacturing is a classic example of a secondary sector activity. Mining, quarrying, and forestry are primary sector activities that involve the extraction of natural resources directly from the earth. These activities are important for providing the raw materials necessary for secondary sector activities.

q_en: What are Kho-Kho players sitting in the squares called?
e_en: The correct answer is Chasers. The Kho-Kho players sitting in the squares are called Chasers. Chasers are responsible for chasing and tagging the runners to get them out. Runners are the players who run around the field trying to avoid being tagged by the chasers. Active Chasers are the players who are currently chasing the runners. The game of KHO KHO is one of the oldest traditional tag games in India. It is a team game.

q_en: Which two categories of age group are considered in Khelo India Youth Games?
e_en: The correct answer is Under 17 and Under 21. Khelo India Youth Games considers two categories of age groups: Under 17 and Under 21. The games are organized by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports in India. The main objective of the games is to promote sports and fitness among youth in India. The games also provide a platform for young athletes to showcase their talent and compete at the national level. The Khelo India Youth Games will be held at eight locations.

q_en: Kelucharan Mohapatra was related to which classical dance form?
e_en: The correct answer is Odissi. Kelucharan Mohapatra was a legendary Indian classical dancer, guru, and exponent of Odissi dance, who is credited with the revival and popularizing of this classical dance form in the 20th century. He is the first person to receive the Padma Vibhushan from Odisha. He was born on 8 January 1926 and died on 7 April 2004, in Bhubaneswar.

q_en: The council of ministers in a state are appointed on the advice of the ___________.
e_en: The correct answer is the Chief minister. The council of ministers in a state is appointed on the advice of the Chief Minister. The Council of Ministers performs the following functions: Formulation of Policies: The Ministers formulate the policies of the government.

q_en: GNP stands for ___________.
e_en: The correct answer is a gross national product. ​GNP - Gross National Product. It is the total value of all the final products and services in a given period in terms of production by a country's residents.

q_en: Who among the following is related with Mohiniyattam?

q_en: How is the vegetation affected by construction of large dams?
o_en: The plants produce nodules to produce nitrogen-fixing bacteria.
Vegetation gives rise to oxygen under aerobic conditions.
The growth of fungus is a lot
The submerged vegetation rots under anaerobic conditions and gives rise to large amounts of methane, which is also a greenhouse gas
e_en: The correct answer is The submerged vegetation rots under anaerobic conditions and gives rise to large amounts of methane, which is also a greenhouse gas. The construction of large dams leads to the flooding of vast areas, which results in the submergence of vegetation and the subsequent rotting of submerged plants under anaerobic conditions. This rotting vegetation gives rise to large amounts of methane, which is a potent greenhouse gas that contributes to global warming.

q_en: Which project is built for hydel power production and irrigation in the Sutlej river basin?
e_en: The correct answer is the Bhakra Nangal project. Bhakra Nangal project is a multipurpose project built on the Sutlej River in the northern Indian states of Punjab and Himachal Pradesh. The project was built for hydel power production and irrigation purposes. The project is one of the largest and most successful hydroelectric power projects in India. The project has a total installed capacity of 1,325 MW and can irrigate over 10 million acres of land in the region.

q_en: The Non-Cooperation-Khilafat Movement began in January ______
e_en: The correct answer is 1921. The Non-Cooperation-Khilafat Movement began in January 1921. It was a joint movement by the Indian National Congress and the All India Khilafat Committee to protest against the British Government's actions towards the Khilafat issue and to demand Swaraj or self-rule for India. The movement gained widespread support and saw mass participation from all sections of society, including peasants, workers, students, and women.

q_en: When governments legally obliged food producers to add extra nutrients to particular foods or categories of foods it is called ___________ .
e_en: The correct answer is food fortification. Food fortification is the process of adding extra nutrients to particular foods or categories of foods to improve their nutritional value. This is often done by governments to address nutrient deficiencies in the population, such as adding iodine to salt to prevent iodine deficiency disorders. Food protection refers to measures taken to prevent food contamination or spoilage, such as proper storage and handling practices.

q_en: Which among the following festivals is also celebrated to remember King Mahabali in Kerala?
e_en: The correct answer is Onam. Onam is a harvest festival celebrated in the Indian state of Kerala to remember King Mahabali, who is believed to have ruled Kerala in ancient times. It is celebrated in the Malayalam month of Chingam, which usually falls in August or September. The festival is marked by various rituals and cultural activities, including the famous snake boat race, called Vallamkali. Onam is an annual Malayali harvest festival celebrated in the state of Kerala.

q_en: Fundamental Rights was borrowed from the Constitution of .
e_en: The correct answer is the United States of America The idea of passing the Fundamental Rights in the Constitution of India was inspired by the Constitution of the United States of America. Fundamental Rights: The Fundamental Rights have been described in Articles 12-35, Part III of the Indian Constitution. The Right to Property (Article 31) was deleted from the list of Fundamental Rights by the 44th Amendment Act (1978).

q_en: The main items of ________ expenditure are interest payments, defence services, subsidies.
e_en: The correct answer is non-plan. The main items of non-plan expenditure are interest payments, defence services, subsidies. Non-plan expenditure refers to the regular expenses incurred by the government, which are not related to any specific plan or project. Interest payments include the interest paid on loans taken by the government, such as external debt and domestic debt.

q_en: Which classical dance generally narrates the story of the feminine form of Vishnu?
e_en: The correct answer is Mohiniattam. Mohiniattam is a classical dance form that originated in the state of Kerala, India. It is a dance form that is mainly performed by women and is known for its graceful movements and expressions. The dance form generally narrates the story of the feminine form of Vishnu, which is Mohini. Mohini is believed to be the female avatar of Lord Vishnu, who is often depicted as a beautiful woman with enchanting powers.

q_en: India has a parliamentary form of government which is a feature borrowed from the ________ Constitution.
e_en: The correct answer is Britain. India's parliamentary form of government is heavily influenced by the British parliamentary system, which was introduced during the colonial period. The Indian Constitution lays down the framework for the parliamentary system, which is based on the Westminster model of the British Parliament.

q_en: Savitribai, together with her husband Jyotirao Phule, founded one of India's first girls' schools in Pune, at Bhide Wada in _________.
e_en: The correct answer is 1848. Savitribai and her husband Jyotirao Phule were social reformers who worked towards the upliftment of women and lower-caste communities in India. They founded one of India's first girls' schools in Pune, Maharashtra, which was established in 1848 at Bhide Wada. The school aimed to provide education to girls who were otherwise denied access to learning opportunities due to social and cultural barriers.

q_en: Except for the deep sea hydrothermal ecosystem, sun is the only source of energy for all ecosystems on Earth. What comes next in the energy food chain?
e_en: The correct answer is Plants. The energy food chain starts with the sun, which is the primary source of energy for all ecosystems on Earth. Plants, being the primary producers, are the next in the energy food chain. They use the sun's energy to produce food through photosynthesis. Herbivores come next in the chain, as they consume plants for their energy requirements. Carnivores come after herbivores, as they consume other animals for their energy requirements.

q_en: In India, in the sphere of law making, a Bill does not become an Act unless it receives the assent of the ________.
e_en: The correct answer is President. In India, a Bill passed by both the Houses of Parliament becomes an Act only after the President gives his assent to it. The Bill does not become law if the Governor or the President, as the case may be, withholds his assent. The President is the head of the Indian state and exercises his powers and functions through various constitutional offices and authorities, including the power to give assent to Bills passed by Parliament.

q_en: In _______, Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi at Panipat.
e_en: The correct answer is 1526. Babur was a Mongol prince who founded the Mughal Empire in India in 1526 after defeating Ibrahim Lodi, the Sultan of Delhi, at the battle of Panipat. The battle of Panipat was a significant event in Indian history as it marked the beginning of the Mughal Empire, which lasted for more than 300 years and left a lasting impact on Indian culture, art, and architecture.

q_en: An Act to protect children from offences of sexual assault, sexual harassment and pornography and provide for establishment of Special Courts, referred as _________ (POCSO).
o_en: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2013
Prevention of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
Protection of Child from Sexual Ordeal Act, 2012
e_en: The correct answer is Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. The POCSO Act was enacted in 2012 by the Parliament of India to protect children from sexual offences and provide a safe and secure environment for them. The act defines various sexual offences against children, such as sexual assault, sexual harassment, and pornography, and prescribes stringent punishments for the offenders.

q_en: Which of the following scientists is known as the father of the Green revolution in India?
e_en: The correct answer is M.S. Swaminathan. M.S. Swaminathan is known as the father of the Green Revolution in India. M.S. Swaminathan is an Indian geneticist and agricultural scientist who played a crucial role in the development of high-yielding varieties of wheat, rice, and other crops in India. He led the Indian team that successfully implemented the Green Revolution in the 1960s, which helped India achieve self-sufficiency in food production and averted a potential famine.

q_en: Indian athlete Somdev Devvarman is associated with, which of the following sports?
e_en: The correct answer is Lawn Tennis. Indian athlete Somdev Devvarman is associated with Lawn Tennis. Being the only collegiate player to have advanced to three consecutive NCAA finals—having won back-to-back championships at the University of Virginia in his junior and senior years—he garnered headlines. Since 1950, only three other players have been able to match that record.

q_en: Holi is the festival of colours, celebrated in the Hindu month of _______.
e_en: The correct answer is Phalgun. Holi is a Hindu festival that is celebrated in the month of Phalgun, which usually falls in February or March. It is also known as the festival of colors as people play with colored powders and water. The festival celebrates the victory of good over evil and the arrival of spring. It is a time for forgiveness, unity, and spreading joy and happiness.

q_en: Which place's distribution of pressure influences the weather conditions over India in winter?
e_en: The correct answer is Central and Western Asia. Central and Western Asia is known for the formation of a high-pressure area during winters, which causes cold and dry winds to blow towards India. These winds are known as the northwestern winds or the 'winter monsoon,' and they bring in cold and dry air, resulting in a decrease in temperature over the Indian subcontinent.

q_en: Sadanam P.V Balakrishnan won the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in which dance form?

q_en: Who among the following was the first Indian to be recruited in Indian Civil Service in British India?

q_en: Maha Shivratri is celebrated in the honour of the Hindu deity, Lord Shiva in the Hindu month of ________.

q_en: The plan between fifth five year plan and sixth five year plan is known as ______.

e_en: The correct answer is Article 324 Article 324 : ​Article 324 in the Indian Constitution gives power to the Election Commission to direct, control, and conduct elections to all Parliament, to the Legislature of every state, and of elections to the offices of the President and Vice President held under the Constitution.

q_en: Which of the following duties was NOT added by the 42nd amendment to the Indian Constitution?
o_en: To provide opportunities for education to one’s child or ward between the ages of six and fourteen years
To value and preserve the rich heritage of the country’s composite culture
To safeguard public property and to abjure violence
To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India
e_en: The correct answer is To provide opportunities for education to one’s child or ward between the ages of six and fourteen years. The 42nd Amendment of the Constitution of India: The 42nd Amendment of the Constitution of India was enacted in the year 1976. It is officially known as the Constitution Act, of 1976. It was enacted during the Emergency by the Indian National Congress Head Indira Gandhi.

q_en: The first complete census of an Indian city was conducted in 1830 by ________.
e_en: The correct answer is Henry Walter. The first complete census of an Indian city conducted in 1830 hasn't been definitively attributed to a particular individual or organization. A census is an official systematic survey of the population of a country. Census is a process of collecting, compiling, analyzing, evaluating, publishing and disseminating statistical data regarding the population of a country. It covers demographic, social and economic data.

q_en: While computing the national income, _______ is taken as a factor.
e_en: The correct answer is Export. Export:- Export is indeed an important factor that is taken into account when computing the national income of a country. When calculating the national income, the value of exports is included as it represents the income generated from selling goods and services produced domestically to other countries. Export earnings contribute to the overall economic activity and income of a nation.

q_en: National development council (NDC) was set up in ________ in India.
e_en: The correct answer is 1952. National Development Council was formed on 6 August 1952 in India. The Prime Minister of India used to be its ex-officio chairman. National Development Council (NDC) or the Rashtriya Vikas Parishad is the apex body for decision making and deliberations on development matters in India presided over by the Prime Minister.

q_en: Which among the following festival marks the menstruation period of the Goddess Kamakhya in Assam?
e_en: The correct answer is Ambubachi Mela. The Ambubachi Mela:- It is also known as Ambubasi festival or Ameti festival, is an annual religious festival celebrated in the Kamakhya Temple in Guwahati, Assam, India. It is one of the most important festivals in the state of Assam and attracts thousands of devotees from various parts of the country. The festival is centered around the Kamakhya Devi Temple, which is dedicated to the Hindu goddess Kamakhya.

q_en: The _______ industry covers a wide range of products from transistor sets to television.
e_en: The correct answer is electronics. The electronics industry:- It encompasses the manufacturing, design, and sale of electronic components and devices. It includes a broad range of products such as consumer electronics (e.g., televisions, smartphones, laptops, and home appliances), electronic components (e.g., semiconductors, integrated circuits, and resistors), communication devices, medical equipment, automotive electronics, and much more.

q_en: A _______ is a barrier across flowing water that obstructs, directs or retards the flow, often creating a reservoir, lake or impoundment.
e_en: The correct answer is dam. Dam:- A dam is a structure built across a river or stream to hold back water. Manmade dams create artificial lakes called reservoirs. Reservoirs can be used to store water for farming, industry, and household use.

q_en: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India deals with the state executive?
e_en: The correct answer is Articles 153-167. The Articles of the Constitution of India that deal with the State executive are primarily Articles 153 to 167. These articles outline the structure, powers, and functions of the state executive, including the Governor, Council of Ministers, Chief Minister, and other related provisions. Articles 153-167 of the Indian Constitution, which pertain to the state executive, are mentioned in Part VI - The States of the Indian Constitution.​

q_en: Swami Dayanand Saraswati founded the _______, an organisation that attempted to reform Hinduism.
e_en: The correct answer is Arya Samaj. Swami Dayanand Saraswati:-​ Dayananda Saraswati [1824-1883] was the first to give the call for Swarajya – "India for Indians" – in 1876. For his own inspiration, Swami Dayanand went to the Vedas which he regarded as infallible. He rejected all later religious thought if it conflicted with the Vedas. This total dependence on Vedas and their infallibility gave his teachings orthodox coloring.

q_en: The 'Method of Election of the president' in the Indian Constitution has been borrowed from the ______ constitution.
e_en: The correct answer is Irish. The 'Method of Election of the President' in the Indian Constitution has been borrowed from the Constitution of Ireland. Article 55 outlines the manner in which the President is to be elected, the composition of the electoral college, and the value of votes of the members of the electoral college.

q_en: Mohiniyattam is a solo classical dance form related to which of the following states?
e_en: The correct answer is Kerala. Mohiniyattam is a solo classical dance form of Kerala state. Mohiniyattam is one of India's famous classical dances, developed and still popular in the state of Kerala. This dance form derives its name from Mohini, the historical enchanting embodiment of the Hindu god Vishnu, who helps good to prevail over evil by nurturing its feminine energies.

q_en: As per RBI, in India, services sector accounted for _______ on the GDP in the 1980s.
e_en: The correct answer is 38.6 percent Gross domestic product (GDP):-​ Gross domestic product (GDP) is the monetary value of all finished goods and services made within a country during a specific period. GDP provides an economic snapshot of a country, used to estimate the size of an economy and its growth rate. GDP can be calculated in three ways, using expenditures, production, or incomes. It can be adjusted for inflation and population to provide deeper insights.

q_en: Makar Sankranti is celebrated as Pedda Panduga in which of the following states?
e_en: The correct answer is Andhra Pradesh. Pedda Panduga is a major festival celebrated in Andhra Pradesh, particularly in rural areas. It marks the transition of the sun into the zodiac sign of Capricorn (Makara Rasi) and the beginning of longer days. People fly kites, organize cultural events, and participate in traditional sports like bullock cart races and cockfights.</str

q_en: Pick the odd one out (Hint: fiber crops).
e_en: The correct answer is rubber. Rubber is not a fiber crop. It is primarily cultivated for latex production, which is used in various industries, especially in the production of rubber-based products. In contrast, cotton, hemp, and jute are fiber crops that are specifically grown for their fibrous properties, which are used to make textiles, ropes, and other related products.​

q_en: 'Mother of Mohiniyattam' is a docu-fiction based on ______.
e_en: The correct answer is Kalamandalam Kallyanikutty Amma. "Mother of Mohiniyattam" is a docu-fiction based on the life and contributions of Kalamandalam Kallyanikutty Amma. Kalamandalam Kallyanikutty Amma was a prominent figure in Mohiniyattam, a classical dance form of Kerala. She is recognized as a key contributor to the revival and popularization of Mohiniyattam in the 20th century.

q_en: Traditionally, the Budget documents classified total expenditure into ________.
e_en: The correct answer is plan and non-plan expenditure. Budget documents classify total expenditures into plan and non-plan expenditures. Plan expenditures refer to the funds allocated for specific programs, schemes, and projects outlined in the budgetary plan. Non-plan expenditures, on the other hand, encompass general expenses such as salaries, pensions, debt servicing, and maintenance costs.

q_en: Which of the following was the main demand of the peasant movement of Kheda?
o_en: Free irrigation facility to be provided
e_en: The correct answer is Revenue collection be relaxed. The main demand of the peasant movement of Kheda was revenue collection be relaxed. The Kheda Movement was a major civil disobedience movement in the Kheda district of Gujarat, India, led by Mahatma Gandhi in 1918. The movement was a response to the oppressive taxation policies imposed by the British colonial government on the peasants of Kheda, who were already suffering from crop failures and economic hardships.

q_en: In India, during October-November, with the apparent movement of the sun towards the south, the ______ over the northern plains becomes weaker.
e_en: The correct answer is Monsoon trough In India, during October-November, with the apparent movement of the sun towards the south, the Monsoon trough over the northern plains becomes weaker. The monsoon trough is a low-pressure system that develops over the northern plains of India during the summer monsoon season, which typically lasts from June to September.

q_en: Techniques of making silk were first invented in China around ______ years ago.
e_en: The correct answer is 7000. Techniques for making silk were first invented in China around 7000 years ago. The Chinese developed the art of sericulture, mastering the cultivation of silkworms and the collection of their silk cocoons. The secrecy surrounding silk production in China was maintained for centuries, with strict regulations on exporting silkworm eggs or cocoons, allowing the Chinese to maintain a monopoly on silk.

q_en: Which of the following player was the highest scorer in the final match of cricket world cup 1983?
e_en: The correct answer is Krishnamachari Srikkanth. Krishnamachari Srikkanth was the highest scorer in the final match of the cricket world cup in 1983. He is a former Indian cricketer who played as an opening batsman. In the final match against the West Indies, Srikkanth scored 38 runs off 57 balls before being dismissed. Srikkanth's aggressive batting at the top of the order provided a solid start for the Indian team.

q_en: Lime stone is the raw material of _________, among the given industries.
e_en: The correct answer is cement industry. Limestone is a key raw material in cement production. Limestone is a common type of carbonate sedimentary rock. It is composed mostly of the minerals calcite and aragonite, which are different crystal forms of calcium carbonate. It aids in reducing sulfur emissions during fuel combustion in cement kilns. Heating limestone produces clinker, which is ground to make cement.

q_en: At Independence, about ______ percent of the India’s population was dependent on agriculture.
e_en: The correct answer is 75. At the time of India's independence in 1947, approximately 75 per cent of the country's population relied on agriculture for their livelihoods. Agriculture played a central role in the rural economy, with a majority of the rural population engaged in farming or related agricultural activities.

q_en: The honour of Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship carries ______________.
o_en: Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One lakh) along with a Tamrapatra and Angavastram
Rs.3,00,000/- (Rupees three lakh) along with a Tamrapatra and Angavastram
e_en: The correct answer is Rs.3,00,000/- (Rupees three lakh) along with a Tamrapatra and Angavastram. Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship: It is also known as Akademi Ratna Sadasyata. The greatest award bestowed by Sangeet Natak Akademi, regardless of nationality, ethnicity, caste, religion, creed, or sex, is the Fellowship. Anybody under 50 is not ordinarily eligible to be considered for the honor according to the criteria.

q_en: Mawsynram in the ______ of the Khasi Hills receives the highest average rainfall in the world.
e_en: The correct answer is Southern part. Mawsynram: Mawsynram is a town located 69 kilometers from Shillong, the state capital of Meghalaya state in northeastern India, in the Southern Khasi Hills area. In India, Mawsynram experiences the most rainfall. It is said to be the wettest site on Earth, receiving 11,872 millimeters of rain on average per year. The Guinness Book of World Records states that Mawsynram saw 26,000 millimeters of rain in 1985.

q_en: ________________, established in 1829, is the oldest golf club in India and the first outside Great Britain.
e_en: The correct answer is The Royal Calcutta Golf Club. The Royal Calcutta Golf Club was established in 1829, making it the oldest golf club in India. It is also the first golf club established outside of Great Britain. The club is located in Kolkata and has a rich history, having hosted several prestigious golf tournaments. Some of the notable members of the club include famous Indian cricketer Sourav Ganguly and former Indian President Pranab Mukherjee.

q_en: The Legislative Council of a state assembly __________ of the total number of members in the legislative of the state and in no case fewer than 40 members.
e_en: The correct answer is one-third. India's legislature is divided into two houses. Article 169 of the Constitution allows the states to have a Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) in addition to the Legislative Assembly ( Vidhan Sabha), much as Parliament has two Houses (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha).

q_en: Mahavir Jayanti is celebrated in the month of _________.
e_en: The correct answer is March-April. Mahavir Jayanti: For the Jain community, Mahavir Jayanti is one of the most auspicious holidays. The 24th and final Tirthankara (enlightened teacher) Mahavir of the Jain religion is born on this day. Achieving global peace and harmony in a way that harms living things as little as possible is highly valued in Jainism. Jains across celebrate Mahavir Jayanti with great enthusiasm.

q_en: __________banks are owned by their customers and follow the cooperative principle of one person, one vote.
e_en: The correct answer is Cooperative. Cooperative Banks: It is a cooperatively organized institution designed to handle standard banking operations. The founding principles of cooperative banks are share collections, deposit acceptance, and loan disbursements. These are cooperative credit societies, where community members band together to lend money to one another on advantageous terms.

q_en: Which water body surrounds India in the west?
e_en: The correct answer is Arabian Sea. The Arabian Sea lies to the west of India. It is a region of the northern Indian Ocean. It is bounded by Pakistan and Iran, on the west by the Gulf of Aden, Guardafui Channel, and the Arabian Peninsula, on the southeast by the Laccadive Sea, on the southeast by Somali Sea, and on the east by India.​

q_en: The objective of the first five year plan was to ________.
e_en: The correct answer is develop agriculture. First Five year Plan 1st five-year plan was for the period of 1951 to 1956. The target Growth was 2.1 % and the Actual Growth was 3.6 %. It was based on Harrod-Domar. The influx of refugees, severe food shortage & mounting inflation confronted the country at the onset of the first five-year plan. The primary aim of the 1st five-year plan was to improve the living standards of the people of India.

q_en: In the Indian constitution, Right to equality has ________ articles in it.
e_en: The correct answer is 5. Article 14 to Article 18 of the Constitution of India guarantees the right to equality to every citizen of India. This deals with the general principles of equality. Article 14 of the constitution states that: The State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India.

q_en: Which of the following city was the capital of the Pandyas?
e_en: The correct answer is Madurai. The Pandyas were one of the ancient Tamil dynasties that ruled over parts of southern India from around the 6th century BCE to the 17th century CE. Their kingdom was centered in what is now Tamil Nadu. They belonged to the group of three ancient Sangam age kingdoms known as "Muvendar," or the three crowns- The Pandyas, Chera and Chola.

q_en: Which article of the Indian Constitution deals with the fundamental duties?
e_en: The correct answer is 51A. Fundamental Duties: Part IV A of the Indian Constitution contains Article 51A, which deals with the Fundamental Duties. The Soviet Constitution (USSR) is where the idea of fundamental duties originated. Fundamental Duties were recommended in 1976 by the Swaran Singh Committee. Ten Fundamental Duties were added to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976.

q_en:
Which of the following forms an asset for a bank?
I. Reserves
II. Loans
e_en: The correct answer is Both I and II. An asset is something of value that can be owned by an individual or an organization and can be used to produce something profitable. For a bank, these are the resources that generate income and profit. A bank has assets such as cash held in its vaults and moneys that the bank holds at the Federal Reserve bank (called “reserves”), loans that are made to customers.

q_en: Where was the Communist Party of India (CPI) founded, in 1920?
e_en: The correct answer is Tashkent. Communist Party of India (CPI): It is a left-wing political party in India, founded in 1920 in Tashkent (now the capital of Uzbekistan). M.N. Roy was the first elected Commintern leader. The CPI was formally founded in 1925 at the Indian Communist Conference in Kanpur. It declared that revolution would be used to build socialism in India. Among its founders were M. N. Roy, his wife Evelyn Trent, M. P. T. Acharya and Abani Mukherji.

q_en: Which among the following folk dances is popularly known as the 'stick dance'?
e_en: The correct answer is Kolannalu. Kolannalu: India is home to a number of popular folk dances, including the well-known Kolannalu stick dance from Andhra Pradesh. The narrative of the wicked spirit Basavasura that transformed into deity assisting others is explained by the song, dance moves, and background music. The Kolannalu traditional dance is sometimes referred to as kolkolannalu and is widely known among the Andhra Pradeshi people as Kolattam in Telugu.

q_en: Trade agreement between two parties is called:
e_en: The correct answer is bilateral. A bilateral trade agreement is a pact between two parties, countries, or regions that outlines the terms and conditions for trade between them. In it, both parties agree to reduce or eliminate trade barriers such as tariffs and quotas to promote trade and investment. It can help to increase economic growth, create job opportunities, and improve the standard of living in both countries.

q_en: The Consumer Protection Act provides for a ___________ tier Consumer Disputes Redressal Agencies in India.
e_en: The correct answer is Three. Consumer Protection Act, 1986: The historic Consumer Protection Act, passed by the Indian Parliament in 1986, is a significant piece of socio-economic law that aims to promote public welfare by allowing consumers to engage directly in the market. The Act's goal when it was passed was to give greater protection to consumer interests.

q_en: Agriculture and fishing activities belong to which sector?
e_en: The correct answer is Primary sector. Products and services are produced as a result of economic activity, and sectors are collections of economic activities categorised according to certain standards. Based on ownership, labour conditions, and the type of activity, the Indian economy can be divided into several sectors.

q_en: ______ are a narrow belt of high altitude (above 12,000 m) westerly winds in the troposphere. Their speed varies from about 110 km/h in summer to about 184 km/h in winter.
e_en: The correct answer is Option A. Jet streams are narrow bands of strong high-altitude winds that flow in the upper troposphere and lower stratosphere, typically between 9 to 16 kilometers (5.5 to 10 miles) above the Earth's surface. They are characterized by high wind speeds, often exceeding 100 kilometers per hour (60 miles per hour), and have a significant impact on weather patterns. The jet streams are predominantly westerly winds, meaning they flow from west to east.

q_en: After independence, India launched its First five year plan in ______.
e_en: The correct answer is Option D. India launched its First Five-Year Plan in 1951. The plan was formulated by the Planning Commission, which was set up by the Government of India in 1950 to formulate and implement economic policies and development plans. The First Five-Year Plan aimed to achieve rapid industrialization and economic growth in India.

q_en: Which Indian dancer among the following was the Youngest recipient of Padma Vibhushan in 2003?
e_en: The correct answer is Option B, Sonal Mansingh, an eminent Indian classical dancer, was indeed the youngest recipient of the Padma Vibhushan in 2003. She received this prestigious award for her significant contributions to the field of dance.

q_en: Gandhi-Irwin pact was signed in which year?
e_en: The correct answer is Option A. The Gandhi-Irwin Pact, also known as the Delhi Pact, was signed on March 5, 1931. It was an agreement between Mahatma Gandhi, the leader of the Indian National Congress, and Lord Irwin, the then Viceroy of India, representing the British government. The pact marked a significant step in India's struggle for independence from British rule and initiated a dialogue between the Indian National Congress and the British government. ​

q_en: A budget document, which deals with the revenue receipts and revenue expenditure of the government for a particular financial year, is called ______.
e_en: The correct answer is Option A. A budget document that deals with the revenue receipts (income) and revenue expenditure (expenses)

q_en: Which union territory has the highest sex ratio as per the 2011 Census?
e_en: The correct answer is Puducherry. Puducherry has the highest sex ratio of 1037 females to every 1000 males. As per the 2011 census, India has 943 females per 1000 males. Puducherry: Puducherry, a French colonial settlement in India until 1954, is now a Union Territory town bounded by the southeastern Tamil Nadu state. Pondicherry is synonymous with the Aurobindo Ashram, founded by Sri Aurobindo and Mirra Alfassa in 1926.​

q_en: _______ is celebrated as Gujarati New Year in India.
e_en: The correct answer is Bestu Varsh. Gujarati New Year or Bestu Varsh was celebrated on 26 October 2022. The Gujarati New Year is also known as Vikram Sanvat 2079. Homes are decorated with Asopalav torans and marigold flowers. On this auspicious day, businessmen and traders start their new account books after closing the old ones.

q_en: Primary raw material for sugar industry is _______.
e_en: The correct answer is Sugar cane. Sugar cane is the primary raw material for the sugar industry. Sugar cane is a tropical, perennial grass that forms lateral shoots at the base to produce multiple stems, typically three to four meters high and about five cm in diameter. Its composition varies depending upon the climate, soil type, irrigation, fertilizers, insects, disease control, varieties, and the harvest period.

q_en: Which among the following classical dance forms was introduced in the 16th century by Vaishnava saint Mahapurusha Sankaradeva?
e_en: The correct answer is Sattriya. The great Assamese reformer and Vaishnava saint Mahapurusha Sankaradeva established the Sattriya dancing style in the 15th century A.D. as a potent means of spreading the Vaishnava religion. It is one of India's eight classical dance genres. Sankaradeva created this dance style by fusing ideas from numerous treatises with popular dance styles, regional folk dances, and his own unique perspective.

q_en: In which city is the Mohun Bagan Athletic club situated?
e_en: The correct answer is Kolkata. Established on 15th August 1889, Mohun Bagan Athletic Club is one of the oldest clubs in India & Asia. It is situated in Kolkata. It created history in 1911 by becoming the first Indian team to win IFA Shield, an event that has been closely linked with Indian nationalism. Mohun Bagan football team has won National League/I-League five times and Federation Cup a record fourteen times.

q_en: Removal of president of the country from the office is known as _______.
e_en: The correct answer is Impeachment. The removal of India’s President is done through the process of Impeachment. Article 61 of the Indian constitution provides the procedure of impeachment of the President.​

q_en: Who among the following Greek rulers sent Megasthenes to the court of Chandragupta Maurya?
e_en: The correct answer is Seleucus Nicator. Megasthenes was a Greek Diplomat, Historian, and ethnographer whose extensive writings about the cultures of India gave an insight into the lives of ancient Indians during the rule of Chandragupta Maurya. Seleucid-Mauryan War around 305 BC, Megasthenes became an ambassador for Seleucus I to the court of Chandragupta Maurya in Pataliputra. The compilation of Megasthenes’ work is known as Indica.

e_en: The correct answer is Division of land. The right of inheritance, specifically in the context of land or property, often leads to the division of land among heirs. Jyotibha Phule, the founder of Satyashodhak samaj Satyashodhak Samaj(Truth-seekers' Society) was a social reform society founded by Jyotirao Phule in Pune, Maharashtra, on 24 September 1873.
