The Halda Festival, one of Lahaul's most anticipated events, offers a memorable experience with its exotic drinks, hypnotic dance performances, joyful family reunions, and vibrant cultural celebrations.

q_en: Yamini Krishnamurthy has won various accolades in which form of dance?
e_en: The correct answer is Kuchipudi and Bharatanatyam. <span style="--tw-border-spacing-x: 0; --tw-border-spacing-y: 0; --tw-translate-x: 0; --tw-translate-y: 0; --tw-rotate: 0; --tw-skew-x: 0; --tw-skew-y: 0; --tw-scale-x: 1; --tw-scale-y: 1; --tw-pan-x: ; --tw-pan-y: ; --tw-pinch-zoom: ; --tw-scroll-snap-strictness: proximity; --tw-gradient-from-position: ; --tw-gradient-via-position: ; --tw-gradient-to-position: ; --tw-ordinal: ; --tw-slashed-zero: ; --tw-numeric-figure: ; --t…

q_en: The main focus of the First Five Year Plan was to develop the _________ sector like agriculture.
e_en: The correct answer is agricultural sector. The First Five Year Plan in India was active between 1951 and 1956. The plan was based on the Harrod-Domar model. This plan gave priority to the agricultural sector of the country. The First Five Year Plan was presented before the parliament by Jawaharlal Nehru. Gulzarilal Nanda was the first Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission of India. Economist K N Raj is known as the architect of this plan.

q_en: How many Fundamental rights are provided by Indian Constitution?
e_en: The correct answer 6 (Six). Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel is considered the father of Fundamental rights in India. Fundamental rights are justifiable. In the original constitution, there were seven categories of fundamental rights in India. After the deletion of the Right to property by the 44th Amendment, it was reduced to six. The right to property is a legal right now. The Supreme court and the High Courts are considered as the guardians of Fundamental rights in India.

q_en: The Dronacharya Award for coaches started in which year?
e_en: The Correct Answer is 1985. The Dronacharya Award was instituted in 1985. These awards are given by the Government of India for Excellency in the field of sports coaching. The award is given only to the disciplines included in the events like Olympic Games, Paralympic Games, Asian Games, Commonwealth Games, World Championship, and World Cup along with Cricket, Indigenous Games, and Parasports.

q_en: The _________ refers to the excess of government’s revenue expenditure over revenue receipts.
e_en: - Revenue deficit refers to a situation where the government's expenditure on revenue items such as salaries, subsidies, and interest payments exceeds its revenue receipts from sources such as taxes and dividends. - This means that the government is spending more than it is earning, which can lead to a budget deficit and borrowing to meet its expenses.

q_en: What is the name of the first Indian tribal president?
e_en: The correct answer is Droupadi Murmu. Former Jharkhand Governor and National Democratic Alliance candidate Droupadi Murmu were elected the 15th President of India on 21 July 2022. She is the first tribal woman to be elected to the position & the youngest as well. She defeated opposition candidate Yashwant Sinha by bagging 64.03% of the electoral college votes. She will take oath on 25 July 2022 and will replace Ram Nath Kovind.

q_en: Songkran is a Buddhist festival. This festival is celebrated for several days in the month of _______.
e_en: The correct answer is April. The Buddhist festival 'Songkran' is celebrated mainly in Arunachal Pradesh. This Buddhist festival is observed as a spring cleaning. It is celebrated for several days during the middle of April, people clean their houses wash clothes and enjoy sprinkling perfumed water on the monks.

q_en: As per the 73rd and 74th amendment India has ______-tier government system
e_en: The correct answer is Three. Panchayati Raj System - It was first introduced in India by the then Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru on 2 October 1959 in the Nagaur district of Rajasthan. Panchayati Raj system is the system of local self-government of rural India. Self-governance of urban areas is carried out by municipalities and sub-municipalities. Self-governance of rural areas is carried out through Panchayati Raj Institutions.

q_en: Which state has the highest sex ratio as per the Census 2011?
e_en: The correct answer is Kerala. As per the 2011 census, the State of Kerala had the highest sex ratio in India. Kerala with 1084 has the highest sex ratio. Sex ratio is defined as the number of females per thousand males. It was revealed that the population ratio in India 2011 is 943 females per 1000.

q_en: Shevroy Hills and the Javadi Hills are located to the __________.
e_en: The correct answer is southeast of the Eastern Ghats Shevroy Hills and the Javadi Hills are located to the southeast of the Eastern Ghats. The Western Ghats and the Eastern Ghats mark the western and the eastern edges of the Deccan Plateau respectively. The Western Ghats are higher than the Eastern Ghats. The Eastern Ghats stretch from the Mahanadi Valley to the Nilgiris in the south. Jindhagada Peak (1,690 meters) is the highest peak in the Eastern Ghats.

q_en: Jagoi and Cholom are the two main divisions in which of the following classical dance forms?
e_en: The correct answer is Manipuri. Manipuri is an ancient classical dance form that originated in the northeastern state of Manipur in India. Jagoi and cholom are the two main divisions in Manipur’s dance, the one gentle and the other vigorous, corresponding to the lasya and tandava elements described in Sanskrit literature.

q_en: Which Article of the Constitution of India mandates the position of a Vice President of India?
e_en: The correct answer is option B i.e, ​Article 63. The Vice President of India is the second-highest constitutional office in India after the President. Article 63 of the Indian Constitution states that there shall be a Vice President of India. Article 66 of the Indian Constitution deals with the election of the Vice President. He is the ex-officio chairman of the Rajya Sabha. The first vice president of India was Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan.

q_en: For the first time in the world, the Five-Year Plan (1928–32), was implemented by ___________ in Soviet Union.
e_en: The correct answer is Joseph Stalin. Joseph Stalin was the Russian leader who first implemented the Five Year Plan approach in Russia. Joseph Stalin implemented the first FYP in the Soviet Union in the late 1920s. Most communist states and many capitalist countries later adopted them.

q_en: Which of the following major incidents occurred in 1919?
e_en: The correct answer is 'Jallianwala Bagh Massacre'. The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place on 13 April 1919 (on the day of Baisakhi). It took place at Jallianwala Bagh near the Golden Temple in Amritsar, Punjab province of India. A large peaceful crowd had gathered to protest against the Rowlatt Act An English officer named General Dyer blocked the exit with his troops and ordered them to shoot at the crowd, continuing to fire even as the protestors tried to flee.

q_en: The 12th Five-Year Plan aims to achieve annual average economic growth rate of ___________.
e_en: The correct answer is 8.2 per cent. 12th Five-Year Plan(2012-17) It was India's last five-year plan. It aims at a growth rate of 8%. 12th Five-Year Plan focuses on Growth that is Faster, Inclusive, and Sustainable. It aims to reduce poverty by 10% during the 12th Five-Year Plan. There will be Agriculture growth at 4% and Manufacturing growth at 10%. Every state must attain a higher growth rate than the rate achieved during the 11th plan.

q_en: Which of the following rivers is named only once in Rigveda?
e_en: The correct answer is Ganga. Rigveda is one of the oldest sacred texts of Hinduism, composed in the ancient Sanskrit language. It contains hymns and prayers dedicated to various deities and natural elements like rivers, mountains, and forests. Among the rivers mentioned in Rigveda, Ganga is the only one that is named just once, in the 10th book, hymn 75, verse 5.

q_en: Which of the following is a professional table tennis player?
e_en: The correct answer is Manika Batra. Manika Batra is a professional table tennis player who has won several medals for India at international events.

q_en: Ruler of which dynasty built the Kandariya Mahadeva temple in 999?
e_en: The correct answer is Chandela. The ruler of the Chandela dynasty built the Kandariya Mahadeva temple in 999 AD. The temple is located in Khajuraho, Madhya Pradesh and is one of the finest examples of medieval Indian architecture. The Chandela dynasty ruled over a large part of central India between the 9th and 13th centuries. The temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva and is famous for its intricate carvings and sculptures.

q_en: Which article of Indian constitution is related with Protection of interests of minorities?
e_en: The correct answer is 29. Article 29 provides protection to the interests of minorities by ensuring that they have the right to conserve their distinct language, script, and culture. This article prohibits the denial of admission to any educational institution on the grounds of religion, race, cast

q_en: The prime themes of Kathak are tied to which of the following cults of Hinduism?
e_en: The correct answer is Vaishnavism​. The Vaishnavite cult which swept North India in the 15th century. and the resultant bhakti movement contributed to a whole new range of lyrics and musical forms. The Radha-Krishna theme proved immensely popular alongwith the works of Mirabai, Surdas, Nandadas and Krishnadas.

q_en: What helps in the cultivation of rabi crops?
e_en: The correct answer is Mahawat. Mahawat helps in the cultivation of rabi crops as it brings moisture to the soil and helps in the growth of crops. Southeast trade winds do not have a significant impact on the cultivation of rabi crops as they bring dry air and low humidity. Westerly jet streams are high-altitude winds that do not directly affect the cultivation of crops. Northwest winds can bring cold and dry air, which can adversely affect the growth of crops.

q_en: The Finance Commission of India submits its report to ________.
e_en: The correct answer is The President of India. The Finance Commission of India is a constitutional body that is set up under Article 280 of the Indian Constitution. Its primary responsibility is to recommend the distribution of tax revenues between the central and state governments. The Finance Commission submits its report to the President of India, who is the head of the state and represents the country internationally.

q_en: Which state has the lowest sex ratio as per the Census 2011?
e_en: The correct answer is Haryana. As per Census 2011, Haryana has the lowest sex ratio, i.e., the number of females per 1000 males. The sex ratio is a valuable source for identifying the female population in India and what is the ratio between women and men in India. It was revealed in the 2011 Population Census that the Indian population ratio 2011 is 943 females per 1000 males. Haryana has India's lowest sex ratio and the figure shows a number of 877 females to 1000 males.

q_en: Which of the following is an output of farming?
e_en: The correct answer is crops. Farming is the process of producing food, fiber, and other products by cultivating crops and raising livestock. The output of farming includes various agricultural products such as crops, fruits, vegetables, dairy products, meat, and eggs. Crops are the most common output of farming, and they are grown for various purposes such as food, fuel, fiber, and medicine.

q_en: A microfinance loan is defined as a collateral-free loan given to a household having annual household income up to Rs. _______.
e_en: The correct answer is 3 00000. <span style="--tw-border-spacing-x: 0; --tw-border-spacing-y: 0; --tw-translate-x: 0; --tw-translate-y: 0; --tw-rotate: 0; --tw-skew-x: 0; --tw-skew-y: 0; --tw-scale-x: 1; --tw-scale-y: 1; --tw-pan-x: ; --tw-pan-y: ; --tw-pinch-zoom: ; --tw-scroll-snap-strictness: proximity; --tw-gradient-from-position: ; --tw-gradient-via-position: ; --tw-gradient-

q_en: Which is the last Five year plan that was put to effect in India?
e_en: The correct answer is Twelfth (12th). Twelfth (12th) Five Year Plan (FYP) was the last official Five Year Plan of India. The period of the plan was from 2012-2017. The first priority of the Twelfth Plan was to bring the economy back to rapid growth while ensuring that the growth is both inclusive and sustainable. The broad vision and aspirations which the Twelfth Plan seeks to fulfill were reflected in the subtitle: ‘Faster, Sustainable, and More Inclusive Growth’.

q_en: Gaddam Padmaja Reddy won Padma Shri for which dance form?
e_en: The correct answer is Kuchipudi. <ul style="--tw-border-spacing-x: 0; --tw-border-spacing-y: 0; --tw-translate-x: 0; --tw-translate-y: 0; --tw-rotate: 0; --tw-skew-x: 0; --tw-skew-y: 0; --tw-scale-x: 1; --tw-scale-y: 1; --tw-pan-x: ; --tw-pan-y: ; --tw-pinc

q_en: Captain Roop Singh Stadium is located in which of the following city?
e_en: The correct answer is Gwalior. Captain Roop Singh Stadium is a cricket stadium in the Gwalior district of Madhya Pradesh. It was established in 1978. The first ODI on this ground was played in 1988.

q_en: Why was the year 1757 an important year for the English East India Company in India?
o_en: In 1757 the English East India Company got control over Hyderabad by defeating the Nizam in the Battle of Plassey.
In 1757 the English East India Company got control over Madras by defeating Nawab Siraj-ud-daulah in the Battle of Plassey.
In 1757 the English East India Company got control over Oudh by defeating Nawab Siraj-ud-daulah in the Battle of Berar.
In 1757 the English East India Company got control over Bengal by defeating Nawab Siraj-ud-daulah in the Battle of Plassey.
e_en: The correct answer is Battle of Plassey. The Battle of Plassey was a decisive victory of the British East India Company over the Nawab of Bengal and his French allies on 23 June 1757, under the leadership of Robert Clive. The victory was made possible by the defection of Mir Jafar, who was Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah's commander in chief.

q_en: Which among the following festivals is also known as Dala Puja devoted to worshiping the sun is traditionally celebrated by the people of Bihar?
e_en: The correct answer is Chhath Puja. Chhath Puja: Chhath is a Hindu festival dedicated to the Sun god and his wife Usha in order to thank them for bestowing the bounties of life on earth. The Goddess who is worshipped during the famous Chhath Puja is known as Chhathi Maiya (also known as Usha, wife of the sun god). The word Chhath means sixth and the festival is celebrated on the sixth day of the month Kartika of the Hindu lunar Vikram Samvat calendar.

q_en: M.S.Swaminathan (father of Green Revolution in India), was _______ by profession.
e_en: The correct answer is scientist. M.S. Swaminathan is a renowned Indian scientist, also known as the "Father of the Green Revolution in India." He is an agricultural scientist who is credited with introducing high-yielding varieties of wheat and rice, which helped India become self-sufficient in food production. Swaminathan has received several awards and honors for his contributions to agriculture, including the Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Vibhushan.

q_en: Iron and steel are ______ industries.
e_en: The correct answer is mineral based. Iron and steel industries are mineral-based industries. Iron and steel are manufactured using minerals such as iron ore, coal, and limestone. These minerals are extracted from mines and processed to produce iron and steel. This industry is considered a part of the heavy industry sector, which relies heavily on mineral resources.

q_en: In India, by whom is the Chief Minister appointed?
e_en: The correct answer is Governor. Chief Minister: According to Article 164 in the Indian Constitution, the Governor appoints a Chief Minister. The state's chief minister is chosen from among the leaders of the parties that received the majority of the votes cast in the assembly elections. The Chief Minister has actual executive authority, with the Governor serving as the de facto head of state.

q_en: In India, the monsoon lasts for ______ days from early June to mid-September.
e_en: The correct answer is 100 - 120. Monsoons are seasonal winds that reverse their course in response to the onset of a new season. The Arabic term for season, "mawsim," is thought to be the source of the word "monsoon." It is maintained in the region between 20 °N and 20 °S. It lasts for 100–120 days, starting in early June and ending in mid-September. India receives about 80% of its annual rainfall during the monsoon season.

q_en: Which of the following players scored the first century in a cricket test match for India?
e_en: The correct answer is Lala Amarnath. Lala Amarnath: In Indian cricket, Lala Amarnath Bhardwaj, who lived from 11 September 1911 to 5 August 2000, is revered as the father figure. During England's 1933 tour of India, he achieved the first-ever century for India in Test Cricket. He led India in their maiden Test series victory over Pakistan in 1952 and was the country's first cricket captain after independence.

q_en: What was the main need for the use of high yielding varieties of seeds in the Green Revolution in India?
o_en: Use of old methods of crop cultivation
Use of irregular supply of water
e_en: The correct answer is Use of fertilizers and pesticides. For high yielding seed varieties to flourish, they need an abundance of nutrients. These nutrients are given to the plants by fertilisers, which bo

q_en: In which year was the Depressed Classes Association founded by B.R. Ambedkar?
e_en: The correct answer is 1930. BR Ambedkar founded the Depressed Classes Association (DCA) on July 23, 1930, in Bombay (now Mumbai). It was formed to fight for the rights of the Scheduled Castes/Dalits (formerly known as untouchables), who were oppressed and discriminated against by the upper caste. It was involved in the meetings with Lord Irwin and demanded a provision for separate electorates in India for the depressed classes.

q_en: According to Chola inscriptions, what was the land for maintaining schools called?
e_en: સાચો જવાબ શાલભોગ છે. The following land classifications are mentioned in the Chola inscriptions: devdan Land granted to temples and religious institutions. Shalbhogh Land granted for maintenance of schools. Brahmadeya A type of land granted to Brahmins or priests. Vellanavagai Property/land owned by a non-Brahmin cultivator or soldier. Pallicchandam Land donated to Jain institutions.

q_en: Hurka Baul dance is mainly a narrative dance form performed during the harvesting of maize and paddy crops. It belongs to which of the following states?
e_en: The correct answer is Uttrakhand. Hurka Baul: The "Hurka," or drum, which is used to accompany the "Baul," or singing, is where the word "Hurka Baul" originates. In the Kumaon region of Uttrakhand, it is carried out when growing maize and paddy. Dance is mainly a narrative dance form performed during harvesting. Hurka Baul dance is an integral part of the cultural heritage of Uttarakhand and is performed during various festivals and celebrations in the state.

q_en: The roads connecting the state capital to various district headquarters are known as ______. These roads are constructed and maintained by the State Public Works Department (PWD) in the states and union territories.
e_en: The correct answer is State Highway. State Highway: State Highways are the roads that connect the state capital to various district headquarters. They are considered to be an important part of the transportation infrastructure of a state or a union territory. These are constructed and maintained by the State Public Works Department (PWD) in the respective states and union territories.

q_en: Sajibu Cheiraoba is a Lunar New Year festival of people following the Sanamahism religion in the Indian state of ______.
e_en: The correct answer is Manipur. Sajibu Cheiraoba: Every year, in Manipur, Sajibu Cheiraoba is celebrated at the end of March or the beginning of April. Ritual performances are held to commemorate the occasion and bring good fortune for the coming year. The Cheiraoba festival marks the beginning of a new year based on the lunar calendar and mathematical computations related to the customs and cultural legacy of the Meitei community in India.

q_en: Where were the first modern Olympic Games held under the IOC?
e_en: The correct answer is In Athens. International Olympic Committee (IOC): One non-governmental organization involved in sports is the International Olympic Committee. It is situated in Switzerland's Lausanne. Pierre de Coubertin founded the IOC on June 23, 1894. Demetrios Vikelas served as its first president. The International Olympic Committee (IOC) oversees both the national Olympic Committees (NOCs) and the global Olympic Movement.

q_en: What is the full form of NABARD?
o_en: National Bank for Agriculture and River Development
National Bank for Architecture and Rural Development
National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development
National Body for Agriculture and Rural Development
e_en: The correct answer is National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development. NABARD is the acronym used for National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development. NABARD: India's top development bank, NABARD, aims to support fair and sustainable rural and agricultural development. As per the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development Act, 1981, it is a statutory body that was founded in 1982 by Parliament. Its headquarter is located in Mumbai, India.

q_en: Who among the following has been awarded the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for Kathak?
e_en: The correct answer is Sunaina Hazarilal. Sunaina Hazarilal: Indian classical dancer Sunayana Hazarilal Agarwal is renowned for her proficiency in the Kathak classical dance style. She is purportedly the last living practitioner of the Janakiprasad Gharana of Kathak, popularly referred to as the Banares Gharana. In 2011, the Indian government bestowed upon her the Padma Shri, the fourth highest civilian honor.

q_en: The principle of fundamental rights in the Indian Constitution has been taken from which of the following countries?
e_en: The correct answer is United States of America. Fundamental Rights: Fundamental Rights in the Constitution of India are enshrined in Part III (Article 12-35) of the Constitution, which guarantees civil liberties such as freedom of speech, religion, and equality before the law. These Fundamental Rights were inspired by the Bill of Rights of the United States Constitution, which was adopted in 1791.

q_en: In the first phase of the Green Revolution, the use of HYV seeds was limited to the more prosperous states. Who among the following was not included in this list?
e_en: The correct answer is Karnataka. The Green Revolution, which refers to the large-scale introduction of high-yielding varieties of seeds, fertilizers, and pesticides in agriculture, has been criticized for its negative impact on small farmers. the Government of India launched the Green Revolution in 1965 under the Third Five-Year Plan(1961-66).

q_en: 'Maghi' is another name for which of the following festivals of India?
e_en: The correct answer is Makar Sankranti. Maghi is the regional name for the Makar Sankranti festival, celebrated in Punjab, Haryana, Jammu Division, and Himachal Pradesh. Makar Sankranti is a Hindu festival celebrated in January (usually January 14 of the Gregorian calendar), marking the transition of the sun into the zodiac sign of Makara (Capricorn). It is always celebrated on the first day of the month of Magha in the Vikrami calendar.

q_en: Prince Shuddendra Narayan Singh Deo has been awarded the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for his contribution to ______ dance.
e_en: The correct answer is Chhau. Prince Shuddendra Narayan Singh Deo was awarded the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1963 for his contribution to Chhau dance. He was born in 1927 and was the youngest son of the former Maharaja of Seraikella in Singhbhum district (Now Jharkhand).​ He is a well-known exponent of the Seraikella Chhau style, which is known for its intricate footwork, graceful hand gestures, and elaborate costumes.

q_en: In which decade did the Green Revolution take place in India?
e_en: The correct answer is 1960-1970. The Green Revolution was a period of agricultural transformation that took place in the 1960s and 1970s in India. The goal of the Green Revolution was to increase agricultural productivity and food security by introducing high-yielding crop varieties (HYV seeds), modern irrigation systems, and chemical fertilizers and pesticides.

q_en: Telephones, cellular telecommunications, pagers, telephone exchanges, and radar are examples of which industry?
e_en: The correct answer is Information Technology and Electronics Industry. Telephones, cellular telecommunications, pagers, telephone exchanges, and radar are all examples of electronic devices used for communication and information transfer. The Information Technology and Electronics Industry deals with the design, development, and manufacturing of electronic devices, software, and systems for communication, computing, and entertainment.

q_en: Whom did Udham Singh kill?
e_en: The correct answer is Michael O'Dwyer. Udham Singh was an Indian revolutionary who assassinated Michael O'Dwyer in March 1940. The assassination was carried out as payback for O'Dwyer's involvement in the 1919 Jallianwala Bagh massacre in Amritsar, which Singh personally survived. On December 26, 1899, in Lahore, British India, Udham Singh was born "Sher Singh" into a Sikh household. His parents were Tehal Singh and Narain Kaur.

q_en: Which of the following Chinese pilgrims visited India about 50 years after Xuan Tsang?
e_en: The correct answer is I-king. I-king/sing, also known as Yijing, was a Chinese Buddhist monk who visited India around 50 years after Xuan Tsang. He sailed from Canton to India in 671 and arrived there in 673. Following his tour of the holy Buddhist sites in Magadha. He spent 10 years studying the Vinya at the illustrious Nalanda monastery (676–685).

q_en: How many minutes is the duration of a Kabaddi match?
e_en: The correct answer is 40 minutes. Kabaddi is a popular contact sport in South Asia. It is played between two teams of 7 players each. The objective of the game is for a player, known as a raider, to cross into the opposing team's half and tag as many defenders as possible before returning to their own half. A match consists of two halves, each lasting 20 minutes (total 40 minutes), with a break of 5 minutes in between.

q_en: The only confirmed active volcano located in India, the Barren Island Volcano is located about 138 km north east of _______ in the Andaman Islands.
e_en: The correct answer is Port Blair. Port Blair: It is the capital of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. The only active volcano in India is the Barren Islands, which is located north of Port Blair. It has seen significant improvements in Internet Connectivity with the Chennai-Andaman & Nicobar Islands (CANI) cable. It is the entrance to the pristine islands. It receives roughly 300 cm of rainfall on average.

q_en: ______ is the custodian of the country's foreign exchange reserves and is vested with the responsibility of managing their investments.
e_en: The correct answer is Reserve Bank of India. Reserve Bank of India (RBI) It is India’s central bank. In compliance with the terms of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934. It was founded on April 1, 1935, in Calcutta. It was permanently moved to Mumbai in 1937. Though originally privately owned, since nationalisation in 1949, the Reserve Bank is fully owned by the Government of India. The foreign exchange reserves are solely under its custody.

q_en: How many field umpires are there in a cricket match?
e_en: The correct answer is 2. Field Umpires: Two field umpires are chosen, one for the bowlers' end and one for the strikers' end, to oversee the game. They will choose places from which they may readily observe any action that may necessitate their decision. After one inning for each team, the umpires will switch ends.

q_en: What proportion of the proposed jobs has been reserved for women as per the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)?
e_en: The correct answer is one third. The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA): The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) was enacted by the Central Government of India in the year 2005. It mandates that women must receive priority in order for them to make up at least one-third of the beneficiaries. Established by the Ministry of Rural Development. MGNREGA is one of the biggest labor guarantee programs globally.

q_en: During whose tenure among the following the Swarn Singh Committee was formed?
e_en: The correct answer is Indira Gandhi. Indira Gandhi: She was the first female prime minister of India and the second with the longest tenure. She joined as a member of the Congress's Working Committee in 1955. She declared the nationalization of banks in India on July 19, 1969. She was instrumental in the enactment of the 26th Amendment to the Indian Constitution, which abolished the Privy Purse and nullified Articles 291 and 362.

q_en: Who chooses the Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
o_en: Only members of the Lok Sabha from the ruling party
e_en: The correct answer is All members of Lok Sabha. Speaker of the Lok Sabha: Article 93 of the Constitution provides for the election of the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker. He or she needs to be a House member. He or she is elected from among the members of the Lok Sabha by a simple majority of all members present and voting. His term in office is five

q_en: Which folk dance of Punjab is mainly performed by women?
e_en: The correct answer is Giddha. Giddha: It is a well-liked folk dance performed by females in the Punjab area. It is distinct from other types of Punjabi traditional dance. It is not necessary to perform the two-headed barrel dhol drum. It depicts the histories of women's lives, encompassing domestic life, marriage, and homesickness. Other Punjab folk dances are: Bhangra. Luddi. Kikkli. Sammi. Gatka(Dankara). Jhumar. Jaago.

q_en: How many events are there in decathlon?
e_en: The correct answer is 10. Decathlon is a combined event in athletics consisting of ten track and field events. The events in decathlon are 100 meters, 400 meters,1500 meters, 110 meters of hurdles, long jump, shot put, high jump, discus throw, pole vault, and javelin throw. The pentathlon events that took place at the ancient Greek Olympics gave rise to the decathlon. Pentathlons comprised five events: sprint, discus throw, javelin throw, long jump, and wrestling battle.

q_en: Articles 25 to 28 of the Indian Constitution deal with __________.
e_en: The correct answer is Rights to freedom of religion. Articles 25 to 28 of the Indian Constitution are part of the Fundamental Rights which gives Rights to freedom of religion. Article 25 guarantees the freedom of conscience and the right to freely profess, practice, and propagate religion, subject to public order, morality, and health.

q_en: Per capita income represents the average __________ earned by a person in that country.
e_en: The correct answer is Income. Per capita income is a measure of the average income earned by an individual in a particular country. It is calculated by dividing the total income of a country by its total population. It is a useful indicator of a country's economic well-being and can be used to compare the standard of living across different countries.

q_en: Which of the following is not a category of Indian Railway tracks?
e_en: The correct answer is Foot gauge. Indian Railway tracks are categorized based on the distance between the two rails, which is measured in terms of gauge. These are: Indian Railway tracks <td style="text-align: center;"

q_en: Which of the following festivals is not celebrated in Uttar Pradesh?

Bringing the opponent into immediate danger
Holding of opponent on the ground

Freestyle wrestling is an Olympic sport for both men and women.

q_en: Pongal is a four-day-long harvest festival, which is celebrated at the harvest of crops like sugarcane and __________.
e_en: The correct answer is Rice. Pongal: Pongal is a four-day-long harvest festival celebrated mostly in the states of South India, especially in Tamil Nadu. q_en: From which state, the performing art 'Ottamthullal' belongs?

To protest against the prevalent socio-political structure and prejudices of the society, Kunchan Nambiar used it as a medium. Now it is a famous folk art presented in the temples of Kerala.

Poverty can be measured in terms of income level, but it also encompasses a lack of access to basic needs such as food, shelter, education, and healthcare.

q_en: According to Constitution of India a governor can be appointed _________

This provision allows for administrative efficiency and the reduction of administrative costs. The President of India appoints the Governor, who holds office during the pleasure of the President.

q_en: Credit of invention of the Chess game goes to:
e_en: The correct answer is India. The game of chess is believed to have originated in India during the Gupta Empire in the 6th century AD. It was initially called "Chaturanga," which means "four divisions of the military" - infantry, cavalry, elephants, and chariots, which are represented by the pieces that would evolve into the modern pawn, knight, bishop, and rook, respectively.

q_en: The period from the decline of the Mauryas to the rise of the Guptas (2nd century BCE to 3rd century CE) is known in Indian history as the _________ period.
e_en: The correct answer is Post-Mauryan. The period from the decline of the Mauryas to the rise of the Guptas is referred to as the Post-Mauryan period. This era spanned from the 2nd century BCE to the 3rd century CE. It was a time of significant political fragmentation and the rise of several regional kingdoms in India. The Post-Mauryan period saw the growth of new trade routes, the spread of Buddhism and Jainism, and the flourishing of arts and architecture.

q_en: The first census of Independent India was conducted in 1951, which was the ____________ census in its continuous series.
e_en: The correct answer is eighth. The census is a regular and systematic collection of data about the population. India has a long tradition of conducting the census, which started in 1872. The 1881 Census is considered the first complete census in India, marking the start of the continuous decennial census series under British colonial administration. The first census after India gained independence was conducted in 1951.

q_en: Which Five-Year Plan of India was known as the "Mahalanobis Plan"?
e_en: The correct answer is Second Five-Year Plan. The Second Five-Year Plan of India, spanning from 1956 to 1961, is commonly known as the "Mahalanobis Plan" after the prominent Indian statistician Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis. It focused on the rapid industrialization of the country, particularly emphasizing the development of the heavy industries sector.

q_en: Which of the following has invented the musical instrument Bamhum and Tikzik?

q_en: From which date, Indian Financial year begins?
e_en: The correct answer is 1st April. The Indian Financial Year begins on 1st April and ends on 31st March of the next year. This accounting period is used by the Government of India and most businesses to prepare financial statements and reports. The financial year starting from 1st April aligns with the agricultural cycle in India, facilitating better planning and budgeting for the government and businesses.

q_en: In which year was the Second Anglo-Burma War fought?

Outcome resulted in a decisive British victory and the annexation of Lower Burma, including the key port city of Rangoon (Yangon). Impact strengthened British control over Burma, making it a significant part of British India and laying the groundwork for further conflict leading to the Third Anglo-Burma War in 1885.

q_en: Who was the last ruler of the Mauryan empire?
e_en: The correct answer is Brihadratha. Brihadratha Maurya was the final ruler of the Mauryan dynasty, reigning from around 187 BCE to 180 BCE. He was assassinated by his own general, Pushyamitra Shunga, during a military parade. His reign marked the further disintegration of the Mauryan Empire. His death ended the Mauryan Empire, a significant era in Indian history.

q_en: Which of the following sectors is the most labour absorbing sector of the economy?
e_en: The correct answer is Agriculture. Agriculture is the most labor-absorbing sector in many developing countries, including India. It includes a variety of activities such as crop production, livestock rearing, forestry, and fishing.

q_en:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding Classification of Expenditure of government?
I. Revenue Expenditure is expenditure incurred for purposes other than the creation of physical or financial assets of the central government.
II. Capital expenditure results in creation of physical or financial assets or reduction in financial liabilities.
e_en: The correct answer is Both I and II. Revenue Expenditure refers to expenditures necessary for the day-to-day functioning of the government and the provision of services. These are typically recurring expenses aimed at maintaining current operations rather than investing in new infrastructure or assets. Revenue Expenditure is different from Capital Expenditure, which is spent on creating assets or reducing liabilities.

q_en: What does "LBW" stand for in cricket?
e_en: The correct answer is Leg Before Wicket. Leg Before Wicket (LBW) is one of the ways a batsman can be dismissed in the sport of cricket. The rule is designed to prevent the batsman from using their legs to block the ball from hitting the stumps. The umpire decides if the batsman is out LBW based on specific criteria defined in the cricket laws.

q_en: Which of the following is NOT one of the fundamental rights mentioned in the Indian Constitution?
e_en: The correct answer is Right to exploitation. The Indian Constitution guarantees six fundamental rights to its citizens. The rights mentioned are Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right against Exploitation, Right to Freedom of Religion, Cultural and Educational Rights, and Right to Constitutional Remedies. There is no fundamental right called "Right to exploitation"; the correct term is "Right against Exploitation".

q_en: The growth rate target for the twelfth five year plan was ________.
e_en: The correct answer is 8%. The Twelfth Five-Year Plan of India (2012-2017) aimed to promote "faster, sustainable, and more inclusive growth." The actual GDP growth rate during the Twelfth Plan period averaged around 6-6.5%, significantly lower than the target of 8%. Infrastructure development was one of the most critical components, including transport, energy, telecommunications, and urban development.

q_en: In which of the following states is the festival Vishu celebrated?
e_en: The correct answer is Kerala. Vishu is an important festival in the state of Kerala, celebrated with great enthusiasm and joy. It marks the beginning of the Malayalam New Year and is observed in the month of April. The festival is known for the ritual of 'Vishukkani,' which means "the first thing seen on Vishu." Traditional customs include lighting lamps and seeing auspicious items like rice, fruits, and flowers first thing in the morning.

q_en: Which of the following is a dance form of Assam?
e_en: The correct answer is Bihu. Bihu is a traditional folk dance of Assam that is performed during the Bihu festival, which marks the Assamese New Year. Bihu dance is characterized by brisk dance steps, rapid hand movements, and rhythmic beats played on traditional instruments like the dhol and pepa. The dance is performed by both men and women, dressed in traditional Assamese attire, which includes colorful mekhela chadors for women and dhotis and gamosas for men.

q_en: Rann Utsav promotes natural beauty and other famous traveling places of the stunning zone of _________ During the full moon nights in the winter season, the white sand desert looks more mesmerizing.

q_en: Most of Ashoka's inscriptions were in _________ language and were written in the _________ script.
e_en: The correct answer is Prakrit, Brahmi. Most of Ashoka's inscriptions were in the Prakrit language, which was the lingua franca of the time. Ashoka's use of the Prakrit language and Brahmi script made his messages accessible to a larger audience, including the common people.

q_en: Which sport is played by the Indian sportsperson Bhakti Sharma?

q_en: In which of the following years was the Bombay High Court of India established?
e_en: The correct answer is 1862. The Bombay High Court, one of the oldest High Courts in India, was established on August 14, 1862. It was established under the Indian High Courts Act of 1861 by Queen Victoria. The jurisdiction of the Bombay High Court extends to the states of Maharashtra, Goa, and the Union Territories of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu. The court has its principal seat in Mumbai (Bombay) and benches at Nagpur, Aurangabad, and Panaji (Goa).

q_en: Various Industrialists came together in 1944 and drafted a joint proposal for setting up a planned economy in India. It is famously known as the _________ Plan.
e_en: The correct answer is Bombay Plan. The Bombay Plan was a set of proposals for the economic development of India, put forward by eight leading industrialists in 1944. The key figures involved were J.R.D. Tata, G.D. Birla, Lala Shri Ram, Kasturbhai Lalbhai, Ardeshir Dalal, A.D. Shroff, and John Mathai. The plan emphasized the importance of a mixed economy with both public and private sectors playing significant roles in the economic development.

q_en: India got its central bank in which year?
e_en: The correct answer is 1935. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was established on April 1, 1935. It was set up based on the recommendations of the Hilton Young Commission. q_en: Which state of India has the highest population density as per 2011 census?

q_en: Who was the founder of the Brahmo Samaj?

q_en: What is Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)?

q_en: Who among the following had written the National anthem of Bangladesh 'Amar Sonar Bangla'?
e_en: The correct answer is Rabindranath Tagore. Rabindranath Tagore wrote "Amar Sonar Bangla" to inspire the liberation struggle. The song was written in 1905 during the first partition of Bengal by Lord Curzon. This song was meant to rekindle the unified spirit of Bengal, to raise public consciousness against the communal political divide. The first ten lines of this song constitute Bangladesh's national anthem, adopted in 1971 during its liberation war.

q_en: Which is the highest civilian award in the state of Tamil Nadu, India, to recognize artists in the state for their achievements?
e_en: The correct answer is Kalaimamani. The Kalaimamani is the highest civilian award in the state of Tamil Nadu, India. These awards are given by the Tamil Nadu Iyal Isai Nataka Mandram (literature, music, and theatre), a unit of the Directorate of Art and Culture, Government of Tamil Nadu, to acknowledge artists in the state for their attainment.

q_en: The decennial Census is conducted by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner belonging to which ministry?
o_en: Ministry of Statistics and Program Implementation
e_en: The correct answer is the Ministry of Home Affairs. All censuses after 1951 were conducted under the Census Act of 1948. The responsibility of conducting the decadal census rests with the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India, Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India. The last census was conducted in 2011. Census is a Union subject under Article 246 of the Constitution of India.

q_en: The Indian political system is often described as a federal system with a strong unitary bias. Which feature gives it this unitary bias?
e_en: The correct answer is Single Citizenship. Single Citizenship is defined as every citizen of India holds only one citizenship i.e. is of India rather than that of any state. This implies that all citizens share the same legal rights, obligations, and protections, promoting a unified national identity. Part II of Constitution incudes articles related to citizenship.

q_en: Who among the following was the second ruler of the Mauryan empire?
e_en: The correct answer is Bindusara. Bindusara succeeded his father Chandragupta Maurya. Under Bindusara, the Mauryan Empire is said to have expanded further south. His Greek name, Amitrochates (or Amitrochades), which translates as "the slayer of foes." He was succeeded by his son "Ashoka."

q_en: What is a "maiden over" in cricket?
o_en: An over with no runs scored by the batsman
An over bowled by a spin bowler
An over where the bowler takes a wicket
e_en: The correct answer is An over with no runs scored by the batsman. Innings: This refers to the period during which a team or player bats. In Test matches, each team has two innings, while in limited-overs formats, each team has one. Wicket: This term has dual meanings: it can refer to the set of three stumps and two bails at either end of the pitch or to the dismissal of a batsman (e.g., "He took five wickets in the match").

q_en: A ________ government governs within the bounds established by constitutional law and citizen rights.
e_en: The correct answer is Democratic. In a democratic government, power is derived from the consent of the governed. It operates according to the principles set out in a constitution. important factors of democracy includes: rule of law, Protection of Rights, Separation of Powers, Regular Elections and so on. There are two types of democracy: Direct Democracy: Citizens directly participate in decision-making (e.g., referendums).

q_en: 'Bathukammas' is associated with which of the following states?
e_en: The correct answer is Telangana. Bathukamma" is a floral festival celebrated in Telangana. It is celebrated usually during Navratri, in late September or early October. Bathukamma means "Mother Goddess come alive". It is celebrated with colorful flower decorations, singing, and dancing. The festival is a tribute to Goddess Maha Gauri, a form of Goddess Durga. It is celebrated to emphasizes the importance of nature, femininity, and community.

q_en: Right to freedom of speech and expression is given under:
e_en: The correct answer is Article 19. The Right to Freedom of Speech and Expression under Article 19(1)(a) of the Indian Constitution. Article 19 is not completely absolute. It also impose some reasonable restrictions. The right includes: Right to Propagate One's Views. Right to Information. Freedom of the Press. Right to Criticize Government. Commercial Speech. Article 19(2) allows the state to impose reasonable restrictions on certain grounds.

q_en: In __________, the Planning Commission was set up with the Prime Minister as its Chairperson.
e_en: The correct answer is 1950. The Planning Commission was set up on March 15, 1950. It is headed by Prime Minister of India. Jawaharlal Nehru was the first Chairperson of the Planning Commission. It was a non-constitutional body formed for assessing the country’s resources and developing plans for their effective and balanced utilization. Some key tasks includes: Formulation of Five-Year Plans, Resource Allocation, Continuous Evaluation, Policy Advisory.

q_en: Failure of Third Plan that of the devaluation of rupee (to boost exports) along with inflationary recession led to postponement of Fourth FYP and therefore _________ Annual Plans were introduced instead.
e_en: The correct answer is three. After the failure of the Third Plan, the Fourth Five-Year Plan was postponed, and instead, three Rolling Annual Plans were introduced. These were introduced from 1966 to 1969 to address the economic challenges during that period. Rolling Plans often emphasize immediate or short-term objectives while keeping long-term goals in view.

q_en: As per 2011 Census Hindus form 79.80% with a population of __________.
e_en: The correct answer is over 90 crores. As per the 2011 Census of India, the population of India was approximately 1.21 billion (1,210 million) out of which 79.80% form Hindus.

q_en: Who has written the book 'The philosophy of the bomb?'
e_en: The correct answer is Bhagwati Charan Vohra. Bhagwati Charan Vohra, a prominent member of the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA), wrote "The Philosophy of the Bomb" in 1929. It was written to defend the revolutionary methods adopted by Bhagat Singh and others, especially after the public debates following the bombing of the Central Legislative Assembly by Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt.

q_en: In which year did Abhinav Bindra create history by becoming the first Indian to win an individual gold medal at the Olympic Games in the 10-meter Air Rifle event?
e_en: The correct answer is 2008. Abhinav Bindra is a distinguished player in shooting games. Abhinav Bindra made history in Beijing 2008 Olympics by becoming the first Indian to win an individual gold medal. He is the first Indian to have held concurrently the world and Olympic titles for the men's 10-meter air rifle event, having earned those honors at the 2008 Summer Olympics. Abhinav Bindra has also won seven medals at the Commonwealth Games and three medals at the Asian Games.

q_en:
Read the following about Revenue Receipts.
A. Revenue receipts are those receipts that do not lead to a claim on the government.
B. Revenue receipts are divided into tax and non-tax revenues.
Identify the CORRECT statement/statements.
e_en: The correct answer is Both A and B. There is a constitutional requirement in India (Article 112) to present before the Parliament a statement of estimated receipts and expenditures of the government in respect of every financial year which runs from 1 April to 31 March. This ‘Annual Financial Statement’ constitutes the main budget document. Therefore, the budget comprises of the-Revenue Budget and the Capital Budget.

e_en: The correct answer is West Bengal. Gambhira, D

q_en: Shiv Kumar Sharma's name is synonymous with _____ Indian classical music instrument.
e_en: The correct answer is Santoor. Pandit Shivkumar Sharma (13 January 1938 – 10 May 2022) was an Indian classical musician and santoor player who is credited with adapting the santoor for Indian classical music. As a music composer, he collaborated with Indian flautist Hariprasad Chaurasia under the collaborative name Shiv–Hari and composed music for many Indian films.

q_en: The term "CRR" in the context of Indian banking stands for:
e_en: The correct answer is Cash Reserve Ratio. The Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) is the amount of money banks have to keep with the Reserve Bank of India as liquid cash. It's a way for the RBI to ensure banks have enough cash in hand. CRR is used by the RBI to control liquidity in the banking system. By adjusting the CRR, the RBI can influence the amount of money available for lending, thereby controlling inflation and stabilizing the economy.

q_en: In _________, the All India Kabaddi Federation came into existence and compiled standard rules.
e_en: The correct answer is 1950. The All-India Kabaddi Federation was established in 1950. It aimed to promote and organize Kabaddi at a national level. The federation started organizing national-level competitions, including the Senior National Championship from 1952. The federation compiled and standardized the rules of Kabaddi.

q_en: The unemployment rate is calculated as the ratio of:
o_en: Employed workers to the labour force
Unemployed workers to the labour force
Total population to the labour force
Unemployed workers to the total population
e_en: The correct answer is Unemployed workers to the labour force. q_en: Who was founder of the Agra Gharana?
e_en: The correct answer is Khuda Baksh. Khuda Baksh was a prominent musician and the founder of the Agra Gharana. The Agra Gharana is one of the main vocal styles or 'gharanas' of Hindustani classical music. Khuda Baksh's style emphasized the use of powerful and robust vocal techniques. The Agra Gharana evolved from the 'Dhrupad' tradition and later incorporated elements of 'Khayal' singing.

q_en: Pasumarthy Ramalinga Sastry is associated with which of the following dance style?
e_en: The correct answer is Kuchipudi. Pasumarthy Ramalinga Sastry is a renowned figure associated with the Kuchipudi dance style. He comes from a long line of traditional Kuchipudi gurus and has been instrumental in preserving and promoting this classical dance form. Kuchipudi is a classical dance form from Andhra Pradesh, known for its graceful movements, dramatic expressions, and unique style of storytelling through dance.

q_en: Jawara dance is a popular folk dance of _________.
e_en: The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh. Jawara dance is a popular folk dance of Madhya Pradesh. It is mainly performed in the Bundelkhand region of the state. The dance celebrates a good harvest, symbolizing joy and prosperity among the farming communities. Participants perform this dance with baskets full of crops, primarily jawara (barley), on their heads. The lively music and rhythmic movements express the happiness of the farmers after a successful harvest.

q_en: The languages spoken in Jharkhand and parts of central India mainly belong to which of the following language family?
e_en: The correct answer is Austro-Asiatic family. The languages spoken in Jharkhand and parts of central India, especially among tribal communities, mainly belong to the Austro-Asiatic language family. Munda languages, such as Santali, Mundari, and Ho, are part of this family and are widely spoken in these regions. These languages have ancient roots and are primarily spoken by indigenous and tribal populations.

q_en: On 8 April, 1929, Bhagat Singh and B.K. Dutt threw a bomb in the ____ The aim of the event as their leaflet explained, was not to kill but "to make the deaf hear".
e_en: The correct answer is Central Legislative Assembly. On 8 April 1929, Bhagat Singh and B.K. Dutt threw a bomb in the Central Legislative Assembly in Delhi. The act was intended to protest the Public Safety Bill passed by the British government in 1928. Their revolutionary group was the Hindustan Republican Socialist Association (HRSA), which sought to gain publicity for their cause.

q_en: Which sport is played by the Indian sportsperson Sandeep Kumar?
e_en: The correct answer is Archery. Sandeep Kumar is an Indian archer. He competed in the men's compound archery team event. He won the gold medal at the 2014 Asian Games in Incheon, South Korea. He was awarded the prestigious Arjuna Award in 2015.

q_en: Which of the following festival is celebrated by Khamtis tribe of Arunachal Pradesh?
e_en: The correct answer is Sangken. Sangken is a water festival celebrated by the Khamti tribe of Arunachal Pradesh. It marks the traditional New Year for the Khamti and is also observed by other Tai ethnic groups in Northeast India. The festival involves the ceremonial bathing of Buddha statues and sprinkling water on each other as a sign of purification and goodwill.

q_en: What is the rank of India in terms of the World's area among the countries of the world?
e_en: The correct answer is 7th. India is the 7th largest country in the world by land area. It covers an area of approximately 3.287 million square kilometers. The six countries ahead of India in terms of area are Russia, Canada, the United States, China, Brazil, and Australia. India occupies about 2.4% of the total geographical area of the world. The country’s vast area includes diverse landscapes, such as mountains, plains, deserts, and coastal regions.

q_en: The Attorney-General for India shall hold office during the pleasure of the ____.
e_en: The correct answer is President of India. The Attorney-General for India shall hold office during the pleasure of the President. The term of office is not fixed by the Constitution of India (COI). The Attorney-General may be removed by the President at any time. The Attorney General of India is appointed by the President of India.

q_en: Varahamihira's work Panchasiddhantika deals with ___ astronomical systems.
e_en: The correct answer is Five. Varahamihira's work Panchasiddhantika discusses five astronomical systems. The term Panchasiddhantika translates to "The Five Astronomical Systems." This work synthesizes knowledge from earlier astronomical texts and systems. Varahamihira was a prominent Indian astronomer and mathematician of the 6th century CE. The five systems included are the Surya Siddhanta, Romaka Siddhanta, Paulisha Siddhanta, Garga Siddhanta, and Vashishta Siddhanta.

q_en: Which sport is the Durand cup is associated with?
e_en: The correct answer is Football. Durand Cup: The Durand Cup is one of the oldest football tournaments in India, established in 1888. Significance: It is named after Sir Henry Mortimer Durand, who was the British Deputy Commissioner of Bengal and initiated the tournament to foster goodwill between the Indian and British communities. Teams: The tournament features clubs from various states, including top teams from the Indian Super League (ISL) and the I-League.

q_en: ____, which belongs to Kerala in southern India, takes its name from the mythic enchantress Mohini.
e_en: The correct answer is Mohiniattam. Mohiniyattam is a classical dance form from Kerala, South India. The name Mohiniyattam comes from the mythic enchantress Mohini, who was the female form taken by Lord Vishnu. The dance form reflects the graceful and sensuous movements of Mohini, the enchantress from Hindu mythology. Mohiniyattam literally means "dance of the enchantress."

q_en: In India, "APEDA" is related to which of the following?
e_en: The correct answer is Agriculture. APEDA stands for the Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority. The Government of India established it to promote the export of agricultural and processed food products. APEDA is responsible for providing financial assistance, conducting training, and helping with the development of agricultural export standards. It plays a significant role in enhancing the global reach of Indian agricultural produce.

q_en: ________ is the first Indian dancer, a transgender, to be honoured with Padma Shri.
e_en: The correct answer is Narthaki Nataraj. Narthaki Nataraj is the first Indian dancer from the transgender community to be honored with the Padma Shri. She is renowned for her expertise in Bharatanatyam, specifically the Tanjore style. Narthaki has broken significant barriers, becoming a trailblazer for the transgender community in the field of classical dance. She has performed globally and has been recognized for her contributions to Indian classical dance and culture.

q_en: What was India's literacy rate at the time of independence in 1947?
e_en: The correct answer is 12%. When the British rule ended in India in the year 1947, the literacy rate was just around 12%. The British rule in India refers to the period during which the Indian Subcontinent was under the colonial rule of the British Empire. It began in 1757, following the Battle of Plassey, and continued until India gained independence on August 15, 1947.

q_en: Which sport is the Wimbledon trophy associated with?
e_en: The correct answer is Lawn Tennis. The Wimbledon Championships, commonly known simply as Wimbledon, is the oldest lawn tennis tournament in the world. It is held every year at All England Lawn Tennis and Croquet Club in Wimbledon, London, the United Kingdom. The All England Lawn Tennis and Croquet Club is a private club founded on 23 July 1868, originally as "The All England Croquet Club". In 1877, the club was renamed "The All England Croquet and Lawn Tennis Club".

q_en: The Constituent Assembly of India was set up in which year?
e_en: The correct answer is 1946. The Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946 first proposed the constituent assembly. Members of the Constituent Assembly were elected by the Provincial Legislative Assemblies. It held its first meeting on December 9, 1946, and reassembled on August 14, 1947, as the sovereign Constituent Ass

q_en: Gautama Buddha decided to find his own path to realisation, and meditated for days on end under a ________ tree at Bodh Gaya in Bihar.
e_en: The correct answer is Peepal. Gautama Buddha meditated under a Bodhi tree (Ficus religiosa), also known as Peepal, which is now a sacred symbol in Buddhism. This event took place at Bodh Gaya, located in the state of Bihar, India. Under this tree, Buddha attained enlightenment or nirvana, which marked a key turning point in his spiritual journey. Buddha meditated for days on end, showing his commitment to finding the path to self-realization and truth.

q_en: The spring festival of Holi is celebrated as Yaoshang by the Meitei tribe in the state of ________, lasting about six days.
e_en: The correct answer is Manipur. Yaoshang lasts for about six days, typically coinciding with the full moon of the Lai Haraoba month, which falls in March, marking the arrival of spring. The festival celebrates the arrival of spring and is deeply rooted in the agricultural traditions of the Meitei tribe, symbolizing new beginnings and prosperity.

q_en: Which of the following Acts allowed detention of political prisoners without trial for two years?
e_en: The correct answer is Rowalatt Act. The Rowlatt Act, officially known as the Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act of 1919. The primary purpose of the Rowlatt Act was to curb revolutionary activities and suppress political dissent in India. It allowed for detention without trial for up to two years. During the enactment of the Rowlatt Act in 1919, the Governor-General of India was Lord Chelmsford.

q_en: Who was the renowned Indian Carnatic singer and the first artist to receive both the Bharat Ratna and the Ramon Magsaysay Award?
e_en: The correct answer is MS Subbulakshmi. The renowned Indian Carnatic singer who was the first artist to receive both the Bharat Ratna and the Ramon Magsaysay Award is M. S. Subbulakshmi. Born on September 16, 1916, in Madurai, Tamil Nadu, India. She was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1998, which is India's highest civilian award. She received the Ramon Magsaysay Award for her contribution to the arts in 1974.

q_en: Article 163 of the Indian Constitution is related to which of the following?
o_en: Conduct of Business of the Government of a State
Council of Ministers to aid and advise Governor
e_en: The correct answer is Council of Ministers to aid and advise Governor. Article 74: Council of Ministers to Aid and Advise the President. Article 76: Attorney General for India Article 77: Conduct of Business of the Government of India. Article 78: Duties of Prime Minister as a Head of the Government.

q_en: Every year the Flamingo festival is celebrated at the Pulicat Lake near the Nellapattu Bird Sanctuary located in _________.
e_en: The correct answer is Andhra Pradesh. The Flamingo Festival is a significant event celebrated in India, particularly in the state of Andhra Pradesh. The Flamingo Festival is primarily celebrated at Pulicat Lake, which is located near the border of Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu. The festival is primarily focused on the Greater Flamingo (Phoenicopterus roseus) and the Lesser Flamingo (Phoenicopterus minor).

q_en:
Read the following about the impact of Green Revolution in India.
A. India became self-sufficient in food-grains and had sufficient stock in the central pool, even, at times, India was in a position to export food-grains.
B. The per capita net availability of food-grains has also increased.
Identify the CORRECT statement/statements.
e_en: The correct answer is Both A and B. The Green Revolution refers to a period of agricultural transformation that occurred in the 1960s and 1970s. High-Yielding Varieties (HYVs) Developed through selective breeding and hybridization. Increased use of chemical fertilizers, particularly nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), and potassium (K). The Father of the Green Revolution in India is Dr. M. S. Swaminathan.

q_en: Which measure captures the difference between the government's total expenditure and total receipts, excluding borrowing?
e_en: The correct answer is Fiscal Deficit. The measure that captures the difference between the government's total expenditure and total receipts, excluding borrowing, is known as the Fiscal Deficit. Fiscal deficit occurs when a government's total expenditures exceed its total revenues (excluding borrowing). Fiscal Deficit=Total Expenditure−Total Receipts (excluding borrowing).

q_en: In table tennis, a serve that hits the net but still goes over and lands in the opponent's service area is called a:

The game uses a lightweight plastic ball with a diameter of 40 mm, weighing 2.7 grams. Players use paddles (also known as bats or rackets) made of wood covered with rubber on one or both sides. Table tennis became an Olympic sport in 1988.

q_en: Ghoomar dance is associated with which of the following states?
e_en: The correct answer is Ghoomar. Ghoomar is a traditional folk dance of state of Rajasthan. The name Ghoomar is derived from the word ghoomna, which means spinning or twirling. Ghoomar is performed on traditional Rajasthani folk music, with its rhythmic beats. Common instruments include: the Dhol (drum), Nagada, Shehnai, and Harmonium. It is performed on occasions such as weddings, festivals like Teej, Gangaur, and Diwali, as well as other celebrations.

q_en: In which Indian state is Kambala, the traditional buffalo race, conducted during the winter months to celebrate the harvest season?
e_en: The correct answer is Karnatka Kambala is an annual buffalo race held in the southwestern Indian state of Karnataka. Traditionally, it is sponsored by local Tuluva landlords and households in the coastal districts of Dakshina Kannada and Udupi of Karnataka, and Kasaragod of Kerala, a region collectively known as Tulu Nadu.

q_en: Brahmotsavam festival is historically native to which of the following states?
e_en: The correct answer is Andhra Pradesh Brahmotsavam festival Brahmotsavam, the Hindu festival is an auspicious festival celebrated every year at the Tirumala Venkateswara Temple at Tirupati in Andhra Pradesh. According to legends the origin of this festival is associated with Lord Brahma. The importance of this festival can be known by the fact that every year thousands of devotees flock in Andhra Pradesh to be the witness of this majestic festival.

q_en: Who wrote the original handwritten version of the Indian Constitution?
e_en: The correct answer is Nandalal Bose. The original handwritten version of the Indian Constitution was Prem Behari Narain Raizada Each page had some artwork and the calligraphy in Hindi and English was done by Prem Behari Narain Raizada. The Constitution was published in Dehradun and photo lithographed by the Survey of India. It is preserved in a helium-filled case in Parliament. Artist Nandlal Bose led the initiative to add art on the pages of India's Constitution.

q_en: The concept of "judicial review" in India allows the judiciary to review and strike down laws that are found to be:
o_en: Supported by a two-thirds majority in the State Legislature
e_en: The correct answer is In violation of fundamental rights The concept of "judicial review" in India allows the judiciary (mainly the Supreme Court and High Courts) to review laws and executive actions to ensure that they comply with the Constitution of India. If a law is found to violate the Fundamental Rights guaranteed under the Constitution or go beyond the constitutional provisions, the judiciary can declare it unconstitutional or invalid.

q_en: After the first five-year Plan of India, two subsequent five-year plans were formulated till ___
e_en: The correct answer is 1966 After India's First Five-Year Plan (1951-1956), two subsequent Five-Year Plans were formulated till 1966. After India's independence in 1947, the government adopted a planned economic development approach to promote growth across sectors. The Planning Commission was established in 1950 to oversee this, and the country launched its first Five-Year Plan in 1951.

q_en: In Football a direct ____ is awarded if a player commits any of the following offences against an opponent in a manner considered by the referee to be careless, reckless or using excessive force:
e_en: The correct answer is free-kick In football, a direct free kick is awarded if a player commits any of the following offences against an opponent in a manner considered by the referee to be careless, reckless, or using excessive force. These offences include actions like kicking, tripping, pushing, or striking an opponent. A free kick is an important concept in football. It is awarded when a player commits a foul or infringement.

q_en: Sonal Mansingh is mainly associated with which dance style?
e_en: The correct answer is Bharatnatyam and Odissi. Sonal Mansingh is a prominent Indian classical dancer who specializes in Bharatanatyam and Odissi. For her contributions to promoting ‘Classical dances’, she has received accolades from many national and international organizations. She was the youngest recipient of Padma Bhushan in 1992. In 2003, Sonal became the first Indian woman dancer to be awarded Padma Vibhushan.

Which of the following statements regarding money is correct?
I. Money supply is a stock variable.
II. The total stock of money in circulation among the public at a particular point of time is called money supply.
e_en: The correct answer is Both I and II Money supply is a stock variable. This statement is correct because the money supply represents the total amount of money available in the economy at a specific point in time. Stock variables are measured at a particular moment, distinguishing them from flow variables, which are measured over a period of time (like income or expenditure).

q_en: In which year was the first War of Independence taken place in India?
e_en: The correct answer is 1857 The First War of Independence in India took place in 1857, marking a significant uprising against British rule In 1857, a great struggle took place in India which completely shook the British Government. This struggle did not arise all of a sudden. Earlier as well many such struggles took place in India against the British.

q_en: Into how many ages is the prehistoric times in terms of technology divided?
e_en: The correct answer is Three Prehistoric times are typically divided into three ages in terms of technology: Stone Age: This is the earliest period of human technology, characterized by the use of stone tools. It is further divided into: Paleolithic (Old Stone Age): It is Marked by the use of simple stone tools and the development of hunter-gatherer societies.

q_en: According to the 2011 Census of India, among the State/ UTs, the male and female literacy rate is highest in ____.
e_en: The correct answer is kerala Literacy level and educational attainment are vital developmental indicators in a developing nation like India as they are key variables of measure of development as they indicate the quality of life, awareness level, and also the level of skill of people in the society. The female literacy rate of India as per the 2011 census is 65.5%. The literacy rate at all Indian levels is 74% and the male literacy rate is 82.1%.

e_en: The correct answer is Both 1 and 2 Both pairs of sports persons and their associated sports are correct: Manu Bhaker - Shooting Manu Bhaker is a prominent Indian shooter who has made significant a

q_en: Renowned violinist ____ trained in Carnatic music as well as Western classical music.
e_en: The correct answer is Lakshminarayana Subramaniam Dr. L. Subramaniam He is a reputed Tamil violinist, and composer. He has extensive training in Carnatic and Western classical music and made his mark in fusion orchestral music compositions. He was born into a Tamil family of established musicians. His father V.Lakshminarayana and his mother V.Seethalakshmi have accomplished musicians of their time.

q_en: Which dance style was kept alive by the Devadasis?
e_en: The correct answer is Bharatnatyam The Devadasis, a community of dancers in South India, are credited with originating the popular dance form of Bharatanatyam. Devadasis were women who dedicated their lives to temples, learning classical Indian dances, and performing at temple rituals They were also known by various local terms, such as Basivi in Karnataka, Matangi in Maharashtra, and Kalavantin in Goa and Damaon. Bharatanatyam was originally known as Sadir or Dasi Attam.

q_en: Which sport is played by the Indian sportsperson Sania Mirza?
e_en: The correct answer is Lawn Tennis Former Wimbledon doubles champion Tennis player Sania Mirza has announced that she will retire from tennis after 2022. She became the first Indian to win a WTA singles title in 2005. She has also won two Grand Slam titles with Mahesh Bhupathi - the 2009 Australian Open mixed doubles title and the French Open 2012 mixed doubles. She also won the US and Australian Opens.

q_en: According to the Indian Constitution, how many organs are there in the government of India?
e_en: The correct answer is Three. According to the Constitution of India, there are three organs of government. These are the legislature, the executive, and the judiciary. The legislature refers to our elected representatives. The executive is a smaller group of people who are responsible for implementing laws and running the government. The judiciary refers to the system of courts in this country.

q_en: Independence Day is celebrated at the national level at _______ in Delhi.
e_en: The correct answer is Red Fort. The Red Fort was constructed by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan in 1638 as part of his new capital, Shahjahanabad (now Old Delhi). The fort is built in red sandstone and is a fine example of Mughal architecture, blending Persian, Timurid, and Indian styles.
