q_en: The marked price of an article is Rs. 250. It is sold for Rs. 164.70 after giving three successive discounts of 20%, 10% and x% on the marked price. What is the value of x?
e_en: Calculation: Selling price of 20% discount = 0.8 × Rs 250 = Rs 200 Selling price of 10% discount = 0.9 × Rs 200 = Rs 180 Total discount given = Rs 180 - Rs 164.70 = Rs 15.3 Discount % = 15.3over180 × 100 = 8.5.% ∴ The value of x is 8.5%.

q_en: When x is added to each of the numbers 11, 18, 27, 42, the numbers so obtained are in proportion. What is the mean proportional between (11x + 3) and (9x - 2)?
e_en: Formula: Mean proportional between a, b, and c ⇒ b² = ac Calculation: According to the question- ⇒ 11+xover18+x = 27+xover42+x ⇒ (11 + x) (42 + x) = (18 + x) (27 + x) ⇒ 462 + 11x + 42x + x² = 486 + 18x + 27x + x² ⇒ 53x - 45x = 486 - 462 ⇒ 8x = 24 ⇒ x = 3 The numbers for the mean proportion ⇒ (11 × 3 + 3) and (9 × 3 - 2) ⇒ 36 and 25 Let the mean proportion be "m" ⇒ m²= 36 × 25 ⇒ m = 6 × 5 = 30 ∴ The mean proportion for the numbers is 30.

q_en: A and B started simultaneously and proceeded towards each other from places X and Y, respectively. After meeting each other at a certain point on the way, A and B took 3.2 hours and 1.8 hours, to reach Y and X, respectively. If the speed of B was 12 km/h, then the speed (in km/h) of A was:
e_en: Formula: D = S × T, where D = Distance S = Speed T = Time Calculation: Let the S₁ and S₂ be the speed of A and B respectively and T₁ and T₂ be the time taken to complete the distance after the meeting point. ⇒ S₁over S₂ = sqrt {T₂over T₁} Substituting the values respectively- ⇒ S₁over 12 = sqrt {1.8over 3.2} ⇒ S₁ = 12 × 3over4 = 9 km/hr The speed of A is 9 km/hr.

q_en: If 15% of A is equal to 45% of B, then what percentage of A - B is A?
e_en: Calculation: Let 15over100 × A = 45/100 × B = k ∴ A = 100kover15 and B = 100kover45 According to the question- ⇒ A - B = 100kover15 - 100kover45 = 300k -100kover45 = 200kover45 A% = {100kover15}over{200kover45} × 100 = 100kover15 × 45over200k × 100 = 150% ∴ The answer is 150%.

q_en: A, B and C are three numbers. A is 20% more than B, and C is 20% less than the sum of A and B. The difference between C and B is what per cent less than A (correct to one decimal place)?
e_en: Calculation: Let the number B be 100. ⇒ A = 1.2 × 100 = 120 ⇒ C = 0.8 × (100 + 120) = 0.8 × 220 = 176 Difference between B and C = 176 - 100 = 76 Difference of C and B less than A = 120 - 76 = 44 Difference percentage = 44over120 × 100 = 36.7% ∴ The answer is 36.7%.

q_en: A man borrowed ₹50,000 for 2 years at a rate of 2% on compound interest. The difference in the amount at the end of the first year and that at the end of the second year is:

q_en: A sum of Rs. 15,500 amounts to Rs. 19,189 in 3 1/2 years at a certain rate per cent per annum, at simple interest. The simple interest on the same sum at the same rate for 6 2/3 years will be (nearest to a Rs.):
e_en: Given: Principal = Rs.15500 Amount = Rs.19189 Time = 7/2 years Formula used: SI = (P × R × T)/100 Rate = I(one year)/P Calculation: A = P + 7/2 × I ⇒ 15500 + 7/2 × I = 19189 ⇒ 7/2 × I = 3689 I(one year) = 1054 Rate = I/P × 100 ⇒ 1054/15500 × 100 ⇒ 6.8% SI = (P × R × T)/100 ⇒ (15500 × 6.8 × 20)/(3 × 100) ⇒ (155 × 68 × 2)/3 ⇒ 7026.66 = 7027(nearest) ∴ The correct answer is Rs.7027.

q_en: If the sides of a rectangle, whose area is 154 cm², differ by 3 cm, then find the length (in cm) of the longer side.
e_en: Given: Area = 154 cm² L(Length) - B(Breadth) = 3 cm Formula used: Area of Rectangle = L × B Calculation: L - B = 3 cm (Given) ⇒ L = B + 3 ⇒ 154 = B × (B + 3) ⇒ B² + 3B - 154 = 0 ⇒ B² + 14B - 11B - 154 = 0 ⇒ B(B + 14) - 11(B + 14) = 0 ⇒ (B + 14) (B - 11) = 0 ⇒ B = -14 ,11(Correct value) ⇒ L = 11 + 3 ⇒ L = 14 cm ∴ The correct answer is 14 cm.

q_en: When a number is divided by 3, 4, 6, 15 and 20, the remainder in each case is 1. Also, the number is the greatest 3-digit number. The sum of the digits of the number is:

The greatest number of 3-digits = 999 ⇒ 999 ÷ 60 Reminder = 39 3-digit greatest numbers = 999 - 39 = 960 When a number is divided by 3, 4, 6, 15, and 20, the remainder in each case is 1. q_en: I walk at a speed of 10 km/h and cover a distance in 2 hours. If I increase my speed by 5 km/h, how early would I reach my destination?
e_en: Given: Walking speed = 10 km/h Covered distance = 2 hours If walking speed increased by 5 km/h. Formula: Distance = Speed × Time Calculation: Total distance = 10 × 2 = 20 km Now, Speed after increased by 5 = 10 + 5 = 15 km/h So, new time to cover the same distance ⇒ (20\15) × 60 = 80 minutes So, time will be deducted = 120 - 80 = 40 minutes. ∴ I would reach my destination 40 minutes early.

q_en: A wheel makes 1000 revolutions in covering a distance of 44 km. Find the radius of the wheel.

Calculation: According to the question, ⇒ 2πr × 1000 = 44000 ⇒ 2πr = 44 ​⇒ 2 × 22/7 × r = 44 ⇒ 44/7 × r = 44 ​⇒ r = 7m ∴ The radius of the wheel is 7 m. 1a

q_en: Rakhi offers a discount of 30% on all the items at her shop and still makes a profit of 12%. What is the cost price (in ₹) of an article marked at ₹280?

q_en: 75 workers could complete only one-third of a work in 20 days. It is desired that the work be finished in the next 30 days. How many more workers should be taken to complete the work in the desired time?

Formula used: SP = CP × (100 - L%)/100 SP = CP × (100 + P%)/100 Calculation: Let CP be Rs. x When loss is 15% then, SP = (100 - 15)x/100 = 85x/100 ⇒ SP = 17x/20 When Profit is 5% then, SP = (100 + 5)x/100 = 105x/100 ⇒ SP = 21x/20 According to the question, 21x/20 - 17x/20 = 150 ⇒ 4x/20 = 150 ⇒ x = 750 Hence the CP is Rs. 750.

q_en: 45% of the total candidates who appeared for an examination were girls. 75% of the boys and 80% of the girls passed, and 144 girls failed. How many boys failed?
e_en: Given: Girls = 45% Boys passed = 75% Girls passed = 80% Girls failed = 144 Calculation: Let total students = 400 Girls = 45% = 45/100 × 400 = 180 Boys = 55% = 55/100 × 400 = 220 Boys passed = 75% = 3/4 × 220 = 165 Boys failed = 220 - 165 = 55 Girls passed = 80% = 4/5 × 180 = 144 Girls failed = 180 - 144 = 36 ⇒ 36 units = 144 (According to question) ⇒ 1 unit = 4 Boys failed = 55 × 4 = 220 ∴ The correct answer is 220.

q_en: A salesman sells an item at a profit of 21%. If he had bought it at 12% less and sold it for Rs. 66 less, he would have gained 30%. Find the cost price of the item.

q_en: If the simple interest charged for 9 months be 0.12 times the money borrowed, what is the rate percent per year?
e_en: Given: Time = 9 months SI = 0.12 × Principle Formula Used: SI = (P × R × T)/100 Calculation: 1 year = 12 months ⇒ 1 month = 1/12 years ⇒ 9 months = 9/12 years According to the question, SI = 0.12 × P SI = (P × R × T)/100 ⇒ P × 0.12 = (P × 9 × R)/(12 × 100) ⇒ R = (0.12 × 100 × 12)/9 ⇒ R = 16% ∴ The rate of interest is 16%.

q_en: If the ratio of three numbers A, B and C is 2 ∶ 3 ∶ 5, and the sum of the squares of these numbers is 3800, then the value of C is:

e_en: Given: Anuj completed a double century = 200 Runs Total number of sixes = 15 Total number of four = 18 Calculation: Total runs by sixes = 15 × 6 = 90 Total runs by four = 18 × 4 = 72 Total runs by sixes and fours = 90 + 72 = 162 runs Runs made by Anuj running between the wickets = 200 - 162 = 38 Percentage of runs made by Anuj running between the wickets ⇒ 38/200 × 100 = 19% ∴ 19% of runs were made by Anuj running between the wickets.

q_en: An article is marked 60% above its cost price. If a profit of 20% is made by selling the article, then what is the discount percentage offered on its marked price?
e_en: Given: MP is 60% above its CP Profit is 20% Formula used: 1. MP = CP × (100 + Increase%)/100 2. SP = CP × (100 + Profit%)/100 3. Discount% = [(MP - SP)/MP] × 100 Calculation: Let CP of an article be 100 ⇒ MP = 100 × (100 + 60)/100 = 160 According to the question, SP = 100 × (100 + 20)/100 = 120 ⇒ Discount% = [(160 - 120)/160] × 100 ⇒ Discount% = (40/160) × 100 ⇒ Discount% = 25% ∴ The discount percentage is 25%.

q_en: If the perimeter of a rectangle is 50 cm and its diagonal is 23 cm long, then what is the area of the rectangle?
e_en: Given: Perimeter = 50 cm Diagonal = 23 cm Formula used: Perimeter of rectangle = 2 (l + b) (Diagonal of rectangle)² = l2 + b2 Calculation: Let the length of rectangle be l And the breadth of rectangle is b. Then, Diagonal of rectangle = l2 + b2 = (23)² ⇒ l2 + b2 = 529 Perimeter of rectangle = 2 (l + b) = 50 ⇒ (l + b) = 25 ⇒ (l + b)² = 625 ⇒ l² + b²+ 2lb = 625 ⇒ 2lb = 625 - 529 ⇒2lb = 96 ⇒ l × b = 48 cm² ∴ The area of rectangle is 48 cm²

e_en: Given:- A completes a task in 18 days B completes a task in 27 days C completes a task in 36 days Concept Used: Total Work = Efficiency × Time Calculation: Let the work be finished in x days Let total work be 108 units (LCM of 18, 27,36) ⇒ Efficiency of A = 108/18 = 6 units ⇒ Efficiency of B = 108/27 = 4 units ⇒ Efficiency of C = 108/36 = 3 units According to the question, ⇒ 6(x - 4) + 4(x - 6) + 3x = 108 ⇒ 6x + 4x + 3x - 48 = 108 ⇒ 13x = 156 ⇒ x = 12 days B leaves 6 days bef…

q_en: The LCM of two numbers is 12 times their HCF. If one of the numbers is 15 and the sum of the HCF and LCM is 65, then find the other number.
e_en: Given: LCM = 12 × HCF LCM + HCF = 65 Number₁ = 15 Formula Used: LCM × HCF = N₁ × N₂ Calculation: 12 × HCF + HCF = 65 ⇒ 13 × HCF = 65 ⇒ HCF = 5 ⇒ LCM = 12 × 5 = 60 According to the question, ⇒ 60 × 5 = 15 × N₂ ⇒ N₂ = 300/15 = 20 ∴ The other number is 20.

q_en: If 45% of a number is equal to two-third of another number, what is the ratio of the first number to the second number?

q_en: The simple interest on a certain sum of money at the rate of 7.5% p.a. for 8 years is Rs. 4,080. At what rate of interest can the same amount of interest be received on the same sum for 5 years?
e_en: Given: Simple Interest (SI) = 4080, Time (T) = 8 Year, Rate (r1) = 7.5% Formula Used: Simple Interest (SI) = PRT/ 100 Where, SI = Simple Interest, P = Principal, T = Time, R = Rate Calculation: According to the question, The same amount of interest be received on the same sum for 5 years then, ⇒ 4080 = P × 7.5 × 8/100 ⇒ P = Rs 6800 Now, New Time (T) = 5 Years and same interest and sum Then, R = (SI × 100) / PT ⇒ R = (4080 × 100) / 6800 × 5 ⇒ R = 12% Hence, Rate (R) = 12%

q_en: A sum was put at simple interest at a certain rate for 2 years. If it had been put at 4% higher rate, it would have fetched Rs. 480 more. Find the sum.
e_en: Given: Time (T) = 2 Year, Increasing Rate (r1) = 4% , Increasing Interest (SI1) = Rs 480 Formula Used: Simple Interest (SI) = PRT/ 100 Where, SI = Simple Interest, P = Principal, T = Time, R = Rate Calculation: According to the question, Rate is higher than 4% then, ⇒ PRT/100 + 480 = P(R+4)T/100 Simplify this equation ⇒ PRT/100 + 480 = PRT/100 + 4PT/100 ⇒ 4PT = 48000 ⇒ 4 × 2P = 48000 ⇒ P = Rs 6000 Hence, Sum = Rs 6000

q_en: In an election between two candidates, 8% of the votes were invalid. The winning candidate got 60% of the total valid votes and won the election by 5888 votes. How many voters were registered?
e_en: Given: 8% of the votes are invalid Winner got 60% of the valid votes Winners won by 5888 votes Calculation: Let the total numbers of voters be 100a Valid votes = 100a - 100a × 8% ⇒ 92a Winning candidate got 92a × 60% ⇒ 55.2a So, loosing candidate got = 92a - 55.2a ⇒ 36.8a According to the question, 55.2a - 36.8a = 5888 ⇒ 18.4a = 5888 ⇒ a = 5888/18.4 ⇒ a = 320 So, total voters registered = 320 × 100 ⇒ 32000 ∴ 32000 voters were registered.

q_en: What is the largest 4-digit number that is divisible by 10, 15 and 18?
e_en: Given: The number are 10, 15, and 18 Concept used: We know that, If the number is divisible by given numbers then it should be the multiple of their LCM Calculation: LCM of 10, 15, and 18 = 90 Now the largest 4-digit number is 9999 If we divide 9999 by 90 we get the remainder as 9 The number completely divisible by 10, 15, and 18 = 9999 - 9 ⇒ 9990 ∴ The largest 4-digit number that is divisible by each of 10, 15, and 18 is 9990.

q_en: An AC can cool a hall in 10 min, while an AC of another brand can cool the same hall in 15 min. If both the ACs are switched on at the same time, then in how much time will they cool the hall?
e_en: Given: 1st AC can cool in 10 min 2nd AC can cool in 15 min Concept used: Total work = Time taken by the objects to do a work × efficiency of the objects Calculation: LCM of 10 and 15 = 30 i.e total work Now, Efficiency of the 1st AC = 30/10 = 3 units/min Efficiency of the 2nd AC = 30/15 = 2 units/min Effective efficiency of the two ACs = 3 + 2 = 5 units/min Time taken to cool the hall when two ACs are on together = 30/5 ⇒ 6 min ∴ They will cool the hall in 6 min.

q_en: A batsman in his 18th innings makes a score of 80 and thereby increasing his average by 4. What is his average after the 18th innings?
e_en: Given: Score of the 18th innings = 80 Average increased by 4 Concept used: Average = Sum of elements/Number of elements Calculation: Let his average after 17th innings be X Total runs after 18th innings = 17X + 80 According to the question, [(17X + 80)/18] = X + 4 ⇒ 17X + 80 = 18X + 72 ⇒ X = 8 So, average after 17th innings = 8 Now, After 18th innings his average = 8 + 4 ⇒ 12 ∴ His average after the 18th innings is 12.

q_en: A man sold 30 articles for Rs. 100 and gained 20%. The number of articles he bought for Rs. 100 was:
e_en: Given: Selling Price = Rs. 100 Profit = 20% Sold articles = 30 Formula used: P% = [(SP - CP)/CP] × 100 Calculation: SP of 30 articles =Rs. 100 SP of 1 article = 100/3 = 10/3 ⇒ 20 = [(10/3 - CP)/CP] × 100 ⇒ CP = 25/9 ∵ CP of 1 article = 25/9 ∴ Number of articles = [(100)/(25/9)] ∴ The number of articles = 36 Hence, 36 articles bought in Rs. 100

q_en: A money lender finds that due to a fall in the annual rate of interest from 10% to 8 3/4%, his year's income diminishes by Rs. 84.50. Find his capital.
e_en: Given: Initial Rate(R₁) = 10% Final Rate(R₂) = 8{3over4}% = {35over 4} % Formula used: Diminishing Income = (Ptimes R₁ times T)/(100) - (Ptimes R₂times T )/(100) Calculation: R₁ = 10% R₂ = 8{3over4} % = {35over 4} % The difference in Simple Interest = Rs. 84.50 Rightarrow(Ptimes R₁ times T)/(100) - (Ptimes R₂times T )/(100)=84.50 Rightarrow(Ptimes 10 times 1)/(100) - (Ptimes 8.75times 1 )/(100)=84.50 P = Rs. 6760 Hence, Capital is Rs. 6760.

q_en: What is the smallest number which when increased by 17 becomes exactly divisible by both 520 and 936?
e_en: Given: Two numbers are 52 and 936 Concept used: For this type of question we use LCM of the given number to calculate the required number Calculation: 520 = 2³ × 5 × 13 936 = 2³ × 3² × 13 LCM = 23 × 13 × 3² × 5 ⇒ 4680 So, required number = 4680 - 17 ⇒ 4663 ∴ Required number is 4663.

q_en: On selling an article for Rs. 984, Arun loses 18%. In order to gain 15%, he must sell it for:
e_en: Given: SP = Rs. 984 Loss occurred(L) = 18% Desired profit(P) = 15% Formula used: CP = SP/(100 - L%) x 100 Also, SP = CP x (100 + P%)/100 Calculation: CP = 984/(100 - 18) x 100 = Rs. 1200 Selling Price after 15% Profit SP = 1200 x (100 + 15)/100 = Rs.1380 Hence, SP is Rs.1380.

q_en: Find the unknown value of 'x' in the proportion (5x + 1) ∶ 3 = (x + 3) ∶ 7
e_en: Given: (5x + 1) : 3 = (x + 3) : 7 Formula used: a : b = c : d or a/b = c/d ⇒ ad = bc Calculation: ⇒ (5x + 1) : 3 = (x + 3) : 7 ⇒ (5x + 1)/3 = (x + 3)/7 ⇒ 7(5x + 1) = 3(x + 3) ⇒ 35x + 7 = 3x + 9 ⇒ 32x = 2 ⇒ x = 1/16 Hence, The value of x is 1/16.

e_en: Given: Cost of milk = 50/L Selling price of mixture = 60/L Concept used: Seeling price = Cost price + profit Profit% = (Profit/Cost price) × 100 Calculation: Let the quantity of the milk in the mixture be 3x So, the quantity of the water = 3x × (1/3) ⇒ x Total cost of the mixture = (3x × 50) + x × 0 [As water has no value in money] ⇒ 150x Now, Selling price = 60(3x + x) ⇒ 60 × 4x ; ⇒ 240x Profit = 240x - 150x ⇒ 90x Profit % = (90x/150x) × 100 ⇒ 60 ∴ His profit percentage is 6…

q_en: Jagat Singh sold an article for Rs. 6,000 and incurred a loss. Had he sold it for Rs. 7,400, his profit would have been 2/3 of the amount of loss that he incurred. At what price should he sell it to gain 25% profit?
e_en: Given: First Selling Price = Rs.6,000 Second Selling Price = Rs. 7,400 Profit of second Selling Price = 2/3 of Loss of the first SP Formula used: CP = SP - Profit CP = SP + Loss Also, SP = CP x (100 + P)/100 Calculation: Let Loss be 3x ⇒ Profit = 2x Now, according to the statement 6000 + 3x = 7400 - 2x ⇒ x = 280 ⇒ Profit = 2x = 560 ⇒ CP = 7400 - 560 = 6840 Now, SP for 25 % Profit = 6840 x (100 + 25)/100 ⇒ SP = 8550 ∴ To gain 25 % he should sell the article at 8550 Rs.

q_en: The ratio of three numbers is 3 ∶ 5 ∶ 4 and the sum of their squares is 11250. Find the sum of the numbers.
e_en: Calculation: The ratio of the three numbers are 3x : 5x : 4x Squire of these ratio = 9x² : 25x² : 16x² Sum of their squares = 50x² Value of 50x² = 11250 ⇒ x² = 11250 / 50 = 225 ⇒ x = 15 Sum of these numbers = 3x + 5x + 4x = 12x Sum of numbers = 12 × 15 = 180 ∴ The sum of the numbers is 180

q_en: Two candidates are contesting in an election. All votes are valid votes. A candidate who gets 38% of votes is rejected by 28,800 votes. The total number of votes polled is:
e_en: Given: A candidate who gets 38% of the votes is rejected by 28,800 votes. Calculation: Let the total votes polled be x. The number of votes the winner gets = 62% of x ⇒ 62xover100 Number of votes received by the lost candidates = 38% of x ⇒ 38xover100 Difference, 62xover100 - 38xover100 = 2,88,00 ⇒ 24xover100 = 2,88,00 ⇒ x = {2,88,00 times 100}over24 = 1,20,000 ∴ The total number of votes polled is 1,20,000.

q_en: After getting two successive discounts, Seema got a shirt at Rs. 153, for which the marked price was Rs. 200. If the second discount was 15%, the first discount was:
e_en: Given: Cost price = 153 Rs. MRP = 200 Rs. Second Discount(D2) = 15% First Discount(D%) = ? Formula used: CP = MRP× {(100-D₁)over100}×{(100-D₂)over100} D% = D×100over MRP Calculation: Let the price after the first discount = X ⇒ X × (100-15)over100 = 153 ⇒ X × 85over100 = 153 ⇒ X = 153×100over85 ⇒ X = 180 ⇒ 180 is the price after the first discount of Rs. 200 is the original discount.

q_en: The HCF of 552, 759, and 828 is x. The value of x lies between:

q_en: Ram bought a chair at 35% discount on its market price, Had Ram got no discount, he would have had to pay ₹245 more. How much did Ram pay for the chair?
e_en: Given: Ram bought a chair at a 35% discount on its market price. Had Ram got no discount, he would have had to pay ₹245 more. Concept used: Selling price = Marked Price - Marked Price × Discount% Selling price = Marked price - Discount Calculation: Let the market price of the chair be M. Discount = M × 35% = 0.35M According to the question, 0.35M = 245 ⇒ M = 245/0.35 ⇒ 700 Now, Ram paid for the chair = 700 - 245 ⇒ Rs. 455 ∴ Ram paid Rs. 455 for the chair.

According to the question, (4p × 5) + (3p × 2) + (5p × 1) = 310 ⇒ 20p + 6p + 5p = 310 ⇒ 31p = 310 ⇒ p = 310/31 ⇒ p = 10 Now, the number of 5 rupee coins = 4 × 10 = 40 ∴ The number of 5 rupee coins is 40. 1ba:T

q_en: The greatest number, by which when the numbers 1658 and 2038 are divided, the remainders are 7 and 6, respectively, is:
e_en: Given: First number = 1658 Second number = 2038 Calculation: First number = 1658 - 7 = 1651 Second number = 2038 - 6 = 2032 Prime factors of 1651: 1651 = 13 × 127 Prime factors of 2032: 2032 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 127 H.C.F of 1651 and 2032 = 127 ∴ The correct answer is 127.

q_en: A trader mixes 26 kg of raw salt which costs Rs. 2 per kg with 30 kg of raw salt which costs Rs. 3.60 per kg. If he sells the mixture for Rs. 3 per kg, find his gain%.
e_en: Given: The first type of quantity of salt = 26 kg Cost of the first type of salt = Rs.2/kg The second type of quantity of salt = 30 kg Cost of the first type of salt = Rs.3.60/kg Formula used: Gain% = (profit × 100)/C.P Profit = S.P - C.P Where, C.P = cost price ; S.P = selling price Calculation: C.P of mixture of two quality of salt = {(2 × 26) + (3.6 × 30)}/(26 + 30) ⇒ (52 + 108)/56 = Rs.2.85 Gain% = {(3 - 2.85) × 100}/2.85 ⇒ 15/2.85 = 5.26 ≈ 5% ∴ The correct answer is 5%.

q_en: A, B, and C can complete a work in 4 days, 8 days, and 16 days respectively. If all three work on alternate days such that A works on first day, B works on second day, C works on third day and A works on fourth day and so on, then find the number of days in which 175% of the work is done.
e_en: Given: A can complete the work = 4 days B can complete the work = 8 days C can complete the work = 16 days Formula used: Total work = efficiency × time Calculation: Efficiency Person Time Total work 4 A 4 16 2 B 8 1 C 16 According to the question: New total work = 175% × 16 = 28 ⇒ 3 days = (4 + 2 + 1) = 7 units ⇒ (3 × 4) = 12 days = (7 × 4) = 28 units Total number of days required = 12 days ∴ The correct answer is 12 days.

q_en: Two successive price increases of 5% and 5% of an article are equivalent to a single price increase of:
e_en: Given: First increment % = 5% Second increment % = 5% Formula used: Effective increment % = I + I + (I²/100) Where, I = increment Calculation: Equivalent increment % = 5 + 5 + 5²/100 ⇒ 10 + 0.25 ⇒ 10.25% ∴ The correct answer is 10.25%.

q_en: In which ratio a trader must mix two quantities of ₹18 per kg and ₹27 per kg, so that the price of the mixture becomes ₹25 per kg?
e_en: Correct answer: 2 ∶ 7.

q_en: A man purchased 25 litres of milk at the cost price of Rs. 25 per litre. Now he added 5 litres of water to it and sold the mixture at the cost price. Find the profit percentage for the man.
e_en: Given: Cost price of milk = Rs.25/litre Quantity of milk = 25 litre Formula used: Gain% = (P × 100)/C.P Profit (P) = S.P - C.P Where, C.P = cost price, S.P = selling price Calculation: Total cost price = 25 × 25 = Rs.625 Total Selling price = 30 × 25 = Rs.750 Gain% = {(750 - 625) × 100}/625 ⇒ 12500/625 = 20% ∴ The correct answer is 20%.

q_en: A discount of 20% on one article is the same as a discount of 25% on another article. The marked price of article can be?
e_en: Given: Discount on first article = 20% Discount on second article = 25% Calculation: Let M.P of the first article = M M.P of second article = N ⇒ M × 20% = N × 25% ⇒ M/N = 25/20 ⇒ M/N = (25 × 4)/(20 × 4) ⇒ M/N = 100/80 ∴ The correct option is 3.

q_en: Which number is one less than the sum of all the prime factors of 2310?
e_en: Given: Number = 2310 Calculation: 2310 = 2 × 5 × 3 × 7 × 11 Sum of prime factors = 2 + 5 + 3 + 7 + 11 = 28 Required number = 28 -1 = 27 ∴ The correct answer is 27.

q_en: In a 100-metre race, A can beat B by 20 m and B can beat C by 10 m. In the same race, A can beat C by:
e_en: Given, in a race of 100 m, A can beat B by 20 m and in a race of 100 m, B can beat C by 10 m ∴ Ratio of speeds of A : B = 100 : (100 - 20) = 100 : 80 = 10 : 8 ∴ Ratio of speeds of B : C = 100 : (100 - 10) = 100 : 90 =10 : 9 ∴ Ratio of speeds of A : B : C = 100 : 80 : 72 ∴ Ratio of speeds of A : C = 100 : 72 Thus, A covers 100m at the same time C covers 72 m. Since in a race of 100 m, A beats C by 28 m.

q_en: A batsman scores 50, 56, 42, 38 and 78 in his 5 innings. How much does he need to score in his 6th inning to get his average to 60 in 6 innings?
e_en: Given: Scores in first 5 innings = [50, 56, 42, 38, 78] Target average = 60 Concept: The average is calculated by the total sum divided by the number of elements.

q_en: Find the discount, if the marked price of book is Rs. 500 and sold it for Rs. 400.
e_en: Given: Marked price = Rs. 500 Selling price = Rs. 400 Concept: The discount is the difference between the marked price and the selling price. Calculation: ⇒ Discount = Marked price - Selling price ⇒ Discount = 500 - 400 = Rs. 100 Therefore, the discount is Rs. 100.

q_en: Potato's per-kilogram price has risen from Rs. 18 to Rs. 25. What should be the percentage reduction in potato use so that expenditure does NOT increase?
e_en: Given: Initial price = Rs. 18 Increased price = Rs. 25 Concept: The percentage reduction in the quantity needed is given by ((increased~price - initial~price)/(increased~price)) × 100%. Calculation: ⇒ Percentage reduction = ((25 - 18)/(25)) × 100% = 0.28 × 100% = 28% Therefore, the percentage reduction in potato use should be 28%.

q_en: The base diameter of a closed cylinder is 20 cm and its height is 11 cm. Find the total surface area of the cylinder. (Use π = 22/7)
e_en: Given: Diameter of the base = 20 cm Height of the cylinder = 11 cm π = 22/7 Concept: The total surface area of a closed cylinder is given by the formula 2πr(h + r), where r is the radius and h is the height of the cylinder. Calculation: ⇒ Radius of the base (r) = Diameter/2 = 20/2 = 10 cm ⇒ Total surface area = 2πr(h + r) = 2 × (22/7) × 10 × (11 + 10) = 1320 cm² Therefore, the total surface area of the cylinder is 1320 cm².

q_en: The difference between the value of a number increased by 5 percent and the value of a number decreased by 15 percent is 9. What is the original number?
e_en: Given: Percentage increase = 5% Percentage decrease = 15% Difference in values = 9 Concept: The difference in percentage values of a number can be equated to the given difference to solve for the original number. Calculation: ⇒ Original number = (Difference~in~values)/(Difference~in~percentages) ⇒ Original number = (9)/(0.20) = 45 Therefore, the original number is 45.

q_en: 3⁵ + 3⁶ + 3⁷ + 3⁸ is completely divisible by
e_en: Correct answer: 10.

q_en: A store is running a 'Buy 4 Get 1 Free' promotion scheme. What is the net discount percentage?
e_en: Given: Buy 4 get 1 free Formula: Net Discount = (Free items/Total items) × 100% Calculation: ⇒ Net Discount = (1/(4 + 1)) × 100% ⇒ Net Discount = 20% Therefore, the net discount percentage is 20%.

q_en: A train crosses another train running at the same speed in the opposite direction in 5 seconds. If the speed of the first train is doubled and the speed of the second train is halved, then the time taken by the trains to cross is ________ seconds.
e_en: Given: Time taken by the trains to cross each other when running at the same speed in the opposite direction: 5 seconds. The speed of the first train is doubled. The speed of the second train is halved. Concept: The time taken by two trains to cross each other is inversely proportional to their relative speed. Calculations: Let's the speed of the first train as 'a' and the speed of the second train as 'a' too, as they are running at the same speed.

q_en: What is the least value of x so that the 5-digit number 725x3 becomes divisible by 9?
e_en: Correct answer: 1.

q_en: The cash difference between the selling prices of an article at a profit of 5% and 10% is Rs. 5. The ratio of the two selling prices is:
e_en: Given: Profit of 5% and 10%, Difference in selling prices = Rs. 5 Concept: Selling Price = Cost Price + Profit Calculation: ⇒ Let's assume Cost Price is x ⇒ Selling Price 1 = x + 5% of x ⇒ Selling Price 2 = x + 10% of x ⇒ The difference between the two selling prices is Rs. 5 ⇒ Selling Price 2 - Selling Price 1 = 5 ⇒ Solving the above equation we get x = 500 ⇒ Therefore, the ratio of the two selling prices is 21 ∶ 22 Hence, the ratio of the two selling prices is 21 ∶ 22.

q_en: The sides of a triangle are 5 cm, 12 cm and 13 cm. The area (in cm²) of the triangle formed by joining the mid-points of the sides of the triangle is:
e_en: Given: Sides of the triangle = [5 cm, 12 cm, 13 cm] Concept: The triangle formed by joining the mid-points of a triangle is similar to the original triangle and its area is one-fourth of the original triangle.

q_en: The average marks of eight students is 7. It was found that marks of one student was taken as 10 instead of 6. Find the correct average.
e_en: Given: Incorrect average = 7, Incorrect marks = 10, Correct marks = 6, Total students = 8 Concept: Correct Average = Total Marks / Total Students Calculation: ⇒ Incorrect Total Marks = Incorrect average × Total students = 7 × 8 = 56 ⇒ Correct Total Marks = Incorrect Total Marks - Incorrect Marks + Correct Marks = 56 - 10 + 6 = 52 ⇒ Correct Average = Correct Total Marks/Total students = 52/8 = 6.5 Hence, the correct average is 6.5.

q_en: When 20% of first number is added to second number, the second number increases by 50%. What is the ratio of the first number to the second number?
e_en: Calculation: ⇒ The condition "20% of the first number is 50% of the second number" can be written as 0.2 × First number = 0.5 × Second number. ⇒ Therefore, the ratio First number ∶ Second number = 0.5 ∶ 0.2 = 5 ∶ 2. Hence, the ratio of the first number to the second number is 5 ∶ 2.

q_en: P and Q can complete a work in 8 days, Q and R in 12 days, and R and P in 15 days. How many days will R alone take to complete the work?
e_en: Given: P and Q can complete work in 8 days, Q and R can complete work in 12 days, R and P can complete work in 15 days Concept: Work = Efficiency × Time, where efficiency is the ability of a person to do the work Calculation: Total work = LCM(8, 12, 15) = 120 units &rA

q_en: Anish can do a piece of work in 88 days. Yug can do this work in 66 days. Anish started the work alone. After how many days should Yug join him, so that the work is finished in 44 days?
e_en: Given: Anish can complete work in 88 days, Yug can complete work in 66 days, Total time to complete work = 44 days Concept: Work done = Time × Rate, where rate is the ability of a person to do the work Calculation: Total work = LCM(88, 66) = 264 units Efficiency of Anish = 264/88 = 3 Efficiency of Yug = 264/66 = 4 Work completed by Anish in 44 days = 44 × 3 = 132 units Remaining work = 264 - 132 = 132 units

q_en: What will be the amount due on Rs. 25,000 in 2 years when the rate of interest in successive years is 12% and 10% per annum respectively (interest is compounding annually)?
e_en: Given: Principal = Rs. 25,000 Rate of interest for the first year = 12% Rate of interest for the second year = 10% Concept: Compound interest formula (A = P × (1 + r/n)⁽ⁿt⁾), where A is the amount, P is the principal, r is the rate of interest, n is the number of times the interest is compounded per year, and t is the time in years. Calculation: ⇒ Amount after first year = 25000 × (1 + 12/100) = Rs. 28000 ⇒ Amount after second year = 28000 × (1 + 10/100) = Rs.

q_en: If the diameter of a sphere is 14 cm, find its volume (take π = 22/7)
e_en: Given: Diameter of sphere = 14 cm Concept: Volume of a sphere = (4/3)πr³ Calculation: ⇒ Radius = Diameter/2 = 14/2 = 7 cm ⇒ Volume = (4/3) × (22/7) × (7)³ = 1437.33 cm³ Hence, the volume of the sphere is approximately 1437.33 cm³.

q_en:
A, B and C are three batsmen of a cricket team. Given is the ratio of the runs scored by them in a certain match.
A ∶ B = 6 ∶ 7 and B ∶ C = 5 ∶ 6. At the end of the match, A, B and C together scored 856 runs. The number of runs scored by B is:
e_en: Given: Total runs scored by A, B, and C = 856, A ∶ B = 6 ∶ 7, B ∶ C = 5 ∶ 6 Concept: Ratio of quantities Calculation: ⇒ The total ratio is A ∶ B ∶ C = 30 ∶ 35 ∶ 42 ⇒ Runs scored by B = (35/107) × 856 = 280 Hence, the number of runs scored by B is 280.

q_en: A dealer buys an old car listed at ₹ 85,000 and gets successive discounts of 20% and 10%. He spends ₹ 3,800 on its repairs and sells it at a profit of 20%. Find the selling price of the car.
e_en: Given: Listed price of car = ₹85,000, Discounts = 20% and 10%, Repair cost = ₹3,800, Profit = 20% Concept: Successive discount formula = a + b - ab/100, Profit = Selling price - Cost price Calculation: ⇒ Price after discount = ₹85,000 × (1 - 20/100) × (1 - 10/100) = ₹61,200 ⇒ Cost price including repair = ₹61,200 + ₹3,800 = ₹65,000 ⇒ Selling price = ₹65,000 × (1 + 20/100) = ₹78,000 Hence, the selling price of the car is ₹78,000.

q_en: Compound interest is charged on a certain sum for 2 years at 10% rate per annum, compounding annually. If the amount becomes ₹ 605, then the principal (in ₹) is:
e_en: Given: Compound interest for 2 years at 10% per annum, Total amount = ₹605 Concept: Compound Interest = Total amount - Principal Calculation: ⇒ Let's assume the Principal is P ⇒ P × (1 + 10/100)² = ₹605 ⇒ P × 11/10 × 11/10 = ₹605 ⇒ P = ₹605 × 10/11 × 10/11 ⇒ P = ₹500 Hence, the principal is ₹500.

q_en: In a city, there are 12000 voters. Out of them, 30% voted for A, 25% voted for B and 40% voted for C. Determine the number of voters that did not vote for any of these three participants.
e_en: Given: Total voters = 12000, Voters for A = 30%, Voters for B = 25%, Voters for C = 40% Concept: Number of non-voters = Total voters - (Voters for A + Voters for B + Voters for C) Calculation: ⇒ Number of non-voters = 12000 - (12000 × 30/100 + 12000 × 25/100 + 12000 × 40/100) = 12000 - (3600 + 3000 + 4800) = 600 Hence, the number of voters who did not vote for any of these three participants is 600.

q_en: After allowing a discount of 10% on its marked price, the value of a washing machine is Rs. 28,800. If no discount is allowed, then the shopkeeper gains 25%. The cost price of the washing machine is:
e_en: Given: Selling price after discount = Rs. 28,800, Discount = 10%, Gain = 25% Concept: Marked price = Selling price/(1 - Discount/100), Cost price = Selling price/(1 + Gain/100) Calculation: ⇒ Marked price = Rs. 28,800/(1 - 10/100) = Rs. 32,000 ⇒ Cost price = Rs. 32,000/(1 + 25/100) = Rs. 25,600 Hence, the cost price of the washing machine is Rs. 25,600.

q_en: Prem can do a piece of work in 112 days. Ben can do this work in 90 days. Prem started the work alone. After how many days should Ben join him, so that the total work is finished in 56 days?
e_en: Given: Prem's work time = 112 days Ben's work time = 90 days Total time to finish the work = 56 days Concept: In the scenario of combined work, (Total work) = (Work rate) × (Time), where work rate is the inverse of the time taken to finish the work alone.

q_en: What is the fourth proportional to the numbers 10, 16 and 20?
e_en: Given: Numbers = [10, 16, 20] Concept: If a ∶ b = c ∶ d, then d is the fourth proportional to a, b, c. Calculation: ⇒ 10 ∶ 16 = 20 ∶ x ⇒ x = (20 × 16)/10 = 32 Hence, the fourth proportional to the numbers 10, 16 and 20 is 32.

q_en: The difference between the selling prices of an article available in two schemes of successive discounts 25% followed by 30%, and 25% followed by 20% is Rs. 75. Find the marked price of the article (in Rs.).
e_en: Given: Discounts = [25% and 30%, 25% and 20%] Difference in selling prices = Rs. 75 Concept: Successive discounts can be calculated by taking the product of the reductions, and the difference of the selling prices can be used to calculate the original price. Calculation: ⇒ Let the marked price be x.

q_en: A watch is sold for Rs. 15,000 at a loss of 25%. What is the cost price of the watch?
e_en: Given Data: Selling price = Rs. 15,000 Loss percentage = 25% Concept: Cost price = Selling price / (1 - loss percentage / 100) Calculation: ⇒ Cost price = 15000 / (1 - 25/100) = Rs. 20,000 Therefore, the cost price of the watch is Rs. 20,000.

q_en: Ajay can do a piece of work in 20 days and Vijay can do the same work in 22 days. In how many days they will complete the work together if they work on alternate days and the work is started by Vijay?
e_en: Given Data: Ajay's work time = 20 days Vijay's work time = 22 days Concept: Use the concept of work rates and effective work rates when working on alternate days. Calculation: LCM of 20 and 22 will be 220. Ajay one day work = 220/20 = 11 Vijay one day work = 220/22 = 10 2 days work = 11 +10 = 21. 20 days work = 21 × 10 = 210. Now remaining work done by Vijay = 10/10 = 1 Total work done in 20 + 1 = 21 days.
Correct answer: 100.

q_en: A faulty machine weighs 900 g as 1000 g. A shopkeeper uses this weighing machine to sell 45 kg of rice at Rs.65 per kg which he bought at Rs. 58 per kg. His overall profit percentage is approximately equal to:
e_en: Given: Faulty machine ratio = 900 g ∶ 1000 g Quantity of rice sold = 45 kg Selling price = Rs. 65 per kg Buying price = Rs. 58 per kg Formula used: Profit% = [(Selling Price - Cost Price)/Cost Price] × 100. Calculation: ⇒ Actual weight of rice the shopkeeper sells = (900/1000) × 45 kg = 40.5 kg ⇒ Total cost price = 40.5 kg × Rs. 58 per kg = Rs. 2349 ⇒ Total selling price = 45 kg × Rs. 65 per kg = Rs.

q_en: The value of a machine in a company depreciates by 10% every year. Determine the value (in Rs.) of the machine after 2 years if the current value is Rs. 2 lakh.
e_en: Given: Initial value = Rs. 2 lakh Annual depreciation = 10% Concept: Use the formula for annual depreciation, which is Value after n years = Initial value × (1 - Depreciation rate)ⁿ. Calculation: ⇒ Value after 2 years = 2 lakh × (1 - 10/100)² = Rs. 1,62,000 lakh Hence, the value of the machine after 2 years is Rs. 1,62,000 lakh.

q_en: There are four sections: A, B, C, and D of class X in a school. In every section, there are 30 students. The average score in maths of the four sections is 89.8, 92.6, 99.1, and 94.5, respectively. What is the average score in maths of the whole class X in that school?
e_en: Given: Number of sections = 4 Students per section = 30 Average scores per section = [89.8, 92.6, 99.1, 94.5] Concept: The overall average score can be calculated by summing the products of the number of students and the average score in each section and dividing by the total number of students.

q_en: R runs for 10 hours at speeds of 10 km/h, 9 km/h,....,1 km/h, respectively, in the first hour, second hour, and so on. His average speed is _______ km/h.
e_en: Correct answer: 5.5.

q_en: A shopkeeper allows a discount of 40% on his articles and still makes a profit of 20%. How much cost price does a shopkeeper pay for an article whose marked price is ₹2,400?
e_en: Given: The marked price of the article = ₹2,400 Discount allowed = 40% Profit made = 20% Formula used: Selling price = Marked price(MP) - Discount allowed Profit = Selling price(SP) - Cost price(CP) Calculation: According to question Let MP be 100x Discount= 40% Selling Price = 100x - 40x = 60x From this SP = 60x, Still makes profit = 20% So, CP = 60x ÷ 120 × 100 = 50x CP MP SP 50x 100x 60x 2400(given) CP = 2400 ÷ 100 × 50 = 1200 ∴ Cost price is 1200.

q_en: A man covers a certain distance by scooter at 64 km/h and he returns to the starting place riding a bicycle at 16 km/h. Find the average speed for the whole journey.
e_en: Given: A man covers a certain distance on a scooter driving at 64 km/h. He returns to the starting point riding on a bicycle at 16 km/h. Formula used: Formula: Average speed = 2s1s2/(s1+s2) Solution: Average speed = 2s1s2/(s1+s2) (2 × 64 × 16)/(64 + 16) 25.6 km/h ∴ The answer is 25.6 km/h.

q_en: 5 women can complete a work in 8 days, while 8 children take 10 days to complete the same work. How many days will 2 women and 4 children take to complete the work?
e_en: Correct answer: 10.

e_en: Given: Diameter of the cylinder = 14 cm Height of the cylinder = 2 cm π = 22/7 Formula used: The curved surface area of a cylinder = 2πrh Total surface area of a cylinder = 2πr(r + h) Solution: Curved surface area = 2πrh = 2 &am

q_en: A can paint a painting in 12 days. B can paint the same in 8 days. C can paint the same in 10 days. Find the (approximate) number of days in which the painting can be painted by A if he is accompanied by both B and C together on alternate days and A starts painting on the first day alone.
e_en: Given: A can paint a painting in 12 days. B can paint the same in 8 days. C can paint the same in 10 days. Concept Used: Work = Time × Efficiency Calculation: Total work = LCM(12, 8, 10) = 120 Efficiency of A = 120/12 = 10 Efficiency of B = 120/8 = 15 Efficiency of C = 120/10 = 12 According to question, A if he is accompanied by both B and C together on alternate days. A start alone on first day.

q_en: The population of bears in a city has been growing at 3% every year. If the present population of bears in the city is 21,218, what was the population of bears two years ago?
e_en: Given: The current population of bears = 21,218 Growth rate per year = 3% Formula: Population after 'n' years = Initial population * (1 + growth rate)^n Calculation: Population after two years = Current population × (1 + growth rate)² Let the Population 2 year before = x x × (1 + 0.03)² = 21,218 x × (1.03)2 = 21,218 x = 21218/1.0609 x = 20000 Hence, the population of bears two years ago was approximately 20,000.

q_en: The income of a person is ₹95,000 and his expenditure is ₹75,000. If his income is increased by 18% and the expenditure by 12%, then what will be the percentage increase in his saving?
e_en: Given: Income = ₹95,000 Expenditure = ₹75,000 Formula used: Percentage increase in saving = (Increase in saving / Original saving) × 100 Solution: Saving = 95000 - 75000 = 20000 Increase in income = 18% of ₹95,000 = 18/100 × 95,000 = ₹17,100 Increased Income = 112100 Increase in expenditure = 12% of ₹75,000 = 12/100 × 75,000 = ₹9,000 Increased in expenditure = 84000 New saving = ₹112100 - ₹84000 = ₹ 28100 Percentage increase in saving = (28,100 - 20,000)/20,000 × 100 = 40.5%…

q_en: Mohan is selling a table at Rs. 2,832. If his profit is 18%, then what is the cost price of the table?
e_en: Given: The selling price of the table = Rs. 2,832 Profit = 18% Formula: Selling price = Cost price × (100 + profit%) Solution: 2,832 = Cost price × (100 +18%) CP = (2832 × 100)/118 CP = 2400 ∴ Option D is the correct answer.

q_en: 5 bells start commencing together at 9 AM. They ring at intervals of 12 seconds, 18 seconds, 24 seconds, 36 seconds, and 45 seconds. At what time do the bells ring together again?
e_en: Given: The bells start commencing together at 9 AM. The bells ring at intervals of 12 seconds, 18 seconds, 24 seconds, 36 seconds, and 45 seconds. Formula used: The least common multiple of two or more integers is the smallest number that is a multiple of all of the integers. Solution: The least common multiple of 12, 18, 24, 36, and 45 is 360. This means that the bells will ring together again after 360 seconds. In 6 min has 360 sec, then The bell ring together in 9:06 AM.

q_en: A spends 45% of his salary on food and donates 5 % of his salary on old age homes. If he spends Rs. 28,500 on food and old age homes, then what will be the salary of A?

Therefore, we can say that: 50% of S = Rs. 28,500 To find S (the salary of A), we can rewrite this equation as: S = Rs.

e_en: Correct answer: 5 h.

q_en: X bought 40 pencils for a total of Rs. 180 and bought 2 dozens of pens for Rs. 180. Find the difference between the price of one pen and one pencil.
e_en: Given: X bought 40 pencils for a total of Rs. 180. X bought 2 dozen (24 units) pens for Rs. 180. Calculation: Let's denote the price of one pencil as 'P' and the price of one pen as 'Q'. q_en: How many prime numbers are there between 40 and 50?
e_en: Concept Used: A prime number is a natural number greater than 1 that has no positive divisors other than 1 and itself. Calculation: The prime numbers between 40 and 50 are 41, 43, and 47. So, there are 3 prime numbers between 40 and 50. ∴ Option C is the correct answer.

q_en: A dealer allowed a discount of 20 percent on marked price of Rs. 72000 on an article and incurred a loss of 10 percent. What discount should he allow on the marked price, so that he gains Rs. 440 on the article?
e_en: Correct answer: 10.5 percent.

q_en: The LCM of 192 and 480 is 60 more than the 100 times of X. What is the value of X?
e_en: Given: LCM(192, 480) = 60 + 100 × X Concept: Lowest Common Multiple (LCM) calculation: Solution: ⇒ LCM(192, 480) = 960 ⇒ 960 = 60 + 100 × X ⇒ X = (960 - 60)/100 ⇒ X = 9 Therefore, the value of X is 9.

q_en: Divide Rs. 500 among A, B, C and D so that A and B together get thrice as much as C and D together, B gets 4 times what C gets and C gets 1.5 times as much as D. The value of B’s share is:
e_en: Distribution of Rs. 500 among A, B, C, D Given: A + B = 3 * (C + D) B = 4 * C C = 1.5 * D Concept: Linear equations Solution: ⇒ A + B + C + D = 500 ⇒ Substitute B and C into A + B = 3 * (C + D) to find the values of A, B, C, and D ⇒ B = Rs. 300 Therefore, the value of B's share is Rs. 300.

q_en: A single discount equivalent to two successive discounts 15% and 25% is:
e_en: Given: Successive discounts of 15% and 25% Concept: Successive percentage change formula Solution: ⇒ Equivalent discount = 1 - (1 - 0.15) × (1 - 0.25) ⇒ Equivalent discount = 36.25% Therefore, the equivalent single discount is 36.25%, closest to option D.

q_en: A certain sum of money fetches simple interest of Rs. 4,016.25 at the rate of 7% per annum in 5 years. What is the sum?
e_en: Simple interest problem Given: Simple interest = Rs. 4016.25 Rate = 7% Time = 5 years Concept: Simple interest formula (SI = PRT/100) Solution: ⇒ Principle = (SI * 100) / (R * T) ⇒ Principle = Rs. 11475 Therefore, the sum is Rs. 11475.

q_en: A person drives for 320 kms in 8 hours, cycles for 40 kms in 5 hours and then walks for 40 kms in 7 hours. Find the average speed of the driver.
e_en: Average speed calculation: Given: Distance travelled by car = 320 km Time taken = 8 hours Distance travelled by cycle = 40 km Time taken = 5 hours Distance travelled by walking = 40 km Time taken = 7 hours Concept: Average speed = Total Distance / Total Time Solution: ⇒ Average speed = (320 + 40 + 40) / (8 + 5 + 7) ⇒ Average speed = 20 kmph Therefore, the average speed of the driver is 20 kmph.

q_en: Two trains start at the same time from two stations and proceed toward each other at the speed of 40 km/h and 45 km/h, respectively. When they meet, it is found that one train has travelled 20 km more than the other. Find the distance between the two stations.
e_en: Given: Speed of train 1 = 40 km/h, Speed of train 2 = 45 km/h, Difference in distance = 20 km Concept: Relative speed when moving towards each other = Speed1 + Speed2, Time = Distance/Speed Calculation: ⇒ Time taken to meet = Difference in distance/Difference in speeds = 20 km/5 km/h = 4 hours ⇒ Distance between the stations = (Speed of train 1 + Speed of train 2) × Time = (40 + 45) km/h × 4 hours = 340 km Hence, the distance between the two stations is 340 km.

q_en: A train starts from station P, runs through stations Q, R, S, T and reaches station U. It stops at stations Q, R, S and T for 2 minutes, 4 minutes, 6 minutes, and 8 minutes, respectively. The distance between P and U is 50 km. What is the average speed of the train between stations P and U (in km/h), if it runs for 70 minutes between the stations, with uniform speed?
e_en: Given: Distance = 50 km, Total run time = 70 minutes, Stoppage time at stations = 2 + 4 + 6 + 8 = 20 minutes Concept: Average speed = Total distance/Total time Calculation: ⇒ Total time including stoppages = 70 + 20 = 90 minutes = 90/60 = 1.5 hours ⇒ Average speed = 50 km/1.5 hours = 100/3 km/h Hence, the average speed of the train between stations P and U is 100/3 km/h.

q_en: The compound interest on ₹10,00,000 at 3% per annum, compounding annually is ₹92,727. The number of years required for this is:
e_en: Given: Compound interest = ₹92,727, Principal = ₹10,00,000, Rate = 3% Concept: Compound Interest = Principal × (1 + Rate/100)ⁿ - Principal, where n is the number of periods Calculation: ⇒ 92,727 = 10,00,000 × [(1 + 3/100)ⁿ - 1] ⇒ 92,727/10,00,000 = [(1 + 3/100)ⁿ - 1] ⇒ 92,727/10,00,000 + 1 = (1 + 3/100)ⁿ ⇒ 1092,727/10,00,000 = (1 + 3/100)ⁿ ⇒ (103/100)³ = (1 + 3/100)ⁿ ⇒ (1 + 3/100)3 = (1 + 3/100)ⁿ ⇒ n = 3 years Hence, the number of years required for the compound interest to a…

q_en: Two years ago, the population of a town was 66000. The population increased by 5% in the first year and decreased by 5% in the second year. Find the present population of the town.
e_en: Population growth calculation: Given: Initial population = 66000 Increase by 5% in the first year Decrease by 5% in the second year Concept: Percentage change in population Solution: ⇒ Population after first year = 66000 * 1.05 ⇒ Population after second year = 66000 * 1.05 * 0.95 ⇒ Final population = 65835 Therefore, Final population of the town is 65835.

q_en: The radius of the base of a conical vessel is 5 cm and its height is 24 cm. The vessel is full of water. This water is poured into a cylindrical vessel having the base radius 10 cm. The depth of the water in the cylindrical vessel is:
e_en: Volume transfer from a cone to a cylinder Given: Cone radius = 5 cm, height = 24 cm Cylinder radius = 10 cm Concept: Volume of a cone and cylinder Solution: ⇒ Volume of cone = 1/3πr²h = 1/3π5²24 ⇒ Volume of water in the cylinder = cone volume ⇒ Depth of water = Volume / (πr²) = 1/3 {(π × 5² × 24) / (π × 10²) ⇒ Depth of water = 2 cm Therefore, the depth of the water in the cylindrical vessel is 2 cm.

q_en: Three partners A, B and C started a business and decided to share the profit in the ratio 2 ∶ 3 ∶ 5, respectively. If the share of B is Rs. 7,50,000, then calculate the total profit.
e_en: Correct answer: Rs. 25,00,000.

q_en: P can do as much work as Q and R together can do. P and Q can together do a piece of work in 8 hours and 24 minutes and R can do it in 42 hours. Find the time (in hours) that Q needs to do the work alone.
e_en: Time to complete a work Given: P and Q can do the work in 8 hours 24 minutes. R can do it in 42 hours. P = Q + R Concept: Work and Time Solution: According to the question, P can do as much work as Q and R&nb

q_en: Salary of a person is first decreased by 40 percent and then increased by 40 percent. What will be the percentage decrease in the salary?
e_en: Salary decrease percentage Given: Salary decreased by 40% then increased by 40% Concept: Successive percentage change formula Solution: ⇒ Final decrease = (1 - 0.6) * (1 + 0.4) - 1 ⇒ Final decrease = -16% Therefore, the percentage decrease in the salary is 16%.

q_en: Find the total surface area of a cylinder whose height is 8.5 mm and the base diameter is 10 mm.
e_en: Total surface area of a cylinder Given: Height of cylinder = 8.5 mm Diameter of base = 10 mm Concept: Total surface area of a cylinder Solution: ⇒ Radius = Diameter/2 = 5 mm ⇒ Total surface area = 2πr(h + r) ⇒ Total surface area = 2π5(8.5 + 5) ⇒ Total surface area = 135π mm² Therefore, the total surface area of the cylinder is 135π mm².

q_en: Excluding the stoppages, the speed of a truck is 90 km/h and including the stoppages, the speed of the truck is 36 km/h in a journey. For how many minutes does the truck stop per hour?
e_en: Correct answer: 36 minutes.

q_en: A dealer offers 20% discount on all dolls. He offers a further discount of 5% on the reduced price to those customers who pay in cash. How much will a customer pay in cash for a doll worth Rs. 1,800?
e_en: Discount calculation: Given: Original price of doll = Rs. 1,800 First discount = 20% Second discount = 5% Concept: Successive discount calculation: Solution: ⇒ Price after first discount = 1800 - 20% of 1800 = 1440 ⇒ Price after second discount = 1440 - 5% of 1440 = 1368 Therefore, a customer will pay Rs. 1368 in cash for a doll.

q_en: In a storm 243 trees were left standing out of 300 trees in a garden. What is the percentage decrease in number of trees?
e_en: Percentage decrease in number of trees Given: Initial number of trees = 300 Final number of trees = 243 Concept: Percentage decrease Solution: ⇒ Percentage decrease = ((300 - 243) / 300) * 100 ⇒ Percentage decrease = 19% Therefore, the percentage decrease in number of trees is 19 percent.

q_en: A shopkeeper sells his goods at 10 percent loss on cost price but uses 30 percent less weight. What is his profit?
e_en: Given: Loss = 10% Less weight used = 30% Concept used: Profit = SP - CP Profit percentage = (Profit / Cost price) × 100 Calcultion: Let, CP = 100 units SP = 100 × (100-10)/100 = 90 units Effective CP = 100 × (100 - 30)/100 = 70 units Profit = 90 - 70 = 20 units Profit percentage = 20 / 70 × 100 = 2/7 = 28{4 over7} ∴ His profit is 28{4 over7} percent.

q_en: If 6 men or 8 women can reap a field in 21.5 days. How long will 14 men and 10 women take to reap it?
e_en: Time to reap a field Given: 6 men can reap a field in 21.5 days 8 women can reap the field in 21.5 days Concept: Work and Time Solution: ⇒ 1 man's 1 day's work = 1/6/21.5 = 1/129 ⇒ 1 woman's 1 day's work = 1/8/21.5 = 1/172 ⇒ 14 men and 10 women's 1 day's work = 14/129 + 10/172 = 1/6 ⇒ Time taken to reap the field = 1 / (1/6) = 6 days Therefore, 14 men and 10 women will take 6 days to reap the field.

q_en: Rita buys a toy car for Rs. 12,000 and sells it for Rs. 14,500. What is her gain percent? (rounded off to two digits after decimal)
e_en: Gain percentage calculation: Given: Cost price = Rs. 12,000 Selling price = Rs. 14,500 Concept: Gain percentage Solution: ⇒ Gain = Selling price - Cost price ⇒ Gain = Rs. 14,500 - Rs. 12,000 = Rs. 2,500 ⇒ Gain percentage = (Gain / Cost price) * 100 ⇒ Gain percentage = (2,500 / 12,000) * 100 = 20.83% Therefore, her gain percent is 20.83% (none of the provided options match).

q_en: Three milk bottles of 1 litre, 750 millilitres and 650 millilitres with milk percentage respectively 45%, 50% and 60% are emptied in a same container simultaneously. What is the percentage of milk in the mixture?
e_en: Given values: Volume of first milk bottle: 1L with 45% milk. Volume of second milk bottle: 750ml with 50% milk. Volume of third milk bottle: 650ml with 60% milk. The concept used: The percentage of milk in the mixture is the total amount of milk divided by the total volume. Solution: Calculate the total amount of milk: (1 × 0.45) + (0.75 × 0.50) + (0.65 × 0.60). Calculate the total volume: 1 + 0.75 + 0.65. Calculate the percentage: (Total milk/Total volume) × 100.

q_en: The area of a triangle whose base and corresponding height are, respectively, 3.2 m and 75 cm, is:
e_en: Given: Base of the triangle: 3.2 m Height of the triangle: 75 cm = 0.75 m Concept used: The area of a triangle is given by 0.5 × base × height. Solution: Calculate the area: 0.5 × 3.2 × 0.75. ⇒ Area = 0.5 × 3.2 × 0.75 = 1.2 m² Therefore, the area of the triangle is 1.2 m².

q_en: A dealer marks his goods 30% higher than their cost price. In order to sell his goods at a no profit no loss basis, what discount percentage should he allow (correct up to 2 decimal places)?
e_en: Given: Percentage increase in price: 30% Concept used: The discount needed for no profit no loss is equal to the percentage increase. Solution: Calculate the discount: 30/(1+30/100) × 100. ⇒ Discount = 30/(1+30/100) × 100 = 23.08% Therefore, the dealer should allow a discount of 23.08%.

q_en: 25 doctors can diagnose 75 patients in 5 hours. If five doctors leave the job, then how many patients can be diagnosed in 6 hours?
e_en: Given: Number of doctors: 25 Number of patients: 75 Time: 5 hours Doctors leaving: 5 New time: 6 hours Concept used: The number of patients diagnosed is directly proportional to the number of doctors and time. Solution: Find the rate of work: 75/(25 × 5). Find the number of patients diagnosed: (20 × 6) × rate of work. ⇒ Rate of work = 75/(25 × 5) = 0.6 patients/doctor/hour ⇒ Number of patients = (20 × 6) × 0.6 = 72 patients Therefore, 72 patients can be diagnosed in 6 hours.

q_en: How many digits will be there after the decimal point in the product of 0.124 and 1.0204?
e_en: Given: First number: 0.124 (3 digits after decimal) Second number: 1.0204 (4 digits after decimal) Concept used: When multiplying decimal numbers, the number of digits after the decimal in the result is the sum of the digits after the decimal in the multiplicands. Solution: Add the number of decimal places: 3 + 4. ⇒ Number of decimal places = 3 + 4 = 7 Therefore, there will be 7 digits after the decimal point in the product.

q_en: A merchant offers 20% discount on the marked price. He offers a further discount of 10% on the reduced price on cash payments. What does a customer have to pay in cash for an item whose marked price is ₹5000 ?
e_en: Given: Marked price: ₹5000 First discount: 20% Second discount: 10% Concept used: Successive discounts are calculated individually on the reduced price. Solution: Calculate the price after the first discount: 5000 × (1 - 20/100). Calculate the price after the second discount: price after first discount × (1 - 10/100).

q_en: P can do a piece of work in 15 days, while Q can do it in 10 days. If they work on alternate days beginning with P, in how many days will the work be finished?
e_en: Given: Time taken by P to complete the work alone: 15 days Time taken by Q to complete the work alone: 10 days Concept used: Total work done is the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of individual work days, and the work done by P and Q alternately can be calculated from the total work done. Solution: LCM of 15

q_en: A cop sees a thief at a distance of 120 m. He starts chasing the thief who is running at a speed of 6 m/sec. The cop is chasing him with a speed of 8 m/sec. Find the distance covered by the thief before the cop catches him.
e_en: Given: Initial distance between cop and thief: 120 m Speed of thief: 6 m/sec Speed of cop: 8 m/sec Concept used: Relative speed is the difference of individual speeds, and the distance covered by the thief before the cop catches him is the product of the thief's speed and the time it takes for the cop to catch him. Solution: Calculate the relative speed: 8 m/sec - 6 m/sec. Calculate the time for the cop to catch the thief: 120 m / relative speed.

q_en: A police officer follows a thief who is at a distance of 800 m from him. If they run at the speeds of 8 km/h and 7 km/h, respectively, what distance (in metre) does the police officer run to catch the thief?
e_en: Correct answer: 6400.

q_en: If the slant height and radius of a cone are 12 cm and 7 cm, respectively, then find the total surface area.
e_en: Given: The slant height of the cone = 12 cm Radius of cone = 7 cm Concept: The total surface area of a cone = π × r × (r + l), where r is the radius and l is the slant height. Solution: ⇒ Total surface area = π × r × (r + l) ⇒ Total surface area = 22/7 × 7 cm × (7 cm + 12 cm) ⇒ Total surface area = 418 cm² Hence, the total surface area of the cone is 418 cm².

q_en: A shopkeeper announces a discount of 18% on every item in his store. What price should a customer pay for an item of Rs. 5,583? (in Rs., rounded off to the nearest integer)
e_en: Given: Initial price of item = Rs. 5583 Discount = 18% Concept: Price after discount = Initial price - (Initial price × Discount/100) Solution: ⇒ Price after discount = Rs. 5583 - (Rs. 5583 × 18/100) ⇒ Price after discount = Rs. 4578 Therefore, the customer should pay Rs. 4578 for the item.

q_en: The population of a town is 64,000 which grows by 1/8th of its current population every year. What will be the population after two years?
e_en: Given: Initial population = 64,000 Annual growth = 1/8 Concept: The population after n years, growing annually at a rate of r, can be calculated as population × (1 + r)ⁿ. Solution: ⇒ Population after 2 years = 64,000 × (1 + 1/8)² ⇒ Population after 2 years = 81000 Therefore, the population after two years will be 81,000.

q_en: Find the principal if the interest compounded at the rate of 12% per annum, compounding annually for 2 years is Rs. 1,908.
e_en: Given: Compound interest after 2 years = Rs. 1,908 Rate of interest = 12% per annum Concept: CI = P [(1 + r/100)t - 1] Solution: CI = P [(1 + r/100)t - 1] ⇒ 1908 = P [(1 + 12/100)² - 1] ⇒ 1908 = P [(1 + 3/25)² - 1] ⇒ 1908 = P [(28/25)² - 1] ⇒ 1908 = P [784/625 - 1] ⇒ 1908 = P × 159 / 625 ⇒ P = 1908 × 625 / 159 ⇒ P = 12 × 625 = Rs. 7500 Hence, the principal is Rs. 7,500.

q_en: Akshit is selling a suitcase marked at Rs. 5,000 by offering a 10% discount, and further offers a 10% discount if the payment is made in cash. A customer bought the suitcase from Akshit and paid him in cash. How much amount (in Rs.) did he pay to Akshit?
e_en: Given: Marked price = Rs. 5,000 Initial discount = 10% Cash payment discount = 10% Concept: The final price after two discounts is Marked Price × (1 - initial discount) × (1 - cash discount). Solution: ⇒ Final price = Rs. 5,000 × (1 - 10/100) × (1 - 10/100) ⇒ Final price = Rs. 4,050 Hence, the customer paid Rs. 4,050 to Akshit.

q_en: A milkman bought 90 litres of milk for Rs. 1,630 and added 15 litres of water. If he sells it at Rs. 19.00 per litre, his profit percentage will be:
e_en: Given: Cost of milk = Rs. 1630 for 90 litres Added water = 15 litres Selling price = Rs. 19.00 per litre Concept: Profit percentage = (Selling Price - Cost Price)/Cost Price × 100% Solution: ⇒ Total volume = 90 litres + 15 litres = 105 litres ⇒ Total selling price = 105 litres × Rs. 19.00 per litre = Rs. 1995 ⇒ Profit percentage = (Rs. 1995 - Rs. 1630)/Rs. 1630 × 100% ⇒ Profit percentage = 22 64/163 % Hence, the profit percentage is 22 64/163 %.

q_en: What is the percentage loss when the cost price and selling price of an article are in the ratio of 5 ∶ 3?
e_en: Given Data: Cost price to selling price ratio = 5 ∶ 3 Concept: Loss percentage = (Cost Price - Selling Price) / Cost Price × 100% Solution: ⇒ Loss percentage = (5 - 3) / 5 × 100% ⇒ Loss percentage = 40% Hence, the loss percentage is 40%.

q_en: Ranu can finish a piece of work in 10 days while Ruby can finish the same work in 15 days. In how many days the whole work will be finished. If they work on alternate days, starting with Ranu?
e_en: Given Data: Ranu's work completion time = 10 days Ruby's work completion time = 15 days Concept: When two people work on alternate days, the total time taken is 2 × (LCM of individual times / sum of individual rates of work) Solution: ⇒ Ranu's rate of work = 1/10 per day ⇒ Ruby's rate of work = 1/15 per day ⇒ LCM of 10 and 15 = 30 ⇒ Total time taken = 2 × (30 / (1/10 + 1/15)) = 12 days Hence, the work will be finished in 12 days when Ranu and Ruby work on alternate days.

q_en: If x% of y is equal to 2/3 of 90, then the value of xy is _______.
e_en: Given: x% of y = 90 Concept: If x% of y is z, then y = 100 × z/x. Solution: ⇒ xy = 100 × (90) × 2/3 ⇒ Therefore xy = 9000 × 2/3 = 6000 Hence, the value of xy is 6000.

q_en: P takes 12 minutes to complete one round of a circular track and R takes 18 minutes to complete the same round. If they start at the same time from the same point in the same direction at 12:30 p.m., then at which of the following times will they meet at the starting point on the same day?
e_en: Given: P's time to complete one round = 12 minutes R's time to complete one round = 18 minutes Concept: If two people start from the same point at the same time, they meet at the starting point again after the LCM of their individual times. Solution: ⇒ LCM of 12 and 18 = 36 minutes ⇒ They started at 12:30 p.m., so they will meet again at 12:30 p.m. + 36 minutes = 1:06 p.m.

q_en: A car takes 5 hours to cover a distance, if its speed is 30 km/h. What should be its speed to cover the same distance in 2.5 hours?
e_en: Given: Distance covered by car = D (unknown) Time taken with speed 30 km/h = 5 hours Desired time to cover the same distance = 2.5 hours Concept: If the distance remains the same, then the speed is inversely proportional to the time taken to cover that distance.

q_en: If 'a' and 'b' are prime numbers, which of the following CANNOT be the sum of 'a' and 'b' ? (Where a and b are distinct prime numbers)
e_en: Given: a and b are distinct prime numbers Concept: The sum of two prime numbers is always even, except for the case 2 + odd prime. Solution: We know that 2 is the only even prime number. All other prime numbers are odd. For the sum to be even, both numbers must be even, or both must be odd. Now, using the above statements: '6' is an even number.

q_en: The average age of husband and wife is 24 years. The age of their son is 1/9th of the age of the husband. The wife is 6 years younger to the husband. Find the average age of all three members of family.
e_en: Given: Average age of husband and wife = 24 years Age of their son is 1/9th of the age of the husband Wife is 6 years younger than the husband Concept: Average age = Total age/Number of individuals Solution: ⇒ Total age of husband and wife = 24 years × 2 = 48 years ⇒ Age of husband = (48 years + 6 years)/2 = 27 years ⇒ Age of son = 27 years/9 = 3 years ⇒ Total age of all three = 48 years + 3 years = 51 years ⇒ Average age of all three = 51 years/3 = 17 years Hence, the averag…

q_en: Due to leakage in a tank, there are 220 liters of water left in the tank which originally held 240 liters. What is percent loss of water?
e_en: Given: Original amount of water = 240 liters Amount of water left due to leakage = 220 liters Concept: Percentage loss = (Initial Quantity - Final Quantity)/initial Quantity × 100% Solution: ⇒ Percentage loss = (240 liters - 220 liters)/240 liters × 100% = 20/240 × 100% = 8.33% Hence, the percent loss of water is 8.33%.

q_en: A and B can complete a work separately in 10 days and 15 days, respectively. B alone work for 3 days and then he left the work. In how many days will A finish the remaining work?
e_en: Given: A and B can complete a work separately in 10 days and 15 days Calculation: B's 1 day work = 1/15 B's 3 day work = 1/15 × 3 = 1/5 Remaining work = 1 - 1/5 = 4/5 A's 1 day work = 1/10 A can finish the remaining work in 4/5 × 10 = 8 days. Therefore, A can finish the remaining work in 8 days.

q_en: Find the product of the numbers whose HCF and LCM are 8 and 40 respectively.
e_en: Given: HCF = 8 LCM = 40 Formula: The product of the HCF and LCM of two numbers is equal to the product of the two numbers. Solution: Product of the two numbers = HCF × LCM = 8 × 40 = 320 Therefore, the product of the numbers whose HCF and LCM are 8 and 40 respectively is 320.

e_en: Given: Let the principal be Rs 'P' Time = 1 1/2 year = 3/2 years Rate of interest = 8 % Concept Used: Simple interest = (P x T x R)/100 Amount at the rate of compound interest = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ Compound Interest = Amount - Principal (i) Simple interest = (P x T x R)/100 = (P x 3 x 8)/(2 x 100) = 3P/25 (ii) Amount at the rate of compound interest = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ = P(1 + 4/100)³ = P(26/25)³ = 17576P/15625 Compound Interest = (17576P/15625) - P = 1951P/15625 Difference between the…

q_en: A, B and C run at speeds 5 m/s, 3 m/s and 8 m/s respectively. They start the race at the same time from the same point. After some time, it was found that the distance between A and C is 6 m. Determine the distance between A and B.
e_en: Given: Speed of A = 5 m/s Speed of B = 3 m/s Speed of C = 8 m/s Distance between A and C = 6 m Concept: Distance = Speed × Time Solution: The relative speed of A and C is 8 - 5 = 3 m/s. Given the distance of 6 m between A and C, they've been running for 6/3 = 2 seconds. In 2 seconds, B runs 3 m/s × 2 s = 6 m, and A runs 5 m/s × 2 s = 10 m. The distance between A and B is 10 m - 6 m = 4 m. Hence, the distance between A and B is 4 m.

q_en: John borrowed some amount of money from a bank at the rate of 10% per annum on compound interest for which interest is compounded annually. If he repaid his loan by paying ₹21,961.50 at the end of 4 years, what is the amount he borrowed?
e_en: Given: Rate of interest = 10% At the end of four years amount paid by him = ₹21,961.50 Concept used: A = P × (1 + R/100)T Where, A → Amount P → Principal R → Rate of interest T → Time Calculation: Rate = 10% = 1/10 Interest being compounded annually after four year 10⁴ : 11⁴ 10000 : 14641 14641 unit = 21,961.50 1 = 1.5 10000 = 15000 ∴ Option B is the correct answer.

q_en: A bus travels from station P to station Q at a speed of 70 km/h, and from station Q to station P at a speed of 90 km/h. What is the average speed of the bus during the entire journey?
e_en: Given: Speed from station P to station Q: 70 km/h Speed from station Q to station P: 90 km/h Formula: Average speed = 2xy/x + y Solution: Average speed = (2 × 70 × 90)/70 + 90 = 78.75 km/h Therefore, the average speed of the bus during the entire journey is 78.75 km/h

q_en: A dishonest shopkeeper sells rice at the cost price but he uses a faulty weight of 925g for 1000g. Find his gain percentage.
e_en: Given: Actual weight = 1000g Weight used by shopkeeper = 925g Concept: Gain% = [(SP - CP)/CP] × 100% Solution: ⇒ Gain = 1000g - 925g = 75g ⇒ Gain% = (75g / 925g) × 100% = 8.11% Hence, his gain percentage is 8.11%. Note: In this case, the selling price (SP) is considered as the actual weight and the cost price (CP) is the weight the shopkeeper uses.

q_en: Sonal and Arjun together can finish a piece of work in 57 days, Arjun and Rohan in 38 days, and Rohan and Sonal in 38 days, then Sonal, Arjun, and Rohan together can finish the same work in how many days?
e_en: Given: Sonal and Arjun can finish a piece of work in 57 days. Arjun and Rohan can finish the same piece of work in 38 days. Rohan and Sonal can finish the same piece of work in 38 days. Concept Used: The work rate of people working together is the sum of their individual work rates. In this case, the work rate is the reciprocal of the time taken to complete the work. q_en: On selling a table fan at Rs. 2,827.06, the value of gain is 14% more than the value of loss incurred on selling it at Rs. 2,230. In order to gain 14%, the selling price will be:
e_en: Given: When article sold at Rs. 2,827.06 it gains 14% more than value when article sold at Rs. 2230 it losses Formula used: Loss = cost price - selling price Gain = selling price - cost price Gain% = (Gain/cost price) × 100 Solution : Let the cost price be x It losses when selling price = Rs. 2230 ⇒ Loss = (x - 2230) ----(1) It gains when selling price = Rs.

q_en: A single discount equivalent to three successive discounts of 10%, 5% and 3 1/2% will be ______.
e_en: Given: Successive discounts = 10%, 5%, 3.5% Concept: Successive discounts can be computed using the formula: net discount = 1 - (1 - d1) × (1 - d2) × ... Solution: ⇒ Net discount = 1 - (1 - 0.1) × (1 - 0.05) × (1 - 0.035) ⇒ Net discount = 1 - 0.9 × 0.95 × 0.965 = 0.174925 Hence, a single discount equivalent to the three successive discounts is 0.174925 or 17.4925%

q_en: The ratio between the fourth proportional of 7, 5 and 3 to the third proportional of 7 and 13 is:
e_en: Correct answer: 15 ∶ 169.

q_en: What is the smallest positive number that should be subtracted from each of 12 and 21 so that 36 is the third proportion to them?
e_en: Given: Numbers: 12 and 21 Concept: If a ∶ b ∶∶ b ∶ c, then b² = ac Solution: ⇒ Let x be the number to subtract, then (21 - x) × (21 - x) = (12 - x) × 36 ⇒ 441 + x² - 42x = 432 - 36x ⇒ x² - 6x + 9 = 0 ⇒ Solving the quadratic equation gives x = 3 Hence, the smallest positive number to subtract is 3.
